# PART 7A — RECOVERY SUPPORT, NOTICES AND ADR ACCESS (LSP SCOPE; ATTACHABLE)

This Part specifies the **LSP-scope subset** of the Infrabyx Recovery, Litigation and ADR Suite. The full lender-side suite is Finbyx Part 7A (R1–R16), which runs in the RE's system of record. Udofin builds six modules (UR1–UR6) as one attachable module pack, `modules/ur-recovery-support/`, that an RE switches on per product and per capability. Where Part 7A differs from U13 or U15, **Part 7A prevails**. Events, APIs and connector rules follow the Infrabyx Ecosystem Integration Specification (`docs/ecosystem/infrabyx-integration-spec.md`); event names below are the canonical names and must not be renamed.

Labels: **[LAW]** statute, regulation or Direction text; **[JUD]** judicial interpretation; **[INTERP]** our reading; **[REC]** recommendation. Anything unconfirmed carries `[VERIFY: …]`.

## 7A.0 Scope, attach and detach, and LSP limits

### 7A.0.1 What binds Udofin in recovery

| Rule | Source | Effect on Udofin |
|---|---|---|
| The RE guides an LSP acting as recovery agent to comply with RBC and stays fully liable; the RE answers for its recovery agents | [LAW] CF paras 6(5), 6(7); OUT para 17 | UR4 only under an explicit recovery-agent contract (U1); RE suspension switch |
| Agent particulars to the borrower by email or SMS before the agent's first contact, on every assignment or change | [LAW] CF para 9(6) | UR4 hard gate |
| Repayment directly to the RE; no pool or pass-through account; no third-party control; cash recovery reflected the same day, no LSP fee from proceeds | [LAW] CF para 10(2)–(5) | Payment instructions only on RE accounts; cash ledger (UR4) |
| LSP nodal grievance officer; redressal stays with the RE; CMS route after 30 days or rejection | [LAW] CF para 12 | ADR never replaces the CMS route |
| No contacts, call logs, files or telephony; consent before sharing; India-only storage | [LAW] CF paras 13(1), 13(4), 14(4) | No skip tracing, third-party contact or device data |
| Settlement is the RE's discretion, approved one level above the sanctioner (Board for fraud or wilful defaulter); over 3 months or part settlement is restructuring; cooling period at least 12 months; consent decree if a case is pending; decision-making cannot be outsourced | [LAW] RSA paras 16(5), 87, 89–90, 95, 100, 157; OUT para 15 | Udofin relays and displays; [INTERP] a settlement sanction is a credit decision Udofin never takes |
| Conduct until 31 Dec 2026: police verification, notice and authorisation letter, website list, training, no harassment, calls 08:00–19:00; microfinance designated place and 09:00–18:00 | [LAW] RBC paras 90–91, 94–100 | Rule pack A |
| RBC Third Amendment Directions, 2026 (RBI/2026-27/230, 6 Aug 2026), **in force 1 Jan 2027**: paras 89–100 replaced by Section J, paras 100A–100AB | [LAW] RBI notification Id=13672 [VERIFY: official text not supplied in docs/regulations/rbi/] | Rule pack B: IIBF DRA certificate (100I; existing agents one more year); website agency list updated within 7 days (100K); agency details at least 1 day before the first visit (100L); notice of change (100M–N); minimum data to agents (100O); calls logged and recorded with disclosure, kept at least 6 months or until disposal if sub judice (100P); no harsh incentives (100Q); no device personal data (100U); contact 08:00–19:00 unless the borrower asks otherwise, avoiding bereavement, weddings and festivals (100Y(4)); pre-approved written communications naming the sender (100Y(8)); false statements are harsh (100Z); grievance officer's details on every recovery communication (100AA); TCCCPR (100AB). No numeric frequency cap |
| No unilateral appointment or forced choice from the lender's panel; referral to an institution not named in the agreement, with a silent borrower, is unilateral in substance | [JUD] *TRF v Energo* (2017) 8 SCC 377; *Perkins Eastman v HSCC* (2020) 20 SCC 760; *CORE v ECI-SPIC-SMO-MCML (JV)* (SC, 8 Nov 2024); *L&T Finance v Jai Paras Material Store* (Cal HC, 14 May 2026); *Shikha Ghosh v Axis Bank* (Del HC DB, 30 Sep 2026; next date 17 Nov 2026) | Udofin never refers, appoints or sees neutral selection (UR2) |
| Conciliation settlements have arbitral-award status; Mediation Act ss.4–25 and 27–30 not in force (s.26 in force) | [LAW] A&C Act ss.73–74; S.O. 4384(E), 9 Oct 2023 [VERIFY on egazette] | No mediated settlement is called a decree |
| DLG gives no collection right; RE invokes within 120 days overdue; never set off against the loan | [LAW] CF paras 25(2)–(4), 27(1) | DLG never shown in UR1 or used by UR4 |

### 7A.0.2 What Udofin may and may not do

| Activity | Udofin | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| RE-approved reminders, payment links, PTP capture, hardship request | May (all REs) | Servicing scope of the LSP agreement; contact policy; RE templates |
| Settlement request relay and display of the RE's offer; capture of the borrower's acceptance evidence | May (UR1 attached) | Offer is RE-issued and RE-approved; Udofin computes nothing |
| Display of RE-issued notices and case status | May (UR3 attached) | Only instruments and stages the RE's visibility policy permits |
| Borrower link into Equator or another ODR provider for a case the RE has referred | May (UR2 attached) | Referral basis recorded (pre-named institution or written post-dispute consent) |
| Tele-calling, field visits, cash receipts | Only where appointed (UR4) | Explicit recovery-agent contract; gates in UR4 |
| Approve, price or promise a settlement or waiver; negotiate within a band | **Never** | RSA para 16(5); OUT para 15 |
| Refer a dispute to arbitration, mediation, conciliation or Lok Adalat; nominate or veto a neutral | **Never** | The RE refers; Udofin credentials never hold the referral scope |
| Issue a legal notice or letter in Udofin's name (demand, LRN, SARFAESI s.13(2), NI Act s.138, A&C Act s.21, pledge invocation) | **Never** | Sender is always the RE (or its counsel or authorised officer) |
| Hold, pool or net money; take a fee from recovery proceeds | **Never** | CF para 10(2)–(5) |
| Repossess, invoke collateral, invoke DLG, start SARFAESI, litigation or IBC action | **Never** | RE-only acts (Finbyx R4–R10) |
| Skip tracing, asset search, contact with references or family, device lock | **Never** | CF para 13(1); RBC para 100; RBC Third Amendment paras 100S–100U |
| Hold the litigation record, call court-data APIs, see other REs' cases or the RE's settlement mandate | **Never** | Data ownership 7A.0.5 |

### 7A.0.3 Attach and detach

- **Unit of attachment:** RE tenant × product × capability (UR1–UR6). The entitlement is valid only when all three agree: the RE's licence SKU in U1, the LSP agreement scope (for UR4, the recovery-agent contract) and the feature flag `mod.udofin-recovery.[capability]`, evaluated server-side through an OpenFeature-compatible provider.
- **Manifest:** `modules/ur-recovery-support/module.yaml` declares id, version, `requires` (U1, U4, U11, U12, U15, U16, U21; U22 for field work), capabilities, events produced and consumed, APIs, permissions, data categories, `regulatory_refs`, `retention_class`, `licence_sku`, `ui_slots` and migrations.
- **Lifecycle:** `AVAILABLE → LICENSED → INSTALLED → CONFIGURED (maker-checker; RE approves templates, visibility policy and contact pack) → CERTIFIED (connector certification with the RE's suite; ConnectorCertified) → ENABLED (ModuleAttached) → READ_ONLY (ModuleDetached; RE detach or suspension switch, OUT para 17) → DETACHED (records retained)`.
- **On detach:** new allocations and requests are refused; all contact stops at once; open allocations are handed back (the RE issues `CollectionDeallocated` and notifies the borrower: RBC para 95; paras 100M–100N); in-flight settlement requests go to the RE with their evidence; the borrower keeps a read-only history and a "contact [RE name]" route; an export pack (JSON, CSV, PDF/A, SHA-256 manifest) goes to the RE (OUT paras 42–43, 87–88).
- **Read-only, never deleted:** detaching switches writes and UI off; it never shortens retention or lifts a legal hold.

| Record class | Minimum retention | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Call recordings and call logs (UR4) | 6 months, and until final disposal where the matter is sub judice; Udofin default 12 months | [LAW] Third Amendment para 100P from 1 Jan 2027 [VERIFY]; [REC] before then |
| Agent particulars notices, authorisation letters, delivery proofs, contact evaluations | Later of 8 years after loan closure and final disposal of any linked proceeding | [REC], covering limitation periods of 3 to 12 years (Limitation Act arts. 55, 62, 136) |
| Settlement requests, offers as displayed, acceptance evidence | As above | [REC]; RSA paras 89–100 records are the RE's |
| Cash receipts and Udofin's cash-in-transit ledger | 8 years from the end of the financial year | [LAW] Companies Act s.128(5) for Udofin's books |
| Notice delivery and read evidence (Udofin channel) | As the notice it evidences | [REC] |
| ADR case view | Until the RE's case closure plus the RE's schedule; originals stay with the provider | [REC] |

DPDP erasure requests are passed to the RE (`DataPrincipalRequest`); records needed to establish or defend a legal claim are kept under the applicable exemption and the borrower is told why [VERIFY: DPDP Act s.17(1)(a) wording and Rules commencement].

### 7A.0.4 Rule packs

- **Pack A** (to 31 Dec 2026): RBC paras 90–100. **Pack B** (from 1 Jan 2027): Third Amendment paras 100A–100AB. The pack is chosen by the timestamp of each attempt; both are effective-dated rule-pack versions in U16 and UR4.
- **Microfinance window:** pack A uses 09:00–18:00 (RBC para 91(2)). From 1 Jan 2027 microfinance loans move to pack B (RBC Third Amendment, RBI/2026-27/230): window and visit rules per paras 100Y(4), (5) and (7) [VERIFY: official text]; an RE may configure a narrower window (Finbyx IP4.8 keeps 09:00–18:00 by default), never a wider one (Part 7E MG2.8).
- **State overlays:** Karnataka Act 15 of 2025 and the Tamil Nadu Money Lending Entities (Prevention of Coercive Actions) Act, 2025 (notified 9 Jun 2025; ss.20–26 reach NBFCs operating in Tamil Nadu; vires contested) as configurable overlays [VERIFY current text and status].

### 7A.0.5 Data ownership

The RE's system (Finbyx R1–R16 or the RE's suite) is the system of record for the loan, dues, classification, recovery case and strategy, notices, litigation, settlement decisions and ADR referral and mandate; Udofin holds only labelled projections. The ADR provider holds the docket, neutral selection, orders and original settlements and awards; Udofin holds status and links. Udofin is the system of record for borrower interactions in its channels, consents, settlement requests as received, acceptance evidence, its own delivery and read evidence, agent activity and recordings where appointed, cash receipts and LSP grievances.

## UR1. Borrower overdue, settlement and payment centre

**Purpose:** one place where the borrower sees what is overdue, pays the RE, promises payment, asks for help, and asks for or responds to a settlement, without Udofin taking any decision.

**Capabilities:**

- **Overdue view** from the U12 mirror: DPD, SMA status with the RE's examples (IRACP paras 15, 17; RSA para 18) and each penal charge with its reason (RBC para 30(7)).
- **Pay now:** link, UPI intent or QR on the RE's merchant account, or a mandate re-presentation request; Udofin's acknowledgement reads "payment initiated" until the RE's receipt arrives (CF para 10(2)–(3)). Co-lending loans pay into the escrow (TDCR para 117); after `LoanTransferred` or `ServicerChanged` only the new instruction is used and old links are disabled the same day.
- **Promise to pay:** date, amount and channel → `PTPCaptured`. The screen carries no acknowledgement-of-debt wording unless the RE's legal team approves the template, because a written, signed acknowledgement restarts limitation (Limitation Act s.18) [INTERP].
- **Hardship request** (all products by policy; RBC para 89 for microfinance) as a U12 service request to the RE.
- **Settlement request:** proposed amount, schedule, reason and documents (system picker) → `SettlementRequested`.
- **RE offer** (`SettlementOfferIssued`): shown verbatim with hash, validity, schedule and a mandatory RE **characterisation block** (display blocked without it): restructuring if over 3 months or partial (RSA paras 89–90); CIC status "settled" (CIR para 12(4)); cooling period of at least 12 months (RSA para 95); consent decree if a case is pending (RSA para 100); for fraud or wilful defaulters, criminal proceedings and penal measures continue (RSA paras 97–98).
- **Acceptance:** OTP or Aadhaar eSign within validity, bound to the offer hash; sent as `SettlementOfferAccepted` (Integration Spec 6.8) with `offer_ref` and evidence. `SettlementApproved`, `SettlementBreached` and `RecoveryReceiptPosted` update the view with the RE's text.
- **Counter-proposal:** a new `SettlementRequested` linked to the offer. Udofin staff and bots never counter-offer.

**Mobile and web:** same centre on app and web; push carries no amount or PII; desktop web shows UPI QR. The operations portal sees status only, with no approve or edit control. Portal-only REs issue and approve offers in the lender portal under maker-checker that checks the approver's level against the RE's delegation matrix and blocks anyone who sanctioned the loan (RSA para 16(5)(i)); fraud and wilful-defaulter cases need a Board approval reference (para 16(5)(ii)). The field app shows offers read-only.

**States:**

- `settlement_request`: `DRAFT → SUBMITTED → ACKNOWLEDGED_BY_RE → {OFFER_ISSUED → {ACCEPTED → APPROVED → IN_PAYMENT → {COMPLETED | BREACHED} | OFFER_EXPIRED | DECLINED_BY_BORROWER} | DECLINED_BY_RE} | WITHDRAWN`.
- `ptp`: `CAPTURED → DUE → {KEPT | PART_KEPT | BROKEN}`, set only from RE payment events.

**Data:** `settlement_request`, `settlement_offer_mirror` (RE reference, terms, validity, characterisation, hash), `settlement_acceptance_evidence` (method, transaction ID, offer hash, timestamp, device), `ptp`, `hardship_request`; `payment_intent` from U11.

**Controls:** no Udofin role can create or alter an offer, waiver or appropriation; no acceptance after validity; AI explains but never negotiates; no false urgency (para 100Z); borrower's language (RBC para 10) and grievance block (para 100AA); no cross-selling in recovery communications [REC]; DLG never shown as reducing dues (CF para 25(2)).

**Events:** consumes `DPDChanged`, `AssetClassificationChanged`, `PaymentReceived`, `PaymentBounced`, `SettlementOfferIssued`, `SettlementApproved`, `SettlementBreached`, `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `LoanTransferred`, `ServicerChanged`; produces `SettlementRequested`, `SettlementOfferAccepted`, `PTPCaptured`.

**Tests:** offer without a characterisation block is not displayed; acceptance after validity is rejected; no Udofin role can write an offer (permission matrix test); a gateway "success" never marks a due as paid; old payment links are disabled after `ServicerChanged`; a co-lending payment never targets one RE's account; PTP screen contains no unapproved acknowledgement text; portal-only approval by the loan's sanctioner is blocked.

## UR2. Dispute and ADR access (Equator; no separate app)

**Purpose:** let the borrower take part in an ADR process that the RE has lawfully started, or ask the RE for one, from inside the Udofin app or web, while Udofin never refers.

**Routes the borrower may see (RE-approved neutral text):**

| Route | Status today | Udofin role |
|---|---|---|
| RE grievance, then RBI CMS | In force (CF para 12) | Always visible; never displaced by ADR |
| Conciliation (A&C Act Part III) | In force; s.74 award status; 30 days' silence rejects an invitation (s.62(4)) | Shows RE-referred sessions; relays borrower requests |
| Mediation (Mediation Act 2023) | Enforcement provisions not in force; a mediated settlement is a contract only | Never calls it a decree |
| Arbitration | Only where the loan agreement names Equator or another institution, or the borrower gives written post-dispute consent | Link into the provider's flow for RE-referred cases only |
| Lok Adalat (LSA Act ss.19–21) | Deemed decree, no appeal; next National Lok Adalat 12 Dec 2026 [VERIFY: nalsa.gov.in] | Shows the notice and sitting details |
| Consumer commission | An arbitration clause does not bar it (*Emaar MGF v Aftab Singh* (2019) 12 SCC 751) | Never discouraged |

**Capabilities:**

- **Case view** from ADR events sent by the RE, or by Equator under the RE's data-sharing terms: referral (track and basis), consent, neutral appointed (name and disclosure filed; no selection data), hearings, status, outcome and compliance.
- **Signed link** into the provider's web flow: single-use, short-lived, journey-bound token, no PII in the URL; in-app browser tab (Custom Tabs, SFSafariViewController) limited to the provider's allow-listed domain, no JavaScript bridge; a new tab on web. The provider authenticates by OTP and runs any eSign or DigiLocker step itself.
- **Post-dispute consent** is captured in the provider's flow with an explicit decline path (s.11 petition or ordinary courts); online mediation consent (Mediation Act s.30, when in force) and fast-track consent (A&C Act s.29B) are separate. Udofin never pre-ticks, never bundles consent with loan acceptance or a settlement, and never asks again after a decline unless the RE issues a new referral.
- **Borrower-initiated request:** a dispute form (category `adr_request`) goes to the RE as `GrievanceRaised`. The RE decides. The RE's reply, or day 31 without one, shows the CMS route.
- **Reminders** for hearings (at least 3 days before, [REC]) through U16; documents are uploaded in the provider's flow, not stored by Udofin.
- **Outcome:** settlement or award summary as sent; any payment link is the RE's; compliance status from `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`.
- **Disclosure:** the ADR page states that Equator and Udofin are Infrabyx products and that Equator is independent of the RE and of Udofin in appointing neutrals [REC; legal note required].

**Mobile and web:** same case view on app and web; the operations portal sees link health only, never case content; the lender portal shows the RE its own referrals.

**States (mirror):** `NOT_REFERRED → REFERRED → CONSENT_PENDING → {CONSENTED | DECLINED | DEEMED_DECLINED} → NEUTRAL_APPOINTED → HEARING_SCHEDULED ⇄ IN_PROGRESS → {SETTLED | AWARD_ISSUED | NON_SETTLEMENT | WITHDRAWN | STAYED} → COMPLIANCE → CLOSED`. For an arbitration referral, `CONSENTED` follows `REFERRED` only where the basis is `post_dispute_consent`, and a `clause_names_institution` referral goes straight to `NEUTRAL_APPOINTED`; conciliation and mediation referrals always pass through `CONSENT_PENDING` (A&C Act s.62; 30 days' silence is `DEEMED_DECLINED`, s.62(4)).

**Data:** `adr_case_view` (RE reference, provider, provider case ID, track, basis, status, last sequence), `adr_link_issue` (token hash, expiry, used_at), `adr_request`, `adr_info_view_event`.

**Controls:**

- The scope `adr.referral:create` is never issued to Udofin credentials (Ecosystem Integration Specification); a test proves Udofin cannot call it.
- A referral event without `basis` (pre-named institution with clause reference and version, or post-dispute consent reference) shows no call to action; Udofin raises `ComplianceIssueRaised` to the RE and its GRC tool.
- Udofin never sees neutral selection, the RE's settlement mandate or any other lender's case.
- When the RE sends an IBC moratorium, deceased-borrower or court-stay hold, ADR actions are hidden.
- Udofin records nothing in hearings; mediation and conciliation confidentiality (A&C Act s.75; Mediation Act ss.22–23 when in force) means no Udofin analytics on session content.

**Events:** consumes `ADRReferralCreated`, `ADRConsentRecorded`, `ADRNeutralAppointed`, `ADRHearingScheduled`, `ADRCaseStatusChanged`, `ADROutcomeRecorded`, `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`; produces `GrievanceRaised` (ADR request) and `ComplianceIssueRaised` (missing basis).

**Tests:** Udofin client credentials get 403 on referral creation; referral without basis shows no action and raises an issue; link token reuse and expiry rejected; in-app browser blocks non-allow-listed domains; consent screen is never shown inside the loan-acceptance journey; CMS route visible on every ADR screen; hold status hides actions.

## UR3. Notices and case visibility

**Purpose:** deliver the RE's notices and letters as an additional channel with evidence, and show recovery and case status only as the RE permits.

**Capabilities:**

- **Notice inbox** fed by `LegalNoticeIssued`: RE-signed PDF/A with hash, instrument (reminder, loan recall, agent intimation, settlement offer, SARFAESI s.13(2) or possession or sale notice copy, NI Act s.138 or PSS Act s.25 notice copy, A&C Act s.21 notice copy, gold auction notice, pledge invocation notice, Lok Adalat notice), statute reference, language and template version.
- **Udofin channel only:** in-app, SMS with a link to the authenticated inbox, and email, each producing `NoticeServiceUpdated` with Udofin's evidence (delivered, opened, fully scrolled). Udofin's delivery **never replaces** the statutory mode the RE must use (SARFAESI Rules, r.3; A&C Act s.3) and Udofin never marks a notice "served" or "deemed served" (*Sedhram Nilkanth Muglikar v M.R. Makhare*, Bom HC, 2026).
- **Visibility policy** per RE × product × instrument × stage, **off by default**, with RE-legal-approved wording for each status string (for example "Your lender has started proceedings under the SARFAESI Act; next step: …").
- **Case status** projection from `RecoveryCaseOpened`, `RecoveryStrategyChanged` (stage only), `LitigationCaseOpened`, `LitigationCaseUpdated`, `HearingScheduled` (date only), `LitigationCaseClosed`, `AssetRepossessed` (with the possession memo and inventory the RE sends; RBC para 26; *Hari Dutta Sharma v State of UP*, SC, 16 Sep 2026), `AuctionScheduled`, `AuctionConcluded`, `SurplusRefunded` (RBC para 66 for gold), `CollateralInvoked` and `RecoveryCaseClosed`. Udofin calls no court-data API and keeps no litigation record.
- **Borrower actions:** confirm receipt (never an admission of the debt), ask for another language (RBC para 10), dispute the notice with the RE's GRO, download. Addressees are only the borrower, co-borrower and guarantor of record (RBC para 100; para 100Y). No WhatsApp; push carries no content.

**Mobile and web:** inbox on app and web; delivery failures in the operations portal; visibility policy set in the lender portal with maker-checker and RE legal approval.

**States:** `notice_delivery`: `RECEIVED_FROM_RE → PUBLISHED → {DELIVERED → OPENED → READ_FULLY | NOT_DELIVERED → FALLBACK_SENT} → (WITHDRAWN_BY_RE)`.

**Data:** `notice_mirror` (RE reference, instrument, statute reference, language, SHA-256, template version, RE statutory mode, visibility policy version), `notice_delivery_event`, `case_status_projection`, `visibility_policy`.

**Controls:** hash check before display; no Udofin generation or editing of notice content; the sender is always the RE (or its counsel or authorised officer), Udofin appears only as "delivered by Udofin, LSP of [RE name]"; approved status strings only; no "served" state; grievance block on every recovery communication (para 100AA).

**Events:** consumes the events listed above and `NoticeServiceUpdated` from the RE where the policy permits showing statutory delivery status; produces `NoticeServiceUpdated` (Udofin channel) and `GrievanceRaised`.

**Tests:** tampered PDF is not displayed; an instrument outside the policy never appears; no API or UI path sets "served"; WhatsApp channel is not selectable for any recovery template; an unregistered addressee never receives a notice; a withdrawn notice shows the RE's withdrawal text.

## UR4. Recovery-agent operations (only where appointed)

**Purpose:** where an RE appoints Udofin (or an agency Udofin engages with the RE's prior consent, OUT para 34(iv)) as recovery agent, work allocated cases within the RE's policy, the RBC rules and full evidence.

**Hard gates (all must pass; fail closed):**

1. Active `recovery_agent_contract` covering the RE, product, DPD bucket, territory and channel (tele, field, cash) on the attempt date; otherwise `CollectionAllocated` is rejected with a reason.
2. Udofin's recovery role disclosed in the KFS (RBC Annex I Part 2 item 6(ii)) or notified under CF para 9(6).
3. Agent eligible: police and antecedent verification current (RBC para 94); training and code-of-conduct undertaking (paras 98–99); RE authorisation letter and ID (paras 95–96); from 1 Jan 2027, IIBF DRA certificate (para 100I; existing agents by 31 Dec 2027) [VERIFY].
4. Agent particulars delivered to the borrower by email or SMS before first contact (CF para 9(6)); from 1 Jan 2027, agency details at least 1 day before the first visit (para 100L) [VERIFY].
5. `canContact(account, party, channel, purpose, time)` permits the attempt; it runs before every attempt, logs denials and fails closed. Checks: party of record; window per pack, borrower preference and microfinance rules; sensitive-occasion blackout; the RE's Board frequency cap (RBI sets no number); stop on payment, PTP not yet due, open dispute, litigation, ADR or IBC hold, stay or deceased borrower; registered 1600-series caller ID [VERIFY: TRAI coverage of agency calls]; pre-approved template with sender and grievance block (paras 100Y(8), 100AA).

**Capabilities:**

- Allocation intake, worklists by bucket and territory, scripts in the borrower's language, outcome codes, PTP, field-visit check-in on the **agent's** device (never the borrower's location), digital receipts.
- Call recording with a disclosure prompt on every recovery call; call time and count logged (para 100P; [REC] before 1 Jan 2027); legal-hold flag extends retention.
- **Settlement during calls:** the agent or bot may only present an offer the RE has already issued for that account (`SettlementOfferIssued`); anything else is a `SettlementRequested` for the RE.
- **Cash:** only on overdue loans and where the contract allows; full-amount digital receipt; cash-in-transit ledger; RE posting confirmed the same day, otherwise escalation at end of day (CF para 10(5)); per-receipt and per-agent cash limits from the RE [VERIFY: Income-tax Act 2025 cash-receipt limit].
- **Hand-back, not escalation:** Udofin never decides on legal action; it returns the case with outcome codes and the RE issues `RecoveryStrategyChanged` or `CollectionDeallocated`.
- **Agency list feed** to the RE's website (RBC para 97; para 100K update within 7 days).
- **Voicebot or chat agent** [REC; RBI FREE-AI report, 13 Aug 2025, guidance only]: discloses it is automated and acting for the RE; offers a human at any turn; same `canContact` envelope; transcripts kept as recordings.

**Mobile and web:** field app (channel E, U22): minimum case data (para 100O), encrypted offline cache, remote wipe, recorded calls through the RE's trunk, digital ID and authorisation letter (RBC para 95), no contacts, SMS, call-log or storage permissions. Operations portal: tele-calling workspace with the `canContact` banner, QA and the agent register. Lender portal: allocations, conduct metrics, recording samples, suspension switch. Borrower app: agent particulars, "verify this agent" (QR on the agent's ID) and a recovery-grievance button (RBC para 92).

**States:**

- `collection_allocation`: `OFFERED → {ACCEPTED | REJECTED} → NOTICE_PENDING → NOTICE_DELIVERED → ACTIVE → {RESOLVED | RETURNED | DEALLOCATED | SUSPENDED} → CLOSED`.
- `contact_attempt`: `EVALUATED → {DENIED (reason) | PERMITTED → ATTEMPTED → {RIGHT_PARTY | NO_ANSWER | WRONG_PARTY | REFUSED}}`.

**Data:** `recovery_agent_contract`, `recovery_agent`, `agent_certification` (IIBF reference, expiry), `agent_authorisation`, `collection_allocation`, `agent_particulars_notice`, `contact_policy_pack`, `contact_evaluation` (inputs, pack version, decision), `contact_attempt`, `call_recording` (retention_until, legal_hold), `field_visit`, `ptp`, `cash_receipt`, `cash_in_transit_entry`, `agent_scorecard`.

**Controls:** incentives exclude raw call volume and include conduct metrics (para 100Q); DLG cover is invisible to agents and to the policy engine (Part 4.4); the RE audits a sample of cases where Udofin is both DLG provider and recovery agent [REC]; no photographs of people; no contact with references, family or employer; no device data (para 100U).

**Events:** consumes `CollectionAllocated`, `CollectionDeallocated`, `RecoveryAgentNoticeSent` (gate 4 evidence where the RE sends the particulars: CF para 9(6)), `LegalHoldChanged` (retention and contact holds), `RecoveryStrategyChanged`, `SettlementOfferIssued`, `PaymentReceived`, `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `LitigationCaseUpdated` (hold flag), `ModuleDetached`; produces `CollectionActivityLogged`, `PTPCaptured`, `FieldVisitLogged`, `ReceiptIssued`, `SettlementRequested`, `GrievanceRaised` (misconduct), `ComplianceIssueRaised` (gate breach).

**Tests:** allocation rejected without a contract, outside territory or for an ineligible agent; no attempt before a delivered particulars notice; attempts at 07:59 and 19:01 denied (08:59 and 18:01 for microfinance); pack B used from 1 Jan 2027; open dispute stops contact; unrecorded call flagged; unposted cash receipt escalates at end of day; bot cannot state a figure not in an RE offer; detach stops attempts at once.

## UR5. Data feeds to the RE's recovery suite

**Purpose:** give the RE's recovery suite (Finbyx Part 7A or a third-party system through the generic connector) complete, consented and reconcilable data from Udofin.

| Feed | Content | Timing | Event or transport |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promises to pay | Date, amount, channel, captured by | Real time | `PTPCaptured` |
| Settlement requests and acceptances | Proposal or offer reference, evidence | Real time | `SettlementRequested`; `SettlementOfferAccepted` |
| Disputes and complaints on the debt | Category, stop-contact flag | Real time | `GrievanceRaised`, `GrievanceUpdated` |
| Hardship and contact-detail changes | Borrower-verified changes | Real time | U12 service request |
| Contact attempts and outcomes (UR4) | Evaluation result, attempt, recording reference | Real time | `CollectionActivityLogged`, `FieldVisitLogged` |
| Cash receipts (UR4) | Full amount, receipt number, agent, time | Same day | `ReceiptIssued` |
| Notice delivery on Udofin's channel | Delivered, opened, read | Real time | `NoticeServiceUpdated` |
| Consent and rights requests | Withdrawal, erasure, access | Real time | `ConsentWithdrawn`, `DataPrincipalRequest` |
| Risk signals | Payment-failure patterns, suspected fraud | Real time | `RiskSignalRaised` |
| Engagement summary | Overdue-centre views, payment intents per loan | Daily | `DailyReconciliationFile` extension |

**Rules:**

- CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with `tenantid`, `reid`, `consentref` and `seq`; OpenAPI pull for backfill; SFTP file fallback for REs without APIs (Part 5.3); every payload cites a consent reference or a contractual or statutory basis flag (CF para 13(4)).
- Minimum data: no device data, no contact lists, no borrower location, no inferred hardship from device signals.
- **Routing:** co-lending feeds go to the servicer RE named as the single point of interface (TDCR paras 104–105); transferred loans follow `ServicerChanged`.
- **Daily reconciliation:** allocations vs activity, PTPs vs payments, cash receipts vs RE postings (same day), notices delivered, settlement requests acknowledged; breaks aged for the RE's audit committee (OUT paras 12(2), 39).

**States:** `feed_delivery`: `QUEUED → SENT → ACKED → {APPLIED | REJECTED (schema or consent)} → RECONCILED`, with dead-letter and maker-checker replay.

**Mobile and web:** back-end only; feed health and breaks in the operations and lender portals.

**Events:** produces the events in the table; consumes RE acknowledgements and `ConnectorCertified`.

**Tests:** payload without consent or basis is rejected before sending; schema registry rejects a breaking change without a new version; duplicate delivery is idempotent; a co-lending feed never reaches the partner RE directly; reconciliation flags a cash receipt without a same-day RE posting.

## UR6. Conduct, consent and evidence controls

**Purpose:** make every recovery conduct rule provable to the RE, its auditors, RBI and the RE's GRC tool.

| Control | Rule | Mechanism | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| UR6-C01 | Contact window and frequency (RBC paras 91(2), 100; para 100Y(4)) | `canContact` before every attempt | Evaluation log incl. denials; zero out-of-window attempts |
| UR6-C02 | Notice before contact (CF para 9(6); para 100L) | UR4 gate | Delivered-notice reference per allocation |
| UR6-C03 | Agent eligibility (RBC paras 94, 98–99; para 100I) | Register gate | No allocation to an ineligible agent |
| UR6-C04 | Recording and logging (para 100P) | Recording service | Coverage % and retention dates |
| UR6-C05 | Pre-approved, vernacular communications with grievance block (RBC para 10; paras 100Y(8), 100AA) | Template registry | Template ID on every message |
| UR6-C06 | No threats, humiliation or false statements (RBC para 100; para 100Z) | Content lint on scripts and templates; QA sampling | Lint results; QA scores |
| UR6-C07 | No third-party contact or device data (CF para 13(1); para 100U) | Party-of-record check; permission audit | Denials; manifest scans |
| UR6-C08 | Money rules (CF para 10(2)–(5)) | Account validator; cash ledger | Zero Udofin accounts; same-day posting rate |
| UR6-C09 | Settlement authority (RSA para 16(5); OUT para 15) | Permission matrix | Quarterly access review |
| UR6-C10 | ADR referral basis (*CORE*, 8 Nov 2024; *L&T Finance*, 14 May 2026) | Scope denial; basis check | Denied calls; issues raised |
| UR6-C11 | Notices sent only by the RE | Sender check on templates | Template metadata |
| UR6-C12 | No WhatsApp in recovery (platform policy) | Channel configuration test | CI result |
| UR6-C13 | Grievance routing and CMS display (CF para 12; RBC para 92) | U15 routing | Forwarding receipts |
| UR6-C14 | India storage, retention and legal hold (CF para 14(4); para 100P) | Retention engine | Purge and hold logs |
| UR6-C15 | Bot disclosure and human hand-over [REC; FREE-AI report] | Bot policy | Transcript samples |
| UR6-C16 | DLG neutrality (Part 4.4) | No DLG fields in UR4 data | Schema test |

**Capabilities:** conduct dashboard per RE (complaints per 1,000 allocated accounts, out-of-window attempts, recording coverage, QA score, notice-before-contact rate, same-day cash posting rate) feeding the RE's FPC conduct pack (RBC para 8); breach workflow that suspends the agent, raises `ComplianceIssueRaised` within 24 hours [REC] and supports the RE's compensation process (para 100F) [VERIFY]; evidence to LawDocsComply or a third-party GRC tool as `ControlTestResultPublished` and `EvidenceSubmitted`, with periodic OSCAL assessment-results export; aggregate counts and masked sample IDs only, hash-chained, stored in India.

**Mobile and web:** operations and lender portals only; borrowers see the grievance route and agent verification (UR4).

**States:** `control_test_run`: `SCHEDULED → RUNNING → {PASSED | FAILED → ISSUE_RAISED → REMEDIATED → RETESTED}`.

**Events:** produces `ControlTestResultPublished`, `EvidenceSubmitted`, `ComplianceIssueRaised`, `PolicyAttested`; consumes `ObligationPublished`.

**Tests:** every UR6 control has an automated test and an owner; a synthetic out-of-window attempt fails C01 and raises an issue; evidence export contains no unmasked identifier; a detached module still publishes retention evidence; the OSCAL export validates against the OSCAL 1.2.x schema [VERIFY: version in use by each GRC tool].

# PART 7B — LENDER PARTNERSHIPS, DEAL CONFIGURATION AND RE AUDIT EXPORTS

**Purpose.** Turn every lender relationship into a governed, versioned **deal** that passes due diligence, legal execution, technical certification and a controlled pilot before going live; configure it without code inside the guard-rails; give each RE self-service audit, inspection and CIMS export packs; admit credit co-operative societies through a ring-fenced non-RE track; and suspend or exit a deal without stranding a borrower.

**Extends, does not replace.** U1 (tenancy, LSP agreement registry, activity gate), U2 (product catalogue), U18 (DLA register, evidence, audit access), U19 (lender dashboards), Part 5.3 (connector certification), Part 7A.0.3 (module attach and detach) and Part 10.8 (vendor obligations). Where this Part and U1 or U2 differ, this Part prevails. Read-only access for RE auditors and RBI-authorised persons is RA2 (Part 7H); archive format and RE-controlled storage are RA3; co-operative member journeys are MG1 (Part 7E).

**Applicability.**

| Lender class | Track | Binding source | Udofin role |
|---|---|---|---|
| NBFC (BL, ML, UL, TL), NBFC-MFI, NBFC-ICC, HFC | RE track (UP1–UP3, UP5) | CF Ch III paras 6–30 through the RE's contract; OUT Ch III and, where material IT outsourcing, Ch IV | LSP and outsourcing service provider |
| Commercial bank, SFB, UCB, StCB, DCCB | RE track with the bank rule pack | Bank digital-lending and outsourcing Directions [VERIFY: texts not supplied; onboarding blocked until mapped] | LSP |
| Credit co-operative society (State Act or MSCS Act) | Non-RE track (UP4) | Not an RBI RE; State Act or MSCS Act 2002 (as amended 2023); DPDP; consumer law; RE-equivalent conduct by contract | Technology and sourcing provider; DPDP processor |
| Infrabyx group RE | RE track plus group controls | OUT paras 45–51, 90–92 | Arm's length; same clause matrix |

**Codes used.** CF, OUT, RBC, CIR, KYC, AA, MFI, TDCR, CYB, FRM, SR (supervisory returns, for RE references only); non-RBI: `MSCS`, `SCS` (State co-operative Acts), `DPDP`, `CICRA`, `TRAI`, `CCPA-DP` (CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023), `GUID` (RBI FREE-AI report, 13 Aug 2025). Requirement IDs follow Part 8A (`REQ-CF-6(2)`, `REQ-OUT-34(iv)`); new Udofin-only controls are `UP-Cnn`. Labels: **[LAW]** statute, **[REG]** RBI or other regulator's Direction, **[INTERP]** our reading, **[REC]** recommendation, **[MKT]** market practice; anything unconfirmed carries `[VERIFY: …]`.

**Data owned by Udofin.** Deal records, due-diligence packs and Udofin's declarations, the per-deal configuration versions, the RE's approval artefacts, export-pack manifests and delivery logs, the non-RE lender profile and eligibility checks, exit plans and data-return certificates. **Not owned:** the RE's Board policies (Udofin holds evidence copies only), the RE's credit policy and BRE rules (hosted for the RE, never edited: OUT para 15), CIMS filings (the RE files: CF para 18), loan records (Part 5.1).

**Events and APIs (Integration Specification v1.1 section 6.28).** Udofin produces `LenderDealProposed`, `LenderDealApproved`, `LenderDealActivated`, `LenderDealSuspended`, `LenderDealTerminated`; Finbyx (or the RE's GRC tool) consumes them to maintain the RE's LSP register and the OUT para 36 central record of material outsourcing; LawDocsComply receives them in the RE's compliance mode. Every deal event carries `lender_type` (`RE` or `NON_RE_SOCIETY`); the internal tenant class is `lender_class` (`RE` or `NON_RE_COOP`), mapped one to one. The RE's system reads configuration versions through `GET /v1/deals/{id}/config-versions/{version}` and countersigns transitions and versions through `POST /v1/deals/{id}/approvals` (or the same actions in the lender portal). Export packs use `ExportRequested` and `ExportCompleted` (scope `RE_PACK`, section 6.26). Module attachment uses `ModuleAttached` and `ModuleDetached` unchanged.

**Workspaces.** Operations portal (channel C) and lender portal (channel D) both use the top-level menu **Partners**, filtered by role and, in channel D, to the RE's own deals: `Partners › Deals`, `Partners › Due diligence`, `Partners › Configuration`, `Partners › Exports`, `Partners › Exit`, and `Partners › Members` for society staff. The society track (UP4) uses the same menu with society labels. Every list screen supports saved views, CSV export of the visible columns (no PII), `/` to search, `j`/`k` to move and `a` to approve where the role permits; all screens meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

## UP1. Partner onboarding and due-diligence workflow

### Purpose and scope

One workflow takes a prospective lender from first proposal to live operation and keeps it under periodic review. It produces the evidence the RE needs for its own enhanced due diligence on Udofin (CF para 6(2); OUT paras 29–32), records Udofin's counter-party diligence on the RE, and blocks go-live until every regulatory precondition is evidenced. It replaces the U1 "onboarding workflow" bullet with a full state machine.

### Deal state machine

`lender_deal`: `PROPOSED → DUE_DILIGENCE → LEGAL → TECHNICAL_CERTIFICATION → PILOT → ACTIVE`, with `PILOT` or `ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED`, then `TERMINATING → TERMINATED`; `WITHDRAWN` is reachable from `PROPOSED`, `DUE_DILIGENCE` and `LEGAL`, and `UNDER_REVIEW` is an overlay flag on `PILOT` or `ACTIVE` that never stops service.

| Transition | Gate (all must pass; fail closed) | Evidence captured | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| (new) → PROPOSED | Lender class identified (RE or non-RE); RE type and layer from the RBI CoR or registry certificate; conflict pre-check (OUT para 18(vi)); NDA executed | Proposal record, CoR or registration certificate, NDA | `LenderDealProposed` |
| PROPOSED → DUE_DILIGENCE | Udofin's DD pack published (below); RE questionnaire received | Pack hash, delivery receipt | — |
| DUE_DILIGENCE → LEGAL | RE confirms DD complete and records its materiality assessment (OUT para 14) and approving authority under its Board outsourcing policy (OUT para 20(ii)); Udofin's counter-party DD passed or exceptions approved by Udofin's compliance head | RE DD completion letter, materiality note, Udofin DD result | — |
| LEGAL → TECHNICAL_CERTIFICATION | LSP agreement executed with every OUT para 34 clause and, for IT scope, para 74 clause marked present in the clause matrix (`outsourcing_clause_check`); DPA executed; DLG agreement if chosen (CF para 22); recovery-agent contract if chosen (CF para 6(5)); counsel vetting recorded by the RE (OUT para 33) | Executed agreements (hashes), clause matrix, counsel vetting reference | `LenderDealApproved` |
| TECHNICAL_CERTIFICATION → PILOT | Connector certification passed (Part 5.3; `ConnectorCertified`); deal configuration version approved by both sides (UP2); products published and approved (U2); **RE has reported each Udofin DLA on CIMS** and uploaded acknowledgement evidence (CF para 18(1)–(2)); **RE website disclosure page lists Udofin, its DLAs and activities** (CF para 9(4)); app-store listing names the RE as partner (Google Play India personal-loan policy) [VERIFY current policy text]; GRO and nodal-officer contacts live on DLA and in the KFS template (CF para 12(2)); current redress profile (UB-C09) | CIMS acknowledgement, website screenshot with timestamp and URL hash, store listing snapshot, certification report | `LenderDealActivated` (`mode = PILOT`, `resumed = false`) |
| PILOT → ACTIVE | Pilot exit criteria met (below); RE sign-off; Udofin compliance sign-off | Pilot report | `LenderDealActivated` (`mode = GENERAL`, `resumed = false`) |
| PILOT or ACTIVE → SUSPENDED | RE suspension switch (OUT paras 17, 43), Udofin suspension (UP5), regulatory trigger | Reason code, suspension type (UP5) | `LenderDealSuspended` |
| SUSPENDED → PILOT or ACTIVE (state before suspension) | Cause cured and both sides approve | Cure evidence | `LenderDealActivated` (`mode` of the restored state, `resumed = true`) |
| PILOT, ACTIVE or SUSPENDED → TERMINATING → TERMINATED | Exit plan approved and executed (UP5) | Exit plan, data-return certificate | `LenderDealTerminated` on entering TERMINATED |

**Rules.**

- No borrower-facing journey, offer or communication for a lender exists before `LenderDealActivated` with `mode = PILOT`. The activity gate in U1 reads the deal state, not only the agreement.
- Each transition is maker-checker inside Udofin and records the RE approver's name, role and authority reference (`re_change_approval`, received through `POST /v1/deals/{id}/approvals` or the lender portal). A rejected gate returns the deal to the same state with the failing items named; nothing is partially applied.
- Timers: a deal idle in `PROPOSED`, `DUE_DILIGENCE` or `LEGAL` for 90 days raises a reminder to both owners and, after 180 days, a proposal to withdraw [REC]; `PILOT` ends on the pilot plan's end date with an exit decision (go-live, extend once by up to 90 days, or terminate).
- `LenderDealSuspended` carries the event scope `NEW_BUSINESS` for `NEW_SOURCING_PAUSED` and `ALL` for the other suspension types, with the Udofin suspension type in the reason code (UP5).
- A deal is per lender legal entity; products, channels and states are scoped in UP2. One RE may have several deals only if they differ by legal entity [REC].

### Two-way due diligence

**A. Udofin's pack for the RE (versioned, each item with an expiry date; refreshed at least annually and on material change: OUT para 38).**

| Item | Source requirement | Udofin evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Incorporation, CIN, shareholding, directors and KMP | CF para 19 (company for DLG); OUT para 30(i) | MCA master data extract, shareholding register extract |
| Ownership and control declaration: no RE director or relative owns or controls Udofin; for IT scope, no RE KMP, approver or relative | OUT paras 18(vi), 59 | Signed `lsp_declaration` per RE, annual re-declaration |
| Financial soundness: audited financials, net worth, going-concern note | OUT para 30(iv) | Audited statements, auditor's report |
| Litigation, regulatory actions, complaint statistics | OUT para 30(v); CF para 6(2) "past records of conduct" | Litigation register extract; complaints by category and TAT (U19) |
| Technical capability, architecture, uptime history, DR | CF para 6(2); OUT paras 30(vii), 32, 40 | Architecture summary, SLA history, BCP and DR test reports |
| Security assurance: VAPT and IS audit summaries, CERT-In empanelled auditor reports, certification **readiness** status | OUT paras 30(vii), 79; CYB paras 121–126 | Summaries with remediation status; ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 shown only as programme status, never as a certificate unless one is issued |
| Data privacy and storage: privacy policy, storage and destruction policy, data map, localisation attestation | CF paras 14(1)–(4), 15 | Published policy versions and hashes; India-only hosting attestation; sub-processor locations |
| DLA permission manifest per build and platform | CF para 13(1) | `permission_manifest` scan results |
| Sub-processor and supply-chain list | OUT paras 34(iv), 74(xi), 82 | `subprocessor` register with processing location |
| Nodal grievance officer and grievance process | CF para 12(1)–(3) | Appointment letter, process note, contact details |
| Matching mechanism and change log; ranking metric publication | CF para 7(2), 7(4) | `matching_mechanism_version` history; published metric |
| Money-flow design: RE accounts only | CF para 10(1)–(4) | Configuration-validator report; reconciliation proof (Part 4.3) |
| DLG provider declaration (only if DLG is offered) | CF para 20(3) | Statutory-auditor-certified declaration (U14) |
| AI inventory; PI and cyber insurance | [GUID] FREE-AI report; OUT para 30(iv) [REC] | `ai_model_inventory` extract; policy schedules |

**B. Udofin's diligence on the lender (counter-party diligence) [REC].**

| Check | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| CoR verified on RBI's public list; RE type and layer; asset size and date | Rule-pack selection (CYB chapter, OUT Ch IV scope, RB-IOS coverage, IO applicability) | `re_regulatory_profile` with source and date |
| **Board-policy evidence**: outsourcing policy (OUT para 20), FPC (RBC para 7(1)), grievance mechanism with next-higher-level review (RBC para 7(2) Note), interest-rate and charges policy (RBC para 7(3)), microfinance FPC where relevant (RBC para 7(5)), recovery-agent engagement policy and code of conduct (RBC para 7(7)–(8)), DLG policy if DLG (CF para 20(1)), CIR policy (CIR para 20), monitoring mechanism for LSP-originated portfolios (CF para 6(4)), digital-lending and KYC policies | Udofin applies these policies; it must hold the version it applies | `re_board_policy_evidence` (policy type, version, Board or committee approval date, extract or certified copy, expiry or review date) |
| CIC memberships (all four) | CIR para 6; U6 bureau mode | Membership confirmations |
| AA FIU status | AA para 8(12); U6 | FIU registration reference |
| PML Act s.11A notification status | Aadhaar OTP e-KYC routing (U5) | Notification reference or "not notified" |
| Penalties and adverse RBI actions in the last 3 years; caution lists | Reputational risk [REC] | Search log |
| GRO, nodal officer, PNO (if RB-IOS applies), IO (if applicable), CIC nodal officer, recovery-grievance contact | CF para 12; RBC para 92; CIR para 34(2); RB-IOS cl.18(2) | `deal_grievance_contact` (UB3) |
| Website disclosure page and FPC URL | CF para 9(4)–(5); RBC para 21 | URL and snapshot hash |
| 1600-series number registration for RE service calls | TRAI Direction of 19 Nov 2025 for RBI-regulated entities (NBFCs other than those above ₹5,000 crore: from 1 Mar 2026) | Number list for RA5 |

**C. LSP declarations at LEGAL and annually** (`lsp_declaration`, signed by an authorised Udofin officer with a DSC or Aadhaar eSign, stored with its hash): ownership and control (OUT 18(vi), 59); no borrower fees (CF 10(4)); no control of funds or pool account (CF 10(1)–(3)); India-only storage (CF 14(4)); no prohibited permissions or biometric storage (CF 13(1), 14(3)); CIMS never marketed as RBI registration (CF 18(6)); RBI access and inspection of Udofin and subcontractors (OUT 34(viii)–(ix), 81); subcontractor consent (OUT 34(iv)); incident notice (OUT 61); no erasure during transition (OUT 87); AI usage disclosure [GUID].

### Pilot

- **Plan (`deal_pilot_plan`):** products, channels (web first allowed), states, application and disbursal caps, duration (default 90 days [REC]), owners. Caps are enforced by the activity gate; a breach pauses new applications, never servicing.
- **Exit criteria (system-measured):** connector errors below threshold; no reconciliation break older than T+2 in the last 15 business days; KFS acknowledgement evidence on 100% of executed loans; zero money-flow validator exceptions; 100% of grievances forwarded within the U15 target; zero permission-manifest deviations; offer-neutrality audit passed (U19).

### Periodic review (overlay)

- **Annual** (OUT para 38; conduct review, CF para 6(3)): DD pack refreshed, declarations re-signed, conduct pack P3 sent. **Half-yearly:** central-record feed for the RE's Board or RMC review (OUT para 36).
- **Triggered** by change of control, new subcontractor, data-centre move, severity-1 or 2 incident, new product category or regulatory action: the deal enters `UNDER_REVIEW`; service continues unless the RE suspends.
- Findings carry owners and due dates; overdue findings raise `ComplianceIssueRaised` (U18).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| DD item validity and refresh | Item type | 12 months; refresh on material change | Regulatory floor (OUT para 38): may shorten, never lengthen beyond 12 months |
| Expiry alert lead time | Platform | 30 days | Commercial |
| Pilot caps and duration | Deal | 90 days; caps set per deal | Commercial; caps enforced server-side |
| Pilot exit thresholds | Deal | As listed under Pilot | Tighten only |
| Idle-deal reminder and withdrawal proposal | Platform | 90 and 180 days | Commercial |
| Counter-party exception approver | Platform | Udofin compliance head | Fixed role |
| RE approver roles and authority references | Deal | From the RE's outsourcing policy (OUT para 20(ii)) | RE-defined; mandatory |

### Menu and screens

- **Partners › Deals** (C: partnerships, compliance; D: RE CCO, outsourcing owner): pipeline board by state with ageing chips and filters (lender class, RE layer, state, owner, under review); deal detail with tabs Overview, Gates, Due diligence, Configuration, Pilot, Reviews, Events, Audit trail; **New deal** wizard (lender identity from CoR or registry → class and track → NDA → conflict check → owners); actions **Advance** (runs the gate engine and lists each failing item with a fix link), **Suspend**, **Withdraw**, **Start exit**; approval queue (maker-checker and RE countersign).
- **Partners › Due diligence**: Udofin pack builder (items, evidence upload, expiry), RE questionnaire inbox, counter-party checks, declarations to sign (DSC or Aadhaar eSign), expiry calendar; bulk action **Request refresh**.
- Empty and error states: "No deal yet: start with the lender's CoR"; a blocked transition names the clause or paragraph (for example "CIMS acknowledgement missing for Udofin iOS (CF para 18(2))"). Borrower channels show nothing for the lender before `PILOT`.

### Controls

- UP-C01: transitions only through the gate engine; no state skip.
- UP-C02: DD items alert 30 days before expiry and move the deal to `UNDER_REVIEW` on expiry.
- UP-C03: a bank or co-operative-bank RE cannot pass `DUE_DILIGENCE` while its rule pack is `unmapped` [VERIFY: bank texts].
- UP-C04: published declarations and DD packs are immutable; corrections create a new version.

### Acceptance tests

- A deal cannot move from `TECHNICAL_CERTIFICATION` to `PILOT` without a CIMS acknowledgement file, a website disclosure snapshot and a store-listing snapshot; each missing item is named in the error.
- A deal in `PROPOSED` can be `WITHDRAWN`; a deal in `PILOT` cannot be withdrawn, only terminated through UP5.
- An expired VAPT summary moves an `ACTIVE` deal to `UNDER_REVIEW` without stopping borrower journeys.
- The clause-matrix check fails `LEGAL` exit when OUT para 34(iv) (subcontractor consent) is not marked present.
- An RE user from deal A cannot see deal B's DD pack, review findings or approvals (RLS test).
- Pilot cap of N applications: application N+1 is refused with an honest "not available" status and the RE is notified.
- Each state change publishes exactly one event with the correct `mode` attribute; replay is idempotent; resuming a deal suspended during `PILOT` publishes `mode = PILOT` and `resumed = true`.
- A `NEW_SOURCING_PAUSED` suspension publishes `LenderDealSuspended` with scope `NEW_BUSINESS`; a `FULL` suspension publishes scope `ALL`.

## UP2. Per-deal configurator

### Purpose and scope

A single, versioned `deal_config` object per deal captures everything negotiated with the lender, validated against the guard-rails in Part 3.4 and the RE's own policies. It is the only place where per-lender variation lives; code never branches on a lender's identity.

### Configuration sections

| Section | What is configured | Owner and approval | Guard-rails (cannot be overridden) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Commercials | Sourcing, platform, servicing, recovery (only with a recovery-agent contract), DLG and module licence fees (Part 7A, Part 7G); GST, TDS, invoicing and payment terms | Udofin and RE finance; legal-review layer | **Paid by the RE only** (CF para 10(4)); never netted from disbursal or recovery proceeds (CF para 10(5)); any clawback or first-loss term is implicit DLG within the 5% cap (CF para 24; U14); held in the isolated `deal_commercials` schema with no read grant to matching, ranking, routing, offer, AI or marketing services |
| 2. Products and scope | Products (links to `product_offer_version`), channels (Android, iOS, web, assisted), states and pin-code exclusions, borrower segments the RE serves, product-level store-policy gates | RE product owner; Udofin product | Store-policy gate applies per channel (no loan repayable in full in 60 days or less in either store app; no APR above 36% in the iOS app; Part 4.6); unmatched-lender disclosure unaffected by scope (CF para 7(1)) |
| 3. Credit-policy hooks and BRE parameters | Pre-qualification rules and BRE parameters **supplied by the RE**, hosted as RE-owned GoRules decision models; CIC preference and fallback order (CIR para 20); new-to-credit acceptance (CIR para 38(5)); AA usage; microfinance household-income questionnaire fields (CF para 52) | RE credit, approved by the RE's authorised user; Udofin validates syntax only | Udofin cannot author or edit RE rules (OUT para 15); no DLG, fee or conversion input to any rule (CF para 20(2); Part 4.4); every evaluation logs the rule version |
| 4. KFS and document templates | KFS template version and languages (RBC para 29(1)), Annex I Part 2 items (GRO contacts, co-lending block, cooling-off, LSP recovery role), sanction letter, agreement with KFS summary box (RBC para 29(6)), enclosure list (RBC para 14), loan card for microfinance (RBC paras 78–79) | RE legal | KFS must be RE-issued; Udofin never re-renders (CF para 9(3)); missing Annex I Part 2 items block display |
| 5. Data-sharing scope | Field-level allow-list by stage (eligibility, application, servicing, collections), minimal data set Udofin may keep (CF para 14(1)), retention per data class, purge-on-acknowledgement rules, RE-controlled keys option (OUT para 97(vii)), offshore processing (default: none; OUT para 53) | RE DPO or CISO; Udofin DPO | No field leaves without a live consent reference (CF para 13(4)); India-only storage (CF para 14(4)); no device data, contacts or call logs exist to share (CF para 13(1)) |
| 6. SLAs | Uptime, API latency, TAT per journey step, incident notice (target 2 hours from Udofin's detection; OUT para 61), complaint forwarding (target 1 hour; U15), reconciliation (T+1), export-pack turnaround (UP3), support hours | Both | SLA breaches feed UP3 pack P2 and the RE's annual review (OUT para 38) |
| 7. Branding and co-branding | RE name, logo and legal name on every offer, KFS, payment and document screen; co-branded pages and campaigns outside the offer view; white-label (Part 3.1 model 4) | RE marketing and Udofin legal | RE named as lender everywhere (Part 4.1); equal visual weight in the offer view (U23); no "RBI approved" claims (CF para 18(6)); no implied group guarantee (OUT para 46); no co-branded content inside the offer view (CF para 7(4)) |
| 8. Recovery-agent options | None; reminders only; tele-calling; field; cash (overdue loans only); Part 7A capabilities UR1–UR6 attached per product; rule pack A or B by date | RE recovery head; requires a separate `recovery_agent_contract` | Never inferred from DLG (Part 4.4); CF para 9(6) notice before contact; RBC paras 94–100 and Third Amendment paras 100A–100AB from 1 Jan 2027 [VERIFY official text] |
| 9. DLG options | None; cash with the RE; FD with an SCB under lien; bank guarantee (CF para 23); set definition, cap, term, invocation timeline, disclosure clause | RE risk; Udofin finance; statutory-auditor declaration | Cap 5% of disbursed amount of the set (CF para 24); no reinstatement (CF para 25(4)); term not shorter than the longest loan tenor (CF para 27(2)); invisible to matching and agents |
| 10. Grievance contacts and host | RE GRO, Udofin nodal officer, PNO (if covered), IO applicability, CIC nodal officer, recovery-grievance mechanism, RB-IOS coverage flag and CEPC regional office, languages for RB-IOS salient features; grievance-host switch (Part 2) | RE GRO and Udofin GRO | Contacts present before PILOT (CF para 12(2)); display rules in UB3 |
| 11. DLA listing | Which Udofin DLAs (Android, iOS, web, white-label) carry this RE; CIMS Annex-I lines per DLA per platform; RE website disclosure URL; store description partner list | RE CCO and Udofin compliance | One CIMS line per DLA per platform (CF para 18, Annex-I footnotes); change notices to the RE on every add, rename or withdrawal (CF para 18(2)) |
| 12. Modules and add-ons | Part 7A pack, 7E member and group lending, 7F product plug-ins (only where the RE holds the licence) | RE | Wellness add-ons (Part 7D) are **never** a deal item: an RE cannot buy, sponsor, see or configure them |

### Neutrality firewall (CF para 7(4))

- **No ranking or placement field exists in `deal_config`.** The schema validator rejects keys such as priority, boost, featured, sponsored, default_selected, rank_weight or badge.
- Matching inputs remain only the borrower's request, the RE's published eligibility rules and the RE's `EligibilityCheck` response (Part 4.6). The ranking service runs under a database role with no grant on `deal_commercials`, `dlg_*` or `deal_config.commercials`; a CI test proves the grant does not exist.
- A U19 conduct test compares rank-selection shares and display order before and after any commercial change; a statistically significant shift with no change in APR inputs raises `ComplianceIssueRaised` [REC].
- Commercial differences are disclosed to the RE only, never to borrowers as a ranking cue.

### Versioning and RE countersign

`deal_config_version`: `DRAFT → VALIDATED → UDOFIN_APPROVED → SENT_TO_RE → RE_COUNTERSIGNED → SCHEDULED → EFFECTIVE → SUPERSEDED`, with `REJECTED_BY_RE` (back to a new `DRAFT` copy), `WITHDRAWN` (before `RE_COUNTERSIGNED`) and `EXPIRED` (not countersigned within 15 business days [REC]).

| Step | Owner | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| DRAFT → VALIDATED | Udofin maker | Guard-rail validator passes (UP-C05); diff against the current `EFFECTIVE` version and impact analysis generated (products, journeys and in-flight applications affected; synthetic-borrower offer-order check under the neutrality firewall) |
| VALIDATED → UDOFIN_APPROVED | Udofin checker; Udofin legal for sections 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 (Part 3.4) | Checker differs from maker; legal sign-off reference stored |
| UDOFIN_APPROVED → SENT_TO_RE → RE_COUNTERSIGNED | RE authorised approver | Read through `GET /v1/deals/{id}/config-versions/{version}` (no commercials) or the lender portal; countersign through `POST /v1/deals/{id}/approvals` with name, role, authority reference and decision; the countersigned PDF summary is sealed with Udofin's document-signing key and both approvals are hashed into the version (`re_change_approval`); commercials are countersigned by the RE's finance user in the separate `deal_commercials` flow |
| RE_COUNTERSIGNED → SCHEDULED → EFFECTIVE | System | Effective at the stated time (never back-dated); a version may be scheduled up to 90 days ahead; two versions cannot share an effective time |
| Rollback | Udofin maker plus RE countersign | A rollback is a new version copying an earlier one; no version is ever edited or deleted |

- **In-flight rule:** an application keeps the version in force at submission; a KFS accepted within validity binds the RE (RBC para 29(2) Explanation) and no later version changes it.
- **Emergency change** by the RE (product suspension, template withdrawal: OUT paras 17, 43) applies at once as an `EFFECTIVE` version marked `EMERGENCY`, with Udofin's second approval within 1 business day [REC]; an emergency change can only narrow scope, never widen it.
- Notifications: the RE approver receives a task with a 5-business-day reminder; Udofin owners see versions awaiting countersign on the deal page.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Countersign window before `EXPIRED` | Platform | 15 business days | Commercial |
| Sections needing Udofin legal sign-off | Platform | 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 | Regulatory floor (may add, never remove) |
| Maximum schedule-ahead period | Platform | 90 days | Commercial |
| Ranking or placement keys | Schema | None exist | Regulatory floor (CF para 7(4)); cannot be enabled |
| Borrower-paid Udofin fee lines | Schema | None exist | Regulatory floor (CF para 10(4)) |
| DLG cap | Deal | ≤ 5% | Regulatory ceiling (CF para 24) |

### Menu and screens

- **Partners › Configuration** (C: partnerships, legal, finance for commercials; D: RE product, credit, legal, finance): version list with state chips and effective dates; editor by the twelve sections with inline validation and explain-why messages citing the guard-rail; diff viewer (side by side, changed sections highlighted); impact panel; synthetic-borrower simulation; approval and countersign queue; actions **Validate**, **Submit for approval**, **Send to RE**, **Countersign** (D), **Reject with reasons** (D), **Schedule**, **Roll back**; export of any version as JSON plus PDF summary. Borrowers see only the effects.

### Controls

- UP-C05: guard-rail validator runs on every save; a failing version cannot be submitted.
- UP-C06: `deal_commercials` is encrypted with a separate key and readable only by Udofin finance and the RE's own finance users.
- UP-C07: any borrower-facing Udofin fee line in any section fails validation (CF para 10(4)).
- UP-C08: configuration export (JSON plus PDF summary) is attached to the RE's annual review pack.

### Acceptance tests

- Saving a configuration with a `priority` or `featured` key fails schema validation.
- The ranking service's database role receives "permission denied" on `deal_commercials` (CI test).
- Changing RE A's sourcing fee from 1% to 3% leaves the offer order for an identical synthetic borrower unchanged.
- An application submitted under version 4 still uses version 4 rules and templates after version 5 becomes effective.
- Version 5 cannot become `EFFECTIVE` without an RE countersign recorded through the approvals API or the lender portal; a version not countersigned within the window moves to `EXPIRED`; a rollback creates version 6 and leaves versions 4 and 5 unchanged.
- An emergency change that widens scope (adds a product, state or channel) is rejected.
- A KFS template lacking the Annex I Part 2 GRO item blocks publication of the product.
- A recovery option of "field" cannot be enabled without an active `recovery_agent_contract` covering the territory.
- A DLG option with a 6% cap fails validation; a clawback clause is counted inside the 5% cap.
- A co-branded campaign cannot be targeted into the offer-view slot.

## UP3. RE audit, inspection and CIMS export packs

### Purpose and scope

Give each RE, its auditors and, on the RE's request, RBI-authorised persons complete, verifiable evidence of what Udofin did for that RE, generated on demand or on schedule, self-describing, hashed and readable without Udofin (export-archive standard, Integration Specification v1.1; RA3). Interactive read-only access is RA2.

### Pack catalogue

| Pack | Contents | Source requirement | Default cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 CIMS DLA pack | Annex-I extract per DLA per platform in column order (S. No., DLA name, owner, available on, link, GRO name, email, telephone, mobile, RE website); change log; CCO evidence for each para 18(4) point (link to the RE website, LSP nodal officer displayed, paras 13–14 compliance, para 9(4) consistency) | CF para 18(1)–(4), Annex-I | On every DLA change and quarterly |
| P2 Outsourcing oversight pack | Central-record feed (activity, materiality as assessed by the RE, start date, value, subcontractors); SLA performance; incident log with detection and notification times; BCP and DR test evidence; sub-processor list with RE consents; clause-matrix status; DD pack version; declarations | OUT paras 34, 36, 38, 40, 61, 74(iii), 82 | Half-yearly and annual |
| P3 Conduct pack | Offer-display logs (offer set, matched and unmatched lenders, ranking metric and matching mechanism versions, change log); dark-pattern audit results; consent ledger extract; KFS evidence (proposal number, version hash, view, explanation acknowledgement, acceptance time, validity); cooling-off exits; template and language exceptions; recovery-agent notices and contact evaluations (if UR4 is attached) | CF paras 7, 9(6), 11, 13; RBC paras 10, 29, 100; CCPA-DP s.2(e) | Monthly; FPC conduct pack per RBC para 8 |
| P4 Grievance MIS | Complaint register for the RE's borrowers handled or received by Udofin: reference, channel, category (including FS 21(10) grounds), received at Udofin, forwarded to RE, RE acknowledgement, clocks, IO escalation status, final reply, borrower-declared RB-IOS or other external referral, reopen and rating; credit-information complaints with the 21-day and 30-day clocks and compensation details captured (CIR para 35) | CF para 12; OUT paras 56–57; RBC paras 7(2), 8, 92; CIR paras 34–35 | Monthly and on request |
| P5 DLG pack | Arrangements, instruments, set ledgers, cover snapshots, invocations, recovery sharing, monthly website disclosures with publication timestamps, auditor-certified provider declarations | CF paras 20(3), 22–28 | Monthly and at each renewal |
| P6 Data-protection pack | Data inventory for this RE (fields captured, processed, stored; locations); retention schedule and purge certificates; data-principal requests and outcomes; consent withdrawals; breaches and notifications | CF paras 13–14; OUT paras 74(vi)–(viii), 87; DPDP | Quarterly |
| P7 Statutory and internal auditor pack | Selected records for the RE's auditors with sampling support (population counts, random seed, sample IDs), access log of the auditor's use | OUT paras 34(vii), 37, 81 | On request |
| P8 RBI inspection pack | Scope stated in the RE's request (records, logs, configurations, policies), produced under RE maker-checker; delivered to the RE or, if the RE directs, to the RBI team through RA2 | OUT paras 16, 34(viii)–(ix), 81 | On request; target 2 business days [REC] |
| P9 AI pack | AI inventory, model and prompt versions, disclosure texts, human-override statistics, sampled redacted logs | [GUID] FREE-AI report | Quarterly where the RE requires it |
| P10 Reconciliation pack | Daily reconciliation results, break ageing, fee invoices against RE confirmations | OUT paras 12(2)(ii), 39 | Monthly |

### Manifest and integrity

Every pack follows the archive standard (Integration Specification 12.1) with folder profile `re_audit_pack_v1`: the mandatory `00 Start Here/` folder (README as PDF, DOCX and TXT covering purpose, period, scope, filters, generation time in IST, schema versions, masking level and hash-verification steps; `export-manifest.csv`, `manifest.json` and the detached `manifest.json.jws`; data dictionary; code tables; JSON Schemas; the open-source verifier); each dataset as `[dataset].csv`, `[dataset].xlsx` and `[dataset].schema.json`; documents byte-identical with their original hashes (narrative renditions as PDF/A-2b); logs as JSON Lines; and `reconciliation.xlsx` tying control totals to the RE's own figures where supplied. `manifest.json` adds the pack ID, RE, deal, requester, approver, record counts and control totals per file, SHA-256 per file, the pack-level SHA-256 over the sorted file list, the signing key ID and the previous pack in the series.

### Delivery and protection

- Channels: lender-portal download (signed URL valid ≤ 15 minutes), SFTP with checksum acknowledgement (Part 5.3) or the RE's storage target (RA3).
- Masking: P1, P2, P5 and P10 carry no borrower PII; P3, P4 and P6 mask identifiers by default and unmask only on an RE maker-checker request; P8 follows the RE's request.
- Every generation and download is logged; an auditor's or supervisor's download is `ExternalAccessUsed` (RA2). Packs are retained for the deal retention period and are reproducible from the same snapshot with identical hashes.

### States

`re_export_pack`: `REQUESTED → APPROVED (maker-checker where required) → GENERATING → GENERATED → DELIVERED → ACKNOWLEDGED`, with `FAILED` (control-total mismatch, snapshot unavailable or signing failure; automatic retry up to 3 times on the same snapshot, then the failure queue) and `EXPIRED` (download window lapsed; pack retained and re-deliverable). `ExportRequested` on REQUESTED; `ExportCompleted` when the recipient confirms the pack hash or the RE storage target confirms the write (ACKNOWLEDGED), as Integration Specification 6.26 requires. A pack `DELIVERED` but not acknowledged within 5 business days raises a reminder to the RE requester.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pack schedules (P1–P10) | RE | Cadences in the catalogue | RE may add runs; P1 on every DLA change is fixed (CF para 18(2)) |
| Masking level | Pack | P1, P2, P5, P10 no PII; P3, P4, P6 masked | Unmasking needs RE maker-checker |
| Download link validity | Platform | 15 minutes | Security floor (may shorten) |
| Delivery channel | RE | Lender-portal download | RE choice: portal, SFTP or RE storage (RA3) |
| P8 target turnaround | Platform | 2 business days | Commercial [REC] |
| External-access grant for auditors or supervisors (RA2) | Grant | 30 days | Hard maximum 90 days; renewal needs fresh RE approval |

### Menu and screens

- **Partners › Exports** (D: RE compliance, audit, finance; C: operations): pack catalogue with last run and next run; **Request pack** wizard (pack → period → scope and filters → masking → approver → channel); history with state, hashes and **Verify** (runs the verifier on an uploaded copy); schedules; failure queue (C only) with **Retry on same snapshot**. No borrower access.

### Controls

- UP-C09: a pack covers one RE only; a cross-RE row aborts generation and raises a security incident (OUT paras 26–27).
- UP-C10: P8 requires an RE approver and records the supervisory reference supplied by the RE.
- UP-C11: generation runs on a read replica snapshot with the snapshot timestamp in the manifest.
- UP-C12: CIMS pack regeneration and notice to the RE within 1 business day of any DLA change (CF para 18(2)) [REC].

### Acceptance tests

- Hash verification of every file in a generated pack matches `manifest.json`; altering one byte fails verification with the tool supplied in the README.
- A P4 pack's complaint count equals the U15 register count for the same RE and period.
- A P3 pack for RE A contains no offer card from RE B except as an anonymised "other lender" entry in the offer-set context (lender names visible only where the borrower saw them).
- An unmasked P4 request without RE approval is refused.
- A new iOS DLA launch regenerates P1 with a new Annex-I line and notifies the RE.
- Regenerating a pack for a closed period from the same snapshot yields identical hashes.
