## UP4. Non-RE lender track (credit co-operative societies)

### Purpose and scope

Serve credit co-operative societies registered under a State co-operative Act or the MSCS Act 2002 (as amended 2023) as partner lenders to **their own members**, through a ring-fenced track with RE-equivalent conduct imposed by contract. Member journeys are MG1 (Part 7E); this section governs eligibility, deal terms and the hard boundaries.

### Legal position

| Point | Position | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory status | A credit co-operative society is not an RBI RE; co-operative banks are. CF, RBC, OUT and CIR do not bind the society or reach Udofin through it | [REG] RBI press release 22 Nov 2021; TDCR para 97 [INTERP] |
| "Bank" in the name | Non-bank societies may not use "bank", "banker" or "banking" (from 29 Sep 2020) | [LAW] BR Act s.7 read with s.56, as amended by the BR (Amendment) Act 2020; [REG] RBI press release 22 Nov 2021 |
| Deposits | Only from members; under the MSCS Act only from **voting** members; deposits from nominal or associate members are unlicensed banking and carry no DICGC cover | [LAW] MSCS s.67 Explanation; SCS (e.g. MH s.144-5A); [REG] RBI press release 22 Nov 2021; BUDS Act First Schedule items 4(i), 8 |
| Co-lending, direct assignment, split loans with NBFCs | Not permitted: NBFC co-lending is only with scheduled commercial banks, AIFIs and other NBFCs (TDCR para 97); a credit society is not a "lender" for loan transfers at all, and even co-operative banks may transfer only stressed loans (TDCR para 12(4) proviso) | [REG] TDCR paras 97, 12(4) |
| Recovery and disputes | Statutory forums: MSCS s.84 arbitration by the Central Registrar's arbitrator [VERIFY s.84, s.94]; MH s.91 co-operative court and s.101 recovery certificate where notified [VERIFY notification]; no private arbitration for member disputes | [LAW] MSCS; SCS |
| Member grievances | Society GRO; for MSCS, the Co-operative Ombudsman (s.85A) [VERIFY text]; State Registrar; consumer commission | [LAW] MSCS s.85A; SCS |
| Coercive-recovery laws | TN Act 40 of 2025 s.20 applies to societies [VERIFY commencement]; KA Act 15 of 2025 exempts KCS and Souharda societies (s.1(3)); its platform limb is open [VERIFY] | [LAW] |
| Data protection | The society is Data Fiduciary for member lending data; Udofin is its Data Processor; Udofin is Fiduciary for its own platform account | [LAW] DPDP ss.2(i), 8; [INTERP] |
| Bureau | Only if the society is itself a CIC member [VERIFY CICRA eligibility]; never through an RE's or Udofin's access | [LAW] CICRA; [REG] CIR para 6 for REs |

### Eligibility gate (all must pass)

1. Registration certificate verified with the State Registrar or CRCS portal; registered bye-laws on file; area of operation covers the borrower's location.
2. Name free of "bank", "banker" and "banking" (hard block, string and transliteration check).
3. Last three statutory audit reports; in Maharashtra, audit class A or B in each of the last two years [REC; VERIFY mark bands]; no material unrectified objections.
4. Returns filed (MSCS s.120 annual return; CRCS quarterly returns; State equivalents) [VERIFY section numbers].
5. Prudential status: CRCS norms of 22 Jan 2024 for credit MSCS (CRAR 9% or 12% by size, glide to 2028-29; cash 2% of deposits; leverage 10 times) [VERIFY order text]; Maharashtra SLR 25% [VERIFY].
6. Certificate (State Registrar or CRCS) or statutory auditor's confirmation that **no deposits are held from non-voting, nominal or associate members** [REC, modelled on the CRCS branch-expansion condition, Jul 2025].
7. No adverse Registrar, Co-operative Ombudsman or court orders in the last 3 years; not on any regulator or State caution list.
8. Grievance mechanism, KYC process and data-protection measures documented.
9. Counsel opinion on: the State Act; dispute and recovery forum; money-lending-law exemption (e.g. MH Money-Lending Act s.2(13)(e)); State coercive-recovery law; whether any State digital-lending-platform registration applies to Udofin.
10. Signed agreement with RE-equivalent conduct schedule and DPDP processing terms.

### Ring-fencing rules

- **Member-only.** A loan journey for the society opens only after member verification against the society's register through `GET /v1/societies/{id}/members/{ref}` (served by Finbyx IP2 or the society's certified system; Integration Spec 6.24), `MemberAdmitted` for members admitted through Udofin, or the society's verification queue in the lender portal where it has no API. Non-members see only "apply for membership"; share money is paid to the society's own account. Borrowing rights of nominal or associate members follow the bye-law flag `can_borrow`.
- **No deposits through Udofin.** No deposit product, listing, rate display, solicitation, collection or marketing. A member's own existing deposit balance may be shown read-only only if the society opts in and counsel confirms; default off. Udofin never takes a deposit instruction.
- **Separate presentation.** Society loans appear in a separate "Your society" section, never inside the CF para 7 multi-lender offer view, with the lender card: society name, Act, Registrar and registration number, and the statements "This society is not regulated by the Reserve Bank of India" and "Deposits with co-operative societies are not insured by DICGC".
- **Data separation.** No RE sees society data, and no society sees RE data, without the borrower's explicit consent naming the recipient; separate tenant class `lender_class = NON_RE_COOP` (events carry `lender_type = NON_RE_SOCIETY`, Integration Spec 6.24) with its own RLS policies.
- **No co-lending or loan sale with NBFCs** (TDCR paras 97, 12(4)): the configurator rejects co-lending, DA, participation or split routing between a society and an RE. Alternatives for counsel review only (none built without a legal opinion): an RE term loan to the society for on-lending within its limits (MSCS s.67); the society as an RE's sourcing agent where bye-laws permit, with the RE disclosed as lender; independent parallel loans, each lender assessing aggregate affordability.
- **Channel gate.** App-store lending policies may require the lender to be RBI-regulated [VERIFY: Google Play India personal-loan policy and App Store guidelines]. Until confirmed, society loans are offered on the web/PWA and assisted channel (U22) only.

### RE-equivalent conduct by contract

| Area | Adopted standard | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Disclosure | KFS-equivalent in the RBC Annex I format, with APR, in the member's language, with acknowledgement | RBC para 29 adopted [REC] |
| Cooling-off | At least 1 day | CF para 11 adopted [REC] |
| Money flow | Disbursal to the member's account; repayment to the society's account; no pool account; no Udofin control | CF para 10 adopted [REC] |
| Fees | Udofin fees paid by the society only; nothing charged to members by Udofin | CF para 10(4) adopted |
| Data and device | Same permission policy; India-only storage | CF paras 13–14; DPDP |
| Recovery | Contact windows, no harassment, agent particulars before contact, recording; State coercion overlays | RBC rule pack A or B adopted; TN Act 40/2025 |
| Microfinance-type loans | Household-income test and 50% obligation cap for collateral-free loans to low-income households | CF paras 51–57 adopted [REC] |
| Grievance | Society GRO → Co-operative Ombudsman (MSCS) or Registrar (State) → consumer commission; Udofin nodal officer for platform issues; RBI CMS is **not** shown as available | UB3 non-RE route |
| Aadhaar | Offline verification or DigiLocker only; no Aadhaar number stored | Aadhaar Act s.29; societies are not s.11A-notified [VERIFY] |
| Telecom | DLT-registered headers and numbers only; 1600 series not assumed [VERIFY] | TRAI TCCCPR |

### Deal and export differences from the RE track

- UP1 states apply, but the `PILOT` gate replaces CIMS and RBI website evidence with: registration verification, eligibility checks above, society website or notice-board disclosure of Udofin's role [REC], and the counsel opinion.
- UP3 packs are produced for the society, its statutory auditor and the Registrar on the society's request; CIMS, RBI inspection and RB-IOS items are replaced by Registrar-return support and co-operative-audit samples.
- `LenderDeal*` events carry `lender_type = NON_RE_SOCIETY` (Integration Spec 6.28) for a tenant of class `lender_class = NON_RE_COOP`; they go to the society's certified system or are shown in the lender portal only (OUT para 36 does not bind a society).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channels for society loans | Society | Web/PWA and assisted only | Fixed until app-store policy for non-RE lenders is confirmed (`coop_channel_gate`) |
| Deposit features | Tenant class | None exist | Hard block; not configurable |
| Read-only display of a member's own deposit balance | Society | Off | Society opt-in plus counsel confirmation |
| Rule pack | Society | MSCS or the State pack | Pack per (Act, State, effective date) |
| Re-verification of eligibility items 3–7 | Society | Annual | Tighten only |
| Society reply target for grievances | Society | 30 days | Contract floor [REC] |

### Menu and screens

- **Partners › Deals** with lender class "Credit society" (C): eligibility checklist (items 1–10 with evidence and validity), name-check result, rule-pack selection, counsel-opinion upload; bulk **Re-verify** at the annual date.
- **Partners › Members** (D, society staff): verification queue (approve or reject a member lookup where the society has no API), membership applications with the deemed-refusal countdown, members' loan applications with committee-approval references.
- Borrower web: "Your society" (MG1); empty state for a non-member: "Apply for membership"; error for a defaulter: "Please contact your society".

### Controls

- UP-C13: name check blocks "bank", "banker", "banking" and transliterations.
- UP-C14: no deposit-related API, screen or template exists for a `NON_RE_COOP` tenant (route-level test).
- UP-C15: society offers never enter the CF para 7 offer set.
- UP-C16: co-lending, DA and participation flags are rejected for any deal pairing a society with an RE.
- UP-C17: annual re-verification of eligibility items 3–7; failure suspends new sourcing (UP5).

### Acceptance tests

- Onboarding "XYZ Urban Co-operative Bank" as a credit society is rejected at the name check (it would need the RE track as a UCB).
- A non-member opening the society's loan journey is routed to membership application only.
- No deposit product can be published for a society tenant; the API returns 403.
- A member's offer from the society does not appear in the multi-lender offer view and shows the not-RBI-regulated and no-DICGC statements.
- The grievance screen for a society loan shows the society GRO and Registrar or Co-operative Ombudsman route and does not show the RBI CMS link.
- A configuration attempting co-lending between a society and an NBFC fails validation with the TDCR reference.
- On the Android build, the society section is hidden while the store-policy flag is unconfirmed.

## UP5. Deal suspension, exit and portability

### Purpose and scope

Suspend or end a deal in a controlled way that protects borrowers first, preserves records, honours the RE's regulatory duties and lets the RE move to another provider or in-house (OUT paras 40–44, 84–89; CF para 18(2)).

### Triggers and suspension types

| Trigger | Initiator | Default suspension type |
|---|---|---|
| RE instruction (OUT para 17 control) | RE | As instructed |
| Material breach of the agreement or SLA | Either party | New sourcing paused |
| RBI action against the RE (CoR cancellation, business restriction) or against Udofin | Either | Full suspension of new sourcing; servicing per RBI instruction |
| Security incident affecting the RE's data | Either | Connector paused; servicing view read-only |
| Non-RE eligibility failure (UP4) | Udofin | New sourcing paused |
| Agreement expiry or termination notice | Either | Wind-down plan |

Suspension types: `NEW_SOURCING_PAUSED` (no new applications; existing journeys continue to KFS expiry; event scope `NEW_BUSINESS`), `RECOVERY_PAUSED` (Part 7A UR4 stops; reminders continue if the RE allows), `CONNECTOR_PAUSED` (no data exchange; borrower sees honest status; queued messages replayed in order on resumption), `FULL` (all of the above; servicing view read-only); the last three publish event scope `ALL`. A suspension never blocks repayments to the RE's accounts, open grievances, document downloads or cooling-off exits.

### Borrower continuity rules (exit or suspension)

| Borrower position | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Browsing or not yet applied | The RE disappears from new matching; the unmatched-lender list does not name an exited RE [INTERP: an exited lender is no longer a lender with an agreement] |
| Application submitted, no decision | The RE decides or returns it within the agreed wind-down period; the borrower is told the RE's name and status; on return, the borrower may apply elsewhere with fresh consent |
| KFS issued, not accepted | Offer withdrawn at the earlier of KFS validity expiry or the exit date, with notice |
| KFS accepted, not disbursed | The RE is bound by the accepted KFS within validity (RBC para 29(2) Explanation); the RE completes or formally cancels with reasons; Udofin keeps the journey open until then |
| Active loan | Repayments continue to the RE's accounts and mandates in the RE's favour are unaffected; the Udofin servicing view continues for the transition period or becomes read-only with "contact [RE name]" details; payment links and UPI intents are re-pointed only on the RE's instruction |
| Cooling-off running | The exit option stays available to the end of the period |
| Open grievance | Continues to be forwarded and tracked to closure; UB3 clocks and escalation information unchanged |
| Recovery allocation | Handed back to the RE (`CollectionDeallocated`); borrower notified by the RE of the change (RBC para 95; paras 100M–100N from 1 Jan 2027 [VERIFY]) |
| Documents and data | The borrower keeps download access (UB1) for at least 90 days after the servicing view closes [REC], with notice before access ends; afterwards a "request from [RE name]" route |

### RE duties Udofin supports

- **Publicity** is the RE's (OUT paras 44, 89); Udofin sends the RE-approved borrower notice on instruction and records delivery.
- **CIMS and websites:** the RE updates its CIMS lines (CF para 18(2)) and disclosure page (CF para 9(4)) from Udofin's final P1 pack with cessation dates; Udofin removes the RE from store descriptions and its lender list on the exit date.
- **DLG** survives exit: cover, invocation and monthly disclosure continue for the set to the agreed term, not shorter than the longest tenor (CF paras 27(2), 28).

### Data return and destruction

1. **Freeze:** from exit notice, no erasure, purge or alteration of the RE's data except as the RE or regulator directs (OUT para 87); scheduled purges for this RE are suspended and logged.
2. **Return:** full export in the archive standard (Integration Specification v1.1; RA3): borrowers and consents, applications and journeys, KYC evidence references, documents and hashes, communications, grievance records, recordings (if UR4), DLG ledgers, configuration versions and audit trail, with manifest and hashes (OUT para 42; Part 10.8 item 21).
3. **Transition:** full cooperation with the RE and any incoming provider (OUT para 88), with mapping notes and a dry-run import [REC]; the RE acknowledges receipt and integrity by hash.
4. **Destruction:** after acknowledgement and any retention Udofin must keep (its own books, consent evidence, legal holds), Udofin destroys the RE's data and issues a certificate of scope, method and, where required, independent assurance (OUT paras 42, 87, 97(xvi)). Udofin's own records follow its own schedule.

### Portability for the RE

- Annual exit dry-run per active RE: generate the full export on a synthetic copy, verify hashes and import into a reference reader; results go into the P2 pack (Part 10.8 item 21; CYB 102 cited in Part 8A.16.2).
- Export formats are documented and stable; no proprietary encoding.

### States

`deal_exit`: `NOTICE_RECEIVED → PLAN_DRAFTED → PLAN_APPROVED (both parties) → WIND_DOWN → DATA_RETURNED → RE_ACKNOWLEDGED → DESTROYED → CLOSED`, with `DISPUTED` (exit terms contested; freeze continues). The deal itself moves `ACTIVE or SUSPENDED → TERMINATING` at PLAN_APPROVED and `TERMINATED` at CLOSED (`LenderDealTerminated`).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wind-down period for undecided applications | Deal | 15 business days [REC] | Commercial; agreed in the exit plan |
| Borrower download access after the servicing view closes | Platform | 90 days, with notice 15 days before it ends | Floor (may lengthen) [REC] |
| Freeze on purge from exit notice | Deal | On | Regulatory floor (OUT para 87); cannot be switched off |
| Exit dry-run | RE | Annual | Tighten only |
| Destruction assurance | Deal | Udofin certificate; independent assurance where the RE requires (OUT para 97(xvi)) | RE choice |

### Menu and screens

- **Partners › Exit** (C: partnerships, DPO, engineering; D: RE CCO and CTO): exit list by state; exit detail with the borrower-position table (counts and treatment, UP-C19), notice templates for RE approval, export progress with hashes, acknowledgement status, destruction certificate; actions **Suspend** (choose type and scope), **Lift suspension**, **Approve plan** (both parties), **Mark disputed**, **Issue destruction certificate**. Borrower channels: RE-approved notices, read-only servicing view, download prompts with the end date.

### Controls

- UP-C18: purge jobs check a per-RE freeze flag before running; a purge attempt during transition fails and alerts.
- UP-C19: the exit plan cannot be approved without counts and treatment for every borrower position in the table above.
- UP-C20: an exited RE never appears in new offer sets or unmatched-lender lists after the exit date.
- UP-C21: DLG ledgers stay active after `TERMINATED` until the DLG term ends.

### Acceptance tests

- With a freeze active, a scheduled retention purge of the RE's applications is blocked and logged.
- A borrower with a KFS accepted the day before exit still reaches disbursal status from the RE, or sees the RE's cancellation reason.
- A borrower in the cooling-off period on the exit date can still exit through the RE.
- Open grievances for the exited RE continue to show live clocks and RB-IOS information until closed.
- The full export imports into the reference reader with zero hash mismatches; the destruction certificate lists every store, including backups, with dates.
- After `TERMINATED`, the RE's monthly DLG disclosure is still generated for open sets.

# PART 7C — BORROWER DOWNLOADS, TAX DOCUMENTS AND GRIEVANCE ESCALATION

**Purpose.** Give every borrower one dependable place to find, download and export their documents and data; to obtain the lender-issued tax documents they need under the Income-tax Act, 2025; and to raise, track and escalate a complaint through the correct chain, from the help centre to the RE's Internal Ombudsman and the RBI Ombudsman, with the parallel routes for credit information, insurance, personal data, subscriptions and co-operative societies shown accurately.

**Extends, does not replace.** U4 (consent, privacy, data-principal requests), U9 (DMS and "My documents"), U12 (servicing requests, NOC, document-release tracking), U15 (grievance redressal), U25 (borrower dashboard and downloads), Part 7A UR2 (ADR access) and UR3 (notices). **U15 is superseded by UB3 and UB4 for chain, timers, display and borrower capabilities; where they differ, this Part prevails.** U25 "Downloads" becomes a pointer to UB1. Billing for any Udofin subscription is Part 7G; the wellness add-ons are Part 7D.

**Applicability.** Every borrower, co-borrower and guarantor on any Udofin channel, for loans from any partner RE (NBFC of any layer, HFC, NBFC-MFI, bank) and from non-RE lenders on the UP4 track (credit co-operative societies), plus Udofin's own non-loan relationships (platform account, wellness subscriptions). Route selection depends on the lender's profile: RB-IOS 2026 coverage, Internal Ombudsman applicability, HFC status and lender class (UB3).

**Codes used.** CF, RBC, OUT, CIR, KYC, MFI, FS; `RB-IOS 2026` (Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, notified 16 Jan 2026, effective 1 Jul 2026); `IO 2026` (RBI (NBFCs – Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026, issued 14 Jan 2026); non-RBI: `DPDP` (Act 2023 and Rules 2025), `ITA25` (Income-tax Act, 2025, in force 1 Apr 2026), `ITA61` (Income-tax Act, 1961, for FY 2025-26 documents), `GST`, `CICRA`, `MSCS`, `SCS`, `IRDAI`, `CPA19` (Consumer Protection Act, 2019). Labels: **[LAW]**, **[REG]**, **[INTERP]**, **[REC]**, **[MKT]**; unconfirmed items carry `[VERIFY: …]`. New controls are `UB-Cnn`.

**Data owned by Udofin.** Document catalogue entries and request records, data-access and export jobs, the borrower's business tax profile (as captured, with consent), uploaded Form 131 copies (as relayed), grievance cases handled or received by Udofin with their clocks and tier history, case packs, ratings, help-centre content. **Not owned:** RE-issued documents and certificates (Udofin mirrors or fetches them; the RE's DMS is the source), the RE's grievance decisions, IO reviews and Ombudsman proceedings.

**Events.** Consumes `DocumentShared`, `KFSIssued`, `SanctionLetterIssued`, `NOCIssued`, `LoanClosed`, `InterestCertificateIssued` (Integration Specification v1.1 finance domain; RE → Udofin), `GrievanceUpdated`, `GrievanceEscalated` and `OmbudsmanReferralRecorded` (Ombudsman stages the RE reports; section 6.12). Produces `DataPrincipalRequest`, `GrievanceRaised`, `GrievanceReopened`, `GrievanceRated`, `OmbudsmanReferralRecorded` (borrower-declared external filing) and `DocumentShared` (Form 131 relayed to the RE). Borrower self-service exports publish no cross-product event (section 6.26).

**Borrower navigation (channels A and B; used by Parts 7C–7E).** The mobile app has five bottom tabs; the web app shows the same five items in the header (a side rail on desktop). Labels are short, icon-led and vernacular; the active loan and any open complaint show a badge.

| Tab | Contents | Never contains |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Next due date and amount for each loan, tasks (documents to sign, information requested by an RE, consent renewals), open complaint status, notices; a "Your society" tile for verified society members on web (MG1) | Offers pushed by fee or DLG, advertising inside loan cards (Part 4.6; RV4) |
| Loans | Apply (multi-lender offer view), my applications, my loans (statement, schedule, documents for that loan, cooling-off exit, foreclosure request), "Your society" on web and assisted channels (MG1), group loans (MG2–MG3) | Money tools, insurance or plan upsells |
| Pay | Dues across loans with RE-named payment buttons (UPI intent or QR, mandate status), receipts from the RE, overdue centre (Part 7A UR1) | Any Udofin account or any payment to Udofin |
| Help | Help centre, **Raise a complaint**, my complaints with timeline and clocks, external routes when open (UB3–UB4), "verify this agent" (UR4), call-back request | Retention offers, discouraging wording |
| Account | Profile and contacts, security (devices, passkeys, step-up), **My documents and data** (UB1), **Tax documents** (UB2), consents and privacy, language and accessibility, Plans and billing (Part 7G RV2.3, only while S09 is active), Money tools (Part 7D, only while `addons.wellness` is on), Protect (Part 7F, only after the XP1 licence gate) | Loan offers inside Money tools or Protect |

The Account tab is the "Account" section of Part 7G RV2.3. Money tools and Protect are areas reached from Account (and from a Home tile the user has opted into), never extra tabs inside the loan journey; a loan, offer, KFS, payment, overdue or grievance screen never links into them (FW4; XP2.2).

## UB1. My documents and my data

### Purpose and scope

A single "My documents and data" area, identical on app and web, that lists every document relevant to the borrower, says who issued it and where it is, serves RE documents from the RE, explains what the borrower can ask for and when, and lets the borrower download their data in readable formats.

### Document catalogue

Each entry is a `document_catalogue_entry` with issuer, owner, source, availability state and the rule that makes it available.

| Document | Issuer and owner | How Udofin serves it | When available | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KFS (with APR sheet and amortisation schedule) | RE | RE-signed copy stored in U9 on `KFSIssued`, hash and JWS verified before display | On issue; kept after acceptance or expiry | RBC para 29; CF para 9(1), 9(3) |
| Sanction letter | RE | As above on `SanctionLetterIssued` | On sanction | RBC para 13; CF para 9(3) |
| Loan agreement with every enclosure quoted in it | RE | Executed pack from U9 with enclosure checklist | At sanction or disbursal | RBC para 14; CF para 9(3) |
| Summary of loan product, terms and conditions, privacy policies of the RE and Udofin | RE and Udofin | Flowed on execution | On execution | CF para 9(3) |
| Statement of account and repayment schedule | RE | Fetched live from the RE (`GET /v1/documents/{id}`, Integration Specification 6.13) or from the U12 mirror labelled "as at [time], source [RE name]"; cache at most 24 hours [REC] | On demand | CF para 9(3) ("account statements"); U12 |
| Quarterly statement (floating-rate equated-instalment personal loans) | RE | Mirrored | Each quarter | RBC paras 31(6), 32 |
| Receipts, including insurance and other third-party charges collected by the RE | RE | Mirrored; Udofin's own acknowledgement reads "payment initiated", never "receipt" (U11) | Each payment | RBC para 29(4); U11 |
| Change-of-terms and penal-charge communications | RE | Mirrored with the communication log | On event | RBC paras 15, 30(7) |
| Cooling-off exit confirmation | RE | Mirrored | On exit | CF para 11 |
| Foreclosure statement | RE | Service request to the RE | On request | U12 |
| No-objection or closure certificate | RE | Mirrored on `NOCIssued` | On closure (RE policy timeline) | U12; RE policy [INTERP: RBC fixes no NOC deadline] |
| Release of original property documents and charge satisfaction | RE | Tracker with the 30-day clock, borrower's chosen collection place (RBC para 36) and the RE's compensation of ₹5,000 per day of delay attributable to it (RBC para 39) | Within 30 days of full repayment or settlement; 60 days if documents are lost or damaged (RBC para 40) | RBC paras 35–41 (personal loans) |
| Microfinance loan card | RE | Digital card from RE data | From disbursal | RBC paras 78–79 |
| Notices and letters | RE | UR3 notice inbox | On issue | Part 7A UR3 |
| eSign evidence and eStamp certificate | Provider evidence held by Udofin as RE's agent | From U9 | After execution | U9 |
| Tax documents | RE (UB2) | UB2 | Per UB2 | ITA25 |
| Consent receipts and consent ledger | Udofin | Generated from U4 | Any time | CF para 13; DPDP s.6 |
| Grievance case packs | Udofin | UB4 | Any time | UB4 |
| Subscription invoices and credit notes | Udofin (only if a wellness subscription exists) | Part 7G | Each charge | GST |

**Rules.**

- **RE-owned documents are served from the RE.** Udofin displays only the RE-signed version; it never re-renders, edits or re-brands an RE document (CF para 9(3); Part 5.1). A hash or signature mismatch blocks display and raises an exception to the RE.
- **Missing or not-yet-issued documents** show "Not yet issued by [RE name]" with a one-tap request that creates a U12 `service_request` with the RE's SLA from the deal configuration (UP2); overdue requests escalate to the RE and are visible in UP3 pack P4.
- **Co-borrowers and guarantors** see only documents to which they are a party; business-entity borrowers see documents through authorised-signatory roles.
- **After a deal ends** (UP5) the borrower keeps download access for at least 90 days after the servicing view closes, with notice before it ends, then sees "request from [RE name]" with the RE's contact.
- **Deceased borrower:** requests from legal heirs are routed to the RE's published legal-heir procedure (RBC para 38); Udofin releases nothing to heirs on its own authority. For Udofin-owned data, a DPDP nominee is honoured (DPDP s.14) from 13 May 2027 [VERIFY commencement].
- **Non-RE lenders (UP4):** documents are issued by the society and shown with the society's name; RBI-specific labels are suppressed.

### Download and share controls

| Action | Control |
|---|---|
| View in app or browser | Authenticated session; viewer overlays a visible watermark (masked name, "viewed on [date, time IST]", view ID); screenshots blocked on Android (`FLAG_SECURE`) for KFS, sanction letter, agreement and statements; iOS shows a privacy cover in the app switcher |
| **Download original** (byte-identical RE-signed file) | Step-up re-authentication (OTP to the registered mobile, passkey or device biometric unlock, U3) if the last authentication is older than 5 minutes; the file is never altered, so its signature and SHA-256 still verify; the download is logged with a download ID and a "document downloaded" notice goes to the registered channels |
| **Download shareable copy** | Same step-up; a PDF/A rendition watermarked on every page with the masked name, download ID, date and "Copy — verify the original at [verification URL] with this ID"; the verification page confirms issuer, document type, date and hash without showing content |
| Share | Only through the operating-system share sheet with the shareable copy; never a public link; e-mail and SMS carry no attachment |
| Limits and alerts | 20 original downloads per day per borrower [REC]; repeated step-up failures lock downloads for 30 minutes and alert the borrower; downloads from a new device within 24 hours of binding need a second factor |

### My data: access, correction, erasure and export

| Right or feature | Legal position | Udofin implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Summary of personal data and processing; identities of other fiduciaries and processors it was shared with, and a description of what was shared | [LAW] DPDP s.11 (from 13 May 2027) | "What we hold about you": Udofin's own data plus the list of REs and providers that received data, by consent artefact; built now as practice [REC] |
| Correction, completion, updating, erasure | [LAW] DPDP s.12; s.8(7) (erasure unless retention is required by law) | U4 request flow; loan data requests forwarded to the RE as `DataPrincipalRequest` within 1 working day; statutory retention explained in plain words (for example PMLA and KYC records, KYC Directions; CIC reporting) |
| Response time | [LAW] DPDP Rules r.14(3): grievances answered within the period the fiduciary publishes, at most 90 days (from 13 May 2027) [VERIFY: whether the same limit governs s.11–12 requests] | Udofin target 30 days for every request [REC]; clock shown; a shorter RE or RBI clock wins |
| Grievance about data handling | [LAW] DPDP s.13 (exhaust before the Board) | UB3 data route |
| Nomination | [LAW] DPDP s.14; Rules | U4 nomination record |
| Data portability | **No portability right** in the DPDP Act [LAW] | Offered anyway as "Download my data" [REC] |

**"Download my data" package (borrower export).**

- **Scope selection:** account and profile; consents and notices shown; applications and journeys; loans (mirror data, labelled with the RE as source and the "as at" time); documents; communications; grievances. Wellness add-on data (Part 7D) is a **separate** package from its own store and is never merged into this one.
- **Format:** archive standard folder profile `udofin_borrower_v1` (Integration Specification 12.1): `00 Start Here/` with the README as PDF, DOCX and TXT (a plain-language guide in the borrower's language), `export-manifest.csv`, `manifest.json` (files, counts, SHA-256) and its detached JWS; each dataset as `[dataset].csv`, `[dataset].xlsx` and `[dataset].schema.json` (JSON Lines optional); documents byte-identical with their original hashes; readable without Udofin.
- **Security:** step-up authentication (U3); device risk check; package encrypted (AES-256 ZIP or equivalent) with a passphrase the borrower sets on screen; download only in the authenticated app or web through a signed URL valid at most 15 minutes; email and SMS carry a notification, never the file or the passphrase; an alert goes to every registered channel when an export is generated (account-takeover defence); package deleted 7 days after generation [REC].
- **Limits:** at most 3 full exports per 30 days per borrower [REC], unlimited single-document downloads; requests above the limit go to support.
- **RE part:** where the borrower asks for data only the RE holds (for example underwriting data), Udofin forwards a `DataPrincipalRequest` and shows "[RE name] will respond"; Udofin never pulls RE back-office data it does not already hold.

### States

- `document_request`: `REQUESTED → FORWARDED_TO_RE → RE_ACKNOWLEDGED → {FULFILLED | DECLINED (reason) }`, with `OVERDUE` raised by timer and `CANCELLED` by the borrower.
- `data_access_request` (extends U4 `data_principal_request`): `SUBMITTED → IDENTITY_VERIFIED → IN_PROGRESS (Udofin part; RE part forwarded) → READY → DELIVERED → CLOSED`, with `PARTIALLY_REFUSED` (legal retention or third-party rights, with reasons).
- `borrower_export_job`: `REQUESTED → STEP_UP_PASSED → GENERATING → READY → DOWNLOADED → PURGED`, with `EXPIRED` (not downloaded within 7 days; purged) and `FAILED` (generation error; the borrower is told and may retry without using a monthly allowance).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step-up freshness for downloads and exports | Platform | 5 minutes | Security floor (may shorten) |
| Signed-URL validity | Platform | 15 minutes | Security floor (Integration Spec 6.13) |
| Full exports per 30 days | Platform | 3 | Commercial [REC] |
| Export package retention | Platform | 7 days | Commercial [REC] |
| Statement mirror freshness | RE | 24 hours | RE may shorten |
| Document-request SLA | RE | From the deal configuration (UP2 section 6) | RE-defined |
| Post-exit download access | Platform | 90 days | Floor (UP5) |
| Borrower notification on each download | Borrower | On for originals and exports | Cannot be switched off for exports |

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Documents and data** (A, B): tabs **By loan**, **By type**, **My data**; filters (lender, loan, type, year); document card with issuer, status ("Issued", "Not yet issued by [RE name]", "Requested on [date]"), **View**, **Download original**, **Download shareable copy**, **Request**; **Download my data** wizard (scope → step-up → passphrase → generate → download); request tracker with clocks; empty state "No documents yet: they appear when [RE name] issues them".
- Accessibility: tagged PDFs, screen-reader labels, large-type mode, read-aloud of document summaries.
- **Operations portal › Service › Document requests** (C): queues with clocks, never document content beyond what support needs. **Lender portal › Servicing › Document requests** (D): the RE's queue of document and data-principal requests, with **Fulfil**, **Decline with reason** and bulk upload.

### Controls

- UB-C01: no display of an RE document whose hash or JWS fails verification.
- UB-C02: export generation requires step-up authentication within the last 5 minutes.
- UB-C03: wellness data cannot be included in the loan export (separate store and job type).
- UB-C04: document requests and DPDP requests forwarded to the RE carry the receipt timestamp so that the RE's clock is visible in UP3 pack P4 and P6.

### Acceptance tests

- A KFS with a tampered byte is not displayed and raises an RE exception.
- A co-borrower cannot see the primary borrower's separate personal-loan documents.
- A borrower requesting an NOC not yet issued sees the RE's SLA and the request appears in the RE's lender-portal queue.
- A full export contains README, manifest and every selected scope; recomputed hashes match the manifest; the package cannot be opened without the passphrase.
- A fourth full export within 30 days is refused with a support route.
- An original KFS downloaded after step-up has the same SHA-256 as the RE-signed file; a shareable copy carries the download ID on every page and the verification page confirms it; a download without a step-up in the last 5 minutes prompts for OTP or passkey.
- An erasure request covering loan data produces a `DataPrincipalRequest` to the RE within 1 working day and a borrower message naming the RE and the retention reasons.
- Wellness data never appears in a loan export, even when "select all" is chosen.

## UB2. Tax documents and business-borrower details

### Purpose and scope

Present the lender-issued documents borrowers need for income-tax and GST purposes, mapped correctly to the Income-tax Act, 2025, explain the regime position in neutral words, capture business-borrower tax details for the RE, and relay TDS certificates from business borrowers to the RE. **Udofin never issues a tax certificate, never computes a deduction and never gives tax advice.**

### Transition between the two Acts

| Period | Governing Act | Certificate wording |
|---|---|---|
| Financial year 2025-26 (assessment under the 1961 Act) | ITA61 (s.24(b), s.80C, s.80E, s.80EE, s.80EEA, s.80EEB) | 1961-Act variant |
| Tax year 2026-27 onwards | ITA25 (in force 1 Apr 2026) | 2025-Act variant |

[LAW via secondary concordances] The 2025 Act applies by tax year; documents for FY 2025-26 keep 1961-Act references [VERIFY: CBDT transition guidance].

### Lender-issued certificates

| Certificate | 2025-Act provision | Content the RE certificate must carry (validated before display) | Notes shown to the borrower |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home-loan interest certificate | s.22(1)(b) interest on borrowed capital; s.22(1)(c) pre-construction interest in five equal instalments; s.22(2)(a) deduction depends on "a certificate from the person to whom interest is payable"; s.22(4) interest stated, including on any refinancing loan; caps in s.22(2)(a) (₹2,00,000 for s.21(6) property, construction within 5 years), s.22(2)(b) (₹30,000) and s.22(5) (aggregate ₹2,00,000) | RE name and PAN, borrower and co-borrower names with share as recorded by the RE, loan account, sanction date and amount, purpose, property address, possession or completion date, tax year, interest paid or due, pre-construction interest total and the instalment year, refinancing flag, digital signature | Regime notice; "Caps and eligibility depend on your facts; consult a tax professional" [VERIFY: s.21(6) scope] |
| Home-loan principal statement | s.123 with Schedule XV ("repayment of home loan principal"), within the ₹1,50,000 aggregate | Principal repaid in the tax year | Regime notice |
| Legacy additional deductions | s.130 (old 80EE), s.131 (old 80EEA), s.132 (old 80EEB, electric vehicle) for loans sanctioned in the legacy windows only | Sanction date and window flag | Hidden until confirmed [VERIFY: secondary concordances differ on whether old s.80EEA has a successor (s.131) and on the s.130 mapping; confirm both against the official CBDT comparison table before enabling] |
| Education-loan interest certificate | s.129: interest only, no cap, for the initial tax year and the 7 following years (8 in all); lender must be an eligible financial institution or approved charitable institution | Interest paid, year count, lender's eligibility reference | Regime notice; shown only if the RE records its s.129 eligibility [VERIFY: notification requirement for NBFCs] |
| Annual interest and principal statement (any loan) | No specific deduction | Interest and principal for the tax year | "For your records; a deduction depends on how the loan was used" |

**Regime notice (fixed text, shown with every certificate):** "Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 the new tax regime (section 202) applies by default. Deductions under sections 123, 129 to 132, and interest on a self-occupied house property under section 22(1)(b), are not available under it unless you opt out of the new regime. This is general information, not tax advice." [LAW: ITA25 s.202] [VERIFY wording with counsel]

**Rules.**

- **Issuer is the RE only.** A certificate is displayed only when received from the RE (`InterestCertificateIssued` with the signed PDF/A, or `DocumentShared`), with hash and signature verified. Udofin never generates, edits or co-signs one (ITA25 s.22(2)(a): the certificate comes from the person to whom interest is payable) [LAW].
- **Provisional and final:** the borrower may request a provisional certificate during the tax year (for an employer's investment declaration) and the final one after the year ends; both are U12 service requests to the RE with the RE's SLA [MKT].
- **Udofin summary card** (optional): totals read from the RE certificate, labelled "Summary of your lender's certificate — not a tax certificate". It never shows a computed deduction.
- **Co-borrower shares** come only from the RE certificate; Udofin never apportions interest.
- **Society loans (UP4):** the society issues the certificate; same display rules.
- **Retention:** tax documents remain downloadable for at least 8 years after the tax year [REC], subject to the RE's retention and UP5.
- **Never** ask for income-tax e-filing portal credentials, OTPs or AIS downloads.

### Business borrowers: TDS certificates (Form 131)

Where a business borrower is required to deduct tax at source on interest it pays to the RE (ITA25 s.393 table entry that replaced old s.194A [VERIFY entry and threshold]), it must issue Form 131 (old Form 16A) to the RE for each quarter.

- **Upload slot** per loan and quarter, through the system document picker (no storage permission; Part 4.5).
- **Validation:** PDF only; the deductor's TAN and name, the RE's PAN as deductee, quarter, amount and certificate number extracted and confirmed by the borrower; no auto-acceptance of OCR values.
- **Relay:** sent to the RE as `DocumentShared` with the extracted fields; the RE reconciles against its Form 168 credit (old Form 26AS) [VERIFY form number] and returns a status (`matched`, `mismatch`, `not_found`).
- **Display:** the RE's reconciliation status and the RE's policy on whether EMIs are paid gross or net of TDS (from the deal configuration); reminders at quarter-end + 15 days [REC] only if the borrower opts in.
- Udofin never computes TDS, never files the deductor's quarterly TDS statement (Form 140 under the 2025 Act [VERIFY form number]) and never treats a short TDS credit as a payment.

### Business borrowers: GST details and invoices

- **Business tax profile (`business_tax_profile`):** legal name, trade name, constitution, PAN, GSTIN, registration state, status, place of supply.
- **GSTIN validation:** 15-character format; check digit; characters 3–12 equal the business PAN; first two digits equal the registration state code; status verified through the RE's provider or a GSP public-search call [VERIFY API terms]; cancelled or suspended GSTINs flagged to the RE.
- **Sharing:** the GSTIN goes to the chosen RE only within the application consent (CF para 13(4)); a later change is a U12 service request to the RE.
- **GST invoices for RE fees:** taxable fees and charges (processing, documentation, foreclosure, bounce and similar) are invoiced by the **RE** at the applicable rate (typically 18% under SAC 9971 [VERIFY per fee]); interest is exempt (GST: Notification 12/2017-CT(Rate) entry 27(a) [VERIFY wording]); penal charges levied under RBI's penal-charges framework attract no GST (GST: CBIC Circular 245/02/2025-GST); NBFCs are exempt from e-invoicing (CGST Rule 48(4); Notification 13/2020-CT), so RE invoices carry no IRN. Udofin mirrors the RE's B2B invoices and credit notes with the GSTIN for the borrower's input-tax-credit records; it never issues a GST invoice for an RE fee and never charges the borrower any fee of its own (CF para 10(4)).
- **Udofin's own invoices** exist only for a wellness subscription (Part 7D, Part 7G): Udofin is not on the e-invoicing exemption list, so B2B e-invoicing applies once its aggregate turnover crosses the threshold (₹5 crore from 1 Aug 2023; Notification 10/2023) [LAW].

### States

- `interest_certificate_mirror`: `REQUESTED → RECEIVED → VERIFIED → PUBLISHED`, with `REJECTED_INTEGRITY` and `SUPERSEDED` (a revised certificate replaces the earlier version, which stays visible as superseded).
- `tds_certificate_upload`: `UPLOADED → FIELDS_CONFIRMED → SENT_TO_RE → {MATCHED | MISMATCH | NOT_FOUND}`, with `WITHDRAWN`.
- `gstin_check`: `CAPTURED → FORMAT_VALID → VERIFIED_ACTIVE | VERIFIED_INACTIVE | UNVERIFIED`.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Act variant by period | Platform | FY 2025-26 → ITA61; tax year 2026-27 onwards → ITA25 | Fixed by law |
| s.131 legacy line | Platform | Off | Stays off until the successor is confirmed |
| s.129 certificate display | RE | Off until the RE records its eligibility reference | Regulatory gate (UB-C07) |
| Udofin summary card | Borrower | Off | Optional; never shows a computed deduction |
| Form 131 quarter-end reminder | Borrower | Off; quarter-end + 15 days when on | Opt-in [REC] |
| EMI treatment of TDS (gross or net) | RE | From the deal configuration | RE policy, displayed only |
| Tax-document retention | Platform | 8 years after the tax year | Floor [REC]; subject to RE retention and UP5 |

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Documents and data › Tax documents** (A, B): by tax year and loan; certificate card with Act variant, status (requested, received, superseded), **Request provisional**, **Request final**, **View**, **Download original**; regime notice on every view; **Business details** (only for business-entity accounts and authorised signatories): tax profile, GSTIN check result, **Upload Form 131** per quarter with field confirmation, RE reconciliation status, mirrored RE invoices and credit notes.
- **Lender portal › Servicing › Tax** (D): certificate-request queue, Form 131 inbox with extracted fields and **Mark matched / mismatch / not found**. **Operations portal** (C): integrity failures only.

### Controls

- UB-C05: no tax certificate template exists in Udofin's document generator (repository test).
- UB-C06: the regime notice is attached to every certificate view and download (rendering test).
- UB-C07: s.129 certificates are hidden unless the RE's eligibility reference is recorded.
- UB-C08: GSTIN with a PAN segment different from the business PAN is rejected.

### Acceptance tests

- A certificate whose signature fails verification is not shown; the RE is notified.
- A FY 2025-26 certificate displays 1961-Act references; a tax year 2026-27 certificate displays ITA25 references.
- The Udofin summary card carries "not a tax certificate" and shows no computed deduction.
- A Form 131 upload with an RE PAN not matching the loan's RE is rejected before sending.
- A GSTIN "27AAAAA0000A1Z5"-style test value with a wrong check digit fails; a valid one passes format checks and is marked unverified until the provider confirms.
- No Udofin GST invoice is produced for any RE fee line.

## UB3. Grievance escalation chain v2

### Purpose and scope

Route every complaint to the party responsible, run the clocks that matter, unlock each escalation option at the right moment, and display the right external routes for the lender and the subject, without Udofin deciding, closing or filing anything that belongs to the RE, an Ombudsman or the borrower.

### Legal anchors

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| RE and LSP each designate a nodal grievance officer; contacts on the RE website, Udofin website, DLA and KFS; complaints can be lodged on the DLA; redressal responsibility stays with the RE | [REG] CF para 12(1)–(3) |
| If the RE rejects wholly or partly, the borrower is dissatisfied, or no reply within 30 days of receipt by the RE, the borrower may complain on CMS or to CRPC Chandigarh under RB-IOS "as applicable"; this must be conveyed | [REG] CF para 12(4) |
| Grievance responsibility for outsourced services rests with the RE; GRO displayed; 30 days; Ombudsman or CEPC route | [REG] OUT paras 54–57 (para 57(4) still cites the 2021 Scheme) |
| Disputes heard at least at the next higher level; Board review | [REG] RBC paras 7(2) Note, 8 |
| Recovery-grievance mechanism; grievance-officer block on recovery communications | [REG] RBC para 92; Third Amendment para 100AA from 1 Jan 2027 [VERIFY official text] |
| RB-IOS 2026: covers deposit-taking NBFCs and NBFCs with a customer interface and assets of ₹100 crore or more; excludes HFCs, CICs (core investment), IDF-NBFCs, IFCs, NOFHCs, PDs and MGCs; covers credit information companies except CICRA s.18 matters | [REG] RB-IOS 2026 cl.1(3) [VERIFY clause numbering against the official text] |
| Maintainability: complaint first made to the RE (cl.10(1)(e)); RE reply period 30 days (cl.10(1)(f)); Ombudsman complaint within **90 days** from the end of that period or the date of the RE's last communication, **whichever is later** (cl.10(1)(g)); an authorised representative may file, but not an advocate unless the advocate is the aggrieved person (cl.10(1)(b)); complaints received under the Scheme before 1 Jul 2026 continue under the 2021 Scheme (cl.20) | [REG] RB-IOS 2026; RBI FAQ on RB-IOS 2026 [VERIFY: clause numbering against the official text] |
| Compensation up to ₹30 lakh for consequential loss and up to ₹3 lakh for loss of time, expenses, harassment and mental anguish; award accepted within 30 days, complied with within 30 days; appeal to the Appellate Authority (Executive Director in charge of CEPD) within 30 days, extendable by 30 | [REG] RB-IOS 2026 [VERIFY] |
| Principal Nodal Officer of at least General Manager rank; salient features displayed in English, Hindi and the regional language | [REG] RB-IOS 2026 cl.18(2), 18(4)–(6) [VERIFY] |
| Internal Ombudsman: NBFC-D with 10 or more branches and NBFC-ND with assets of ₹5,000 crore or more and a public interface (HFCs and others excluded); wholly or partly rejected complaints auto-escalated to the IO within 20 days; final reply within 30 days | [REG] IO 2026 [VERIFY paragraph numbers] |
| Credit-information disputes: CI has 21 days to send corrected data; ₹100 per calendar day after 30 days; complaint forms capture bank or UPI details for compensation | [REG] CIR paras 34–35 |

### Lender redress profile

Computed per RE from `re_regulatory_profile` and the deal configuration (UP2 section 10), re-evaluated on every asset-size update, and versioned (`re_redress_profile`):

- `rbios_covered` (deposit-taking, or customer interface and assets ≥ ₹100 crore, and not an excluded class);
- `io_applicable` (thresholds above);
- `top_tier` = `RBI_OMBUDSMAN` | `CEPC_REGIONAL_OFFICE` (NBFC outside RB-IOS; OUT para 57(4)(ii)) | `NHB` (HFC; [VERIFY current NHB grievance route]) | `BANK_RBIOS` (bank REs) | `COOP_ROUTE` (UP4 societies);
- PNO, GRO, IO (as published by the RE), CIC nodal officer, recovery-grievance contact, CEPC regional office address.

### Tiers

| Tier | Owner | Entry | Timer and automatic action |
|---|---|---|---|
| T0 Help centre | Udofin | Articles, guided flows, AI assistant (disclosed as AI; "talk to a human" always offered) | No timer; "Raise a complaint" one tap from every screen (UB4) |
| T1 Udofin nodal grievance officer | Udofin (CF para 12(1)) | App, web, email, phone, assisted channel. A chain may also start at the help section of the RE's own website or a Finbyx-hosted page; those cases appear in the borrower's Udofin case list when the grievance host shares them (`GrievanceUpdated`) | Acknowledgement with reference at once (automated); classification within 1 business day; **every complaint about the RE's product, decision or conduct forwarded to the RE immediately, target within 1 hour** (U15), with the RE's receipt acknowledgement stored; complaints about Udofin's own conduct resolved within 7 days [REC] and copied to the RE, because the RE stays responsible (CF para 12(3)) |
| T1a Udofin grievance head | Udofin | Borrower dissatisfied with a Udofin-only reply | Next-higher-level review within 7 days [REC; mirrors RBC para 7(2)] |
| T2 RE GRO | RE (OUT para 57(2)) | Forwarded by Udofin, or direct to the RE (mirrored when the RE shares it) | Reply within 30 days of the RE's receipt; reminder to the RE at day 20 and day 25 [REC]; next-higher-level review inside the RE (RBC para 7(2)) |
| T3 RE Internal Ombudsman | RE, if `io_applicable` | The RE's system escalates any partial or full rejection automatically | Escalated by day 20; final reply by day 30 (IO 2026); Udofin shows "under review by [RE name]'s Internal Ombudsman" from `GrievanceEscalated` |
| T3' Principal Nodal Officer | RE, if `rbios_covered` | Displayed as a contact | No separate clock |
| T4 RBI Ombudsman (CMS or CRPC) | RBI | **The borrower files.** Udofin unlocks the "Take this to the RBI Ombudsman" panel and the case pack; it never files without the borrower's own action | Opens at the earliest of: RE final reply rejecting wholly or partly, borrower marks the reply unsatisfactory, or expiry of the RE's 30-day period with no reply; **closes 90 days after the later of the end of the RE's 30-day period and the RE's last communication** (RB-IOS cl.10(1)(g)); countdown shown; a borrower who declares an Ombudsman filing made before 1 Jul 2026 is tagged `RBIOS_2021` and shown the 2021 Scheme position; filings on or after 1 Jul 2026 use the 90-day window even where the RE received the complaint earlier [INTERP; VERIFY cl.20 wording] |
| T4-alt CEPC of the RBI regional office | RBI | `top_tier = CEPC_REGIONAL_OFFICE` | Same unlocking rule; regional office address from the profile [VERIFY post-2026 CEPC route] |
| T5 Appellate Authority | RBI (ED in charge of CEPD) | Borrower appeals an Ombudsman decision | 30 days, extendable by 30; information only |
| Co-operative route (UP4) | Society GRO → Co-operative Ombudsman (MSCS s.85A; decision within 3 months, appeal to the Central Registrar within 1 month) [VERIFY] or State Registrar → co-operative court or statutory arbitration (MSCS s.84; MH s.91) | Society loans only | 30-day society reply target by contract [REC]; RBI routes not shown |

**Clock rules.**

- **Legal clock start** is the RE's receipt, evidenced by the forwarding acknowledgement; the internal clock starts at Udofin's receipt. Because forwarding targets 1 hour, the two normally coincide. If the RE has not acknowledged within 1 business day, Udofin escalates to the RE's nodal officer and displays the Udofin forwarding time as the receipt date, with that basis disclosed in the case pack [INTERP; record the RE's agreement in the LSP agreement].
- Clocks run in calendar days; Udofin's own SLAs use business days where stated.
- A reopened complaint (UB4) sent to the RE gets a new RE receipt time; the T4 window is recomputed from the RE's last communication.
- Udofin never stops or pauses an RE clock; only the RE's reply events change status.
- `window_closes_at = max(re_received_at + 30 days, last_re_communication_at) + 90 days`, in calendar days and IST; each RE message that is a substantive reply (not an acknowledgement or information request) updates `last_re_communication_at`.

### SLA timers and automatic escalation

| Clock | Starts | Due | Reminder | On breach (automatic) | Visible to borrower |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acknowledgement | Udofin receipt | Immediately | — | Severity-2 alert to Udofin support lead | Yes (reference number) |
| Classification | Udofin receipt | 1 business day | 4 business hours | Page the Udofin grievance head | No |
| Forward to RE | Classification | 1 hour (target) | 30 minutes | Page Udofin GRO; logged in P4 | Yes ("sent to [RE name] at [time]") |
| RE acknowledgement | Forwarding | 1 business day | — | Escalate to the RE nodal officer; receipt basis switches to Udofin forwarding time | Yes (receipt date and basis) |
| Udofin-only resolution | Udofin receipt | 7 days [REC] | Day 5 | Auto-escalate to T1a | Yes |
| RE reply | RE receipt | 30 days | Day 20, day 25 | Unlock T4 panel on day 31; page Udofin compliance and the RE nodal officer at day 25 | Yes (countdown) |
| IO escalation (`io_applicable`) | RE partial or full rejection | 20 days | Day 15 | Internal escalation page if no IO status | Yes ("under review by the Internal Ombudsman") |
| External window | Later of RE period end and last RE communication | + 90 days | 30, 14 and 3 days before close (opt-in) | Panel shows "window closed" with other remedies (consumer commission, courts) | Yes |
| Credit information (CIR para 35) | Complaint to the CI | 21 days (CI), 30 days overall | Day 15 | Compensation clock (₹100 per day) shown | Yes |
| Priority tags (`recovery_conduct`, `fraud`, `PwD`) | Udofin receipt | First action in 24 hours | 12 hours | Page Udofin compliance and the RE nodal officer | Yes |

### Parallel routes (shown by subject, never in place of the RBI route for an RE complaint)

| Subject | Route | Udofin role |
|---|---|---|
| Credit information report errors | RE's CIC nodal officer (CIR para 34(2)) or the CIC directly; 21-day and 30-day clocks; ₹100 per day thereafter (CIR para 35); then RB-IOS (CICs are covered except CICRA s.18 matters) or CEPC | Category `credit_information` with mandatory bank or UPI details for compensation (CIR para 35(8)); immediate forwarding; for wellness credit reports (Part 7D FW1), a deep link to the CIC's own dispute page |
| Insurance (Part 7F products or RE-arranged cover) | Insurer's GRO → Bima Bharosa (optional) → Insurance Ombudsman under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 via the CIO portal, within 1 year of the insurer's reply, claims up to ₹50 lakh [VERIFY rule numbers and limits] | Information, claim-assistance tracking, case pack; never decides |
| Personal data | Udofin's (or the RE's) data-protection contact → exhaust under DPDP s.13 → Data Protection Board of India (from 13 May 2027 [VERIFY]); before then the grievance officer under the IT Act and SPDI Rules [VERIFY] | U4 request and UB3 category `personal_data`; routing to the fiduciary responsible (Udofin or the RE) |
| Udofin subscription or wellness add-on (non-RBI) | Udofin GRO → National Consumer Helpline (1915) → consumer commission via e-Daakhil (CPA19) | Udofin owns and resolves; RE never involved |
| Recovery conduct | RE recovery-grievance mechanism (RBC para 92) and GRO; immediate RE notification; stop-contact flag (Part 7A UR4) | Category `recovery_conduct`; police helpline 112 shown for threats of violence [REC] |
| Fraud or unauthorised transaction | RE (block and report); National Cyber Crime helpline 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in [REC] | Category `fraud`; immediate RE alert (U24) |
| Unregulated lender or deposit scheme | RBI Sachet portal [REC] | Information only |
| ODR (mediation, conciliation, arbitration) | Only through RE referral or the borrower's consent (Part 7A UR2) | Never presented as a substitute for the RBI route |
| Courts and consumer commissions | Any time within limitation | Information only; never discouraged |

### Display rules

- GRO and Udofin nodal officer (name, phone, email) on every DLA help screen, Udofin website and in the KFS (CF para 12(2)); the RE's PNO where `rbios_covered`.
- Link to the RE's disclosure page carrying the CMS and Sachet links (CF para 9(4)–(5); CF para 18(4)(i)).
- RB-IOS salient features mirrored from the RE in English, Hindi and the borrower's regional language (RB-IOS cl.18(4)–(6) is the RE's duty; Udofin mirrors the RE-approved text).
- Every case page shows: who owns it (Udofin or [RE name]), the current tier, the live clock, the next option and when it opens, and the T4 countdown once open.
- Neutral wording only: no "we recommend you do not escalate", no delay tactics, no success predictions; the CMS route is visible on every ADR screen (UR2).
- For society loans: "The RBI Ombudsman does not cover co-operative societies" with the correct route.
- For an HFC: the RB-IOS exclusion and the NHB route as configured [VERIFY].

### States (extends U15)

`grievance`: `DRAFT → SUBMITTED → ACKNOWLEDGED → CLASSIFIED → {UDOFIN_HANDLING → (RESOLVED_BY_UDOFIN | ESCALATED_UDOFIN_HEAD) | FORWARDED_TO_RE → RE_ACKNOWLEDGED → RE_IN_PROGRESS → (IO_REVIEW)? → RE_FINAL_REPLY (resolved | partially_resolved | rejected | no_reply_30d)} → BORROWER_RESPONSE (accepted | not_satisfied) → {CLOSED | EXTERNAL_ROUTE_OPEN → EXTERNAL_REFERRAL_DECLARED → CLOSED_EXTERNAL_PENDING} → REOPENED?`, plus `WITHDRAWN`.

- `EXTERNAL_ROUTE_OPEN` carries `window_opens_at`, `window_closes_at` and `route` (RBI Ombudsman, CEPC, NHB, co-operative, insurance, DPB, consumer).
- `EXTERNAL_REFERRAL_DECLARED` stores the borrower-declared CMS or other reference and date (`OmbudsmanReferralRecorded`); Udofin then mirrors any RE-reported Ombudsman stages (facilitation, conciliation, advisory, award) if the RE shares them. Event `forum` values (Integration Spec 6.12): RBI Ombudsman → `RBIOS_2026`; Co-operative Ombudsman → `COOP_OMBUDSMAN`; State or Central Registrar → `REGISTRAR`; consumer commission → `CONSUMER_COMMISSION`; CEPC, NHB, insurance, Data Protection Board and courts → `OTHER` with the local route code.
- Exception paths: a borrower may withdraw at any state (record kept); an RE reply received after the T4 panel opens is shown and recomputes the window only if it is later than the period end; a duplicate complaint on the same subject within 7 days is linked to the open case, never silently merged.

### Automatic actions

- Udofin auto-escalates **internally** only, as the timer table sets out (`PwD` tag: RBC para 28); every escalation is a `grievance_tier_transition` with reason and actor `SYSTEM`, idempotent per clock and breach.
- Udofin auto-unlocks **borrower** options; it never auto-files externally and never acts as the borrower's representative before an Ombudsman [REC: conflict of interest].
- Outage rule: if the RE connector is down, forwarding falls back to the RE's agreed e-mail or SFTP channel within the 1-hour target, the fallback is logged, and the clocks keep running.
- AI may draft classifications and replies for staff review; it never rejects, closes, settles or advises against escalation (U20; FREE-AI human authority [GUID]).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| RE reply period | Platform | 30 days | Regulatory ceiling (CF para 12(4); OUT para 57); RE may reply sooner |
| External window | Platform | 90 days (RB-IOS 2026) | Fixed by the Scheme |
| RE reply reminders | RE | Day 20 and day 25 | Tighten only |
| Forwarding target | Platform | 1 hour | Commercial floor (U15) |
| Udofin-only resolution target and T1a review | Platform | 7 days each | Commercial [REC] |
| Redress profile (RB-IOS coverage, IO, top tier) | RE | Computed from `re_regulatory_profile` | Computed; manual override only with Udofin compliance approval and evidence |
| Borrower window reminders | Borrower | Off | Opt-in |
| AI drafting of replies | Platform | On, staff approval required | AI never sends, rejects or closes |

### Menu and screens

- **Help › My complaints** (A, B): see UB4.
- **Operations portal › Grievances** (C): tiered queues (T0–T2, priority tags first), case detail with timeline, clocks and forwarding evidence, clock heatmap, breach board, RE acknowledgement monitor; actions **Classify**, **Forward to RE**, **Resolve (Udofin only)**, **Escalate to grievance head**, **Request information**; saved views by RE and category; keyboard shortcuts (`f` forward, `r` reply, `e` escalate).
- **Lender portal › Grievances** (D): the RE's queue with clocks, **Acknowledge**, **Reply**, **Final reply** (resolved, partially resolved, rejected), IO status update, Ombudsman stage update, monthly MIS (UP3 pack P4). Finbyx or LawDocsComply as grievance host under the Part 2 switch use the same events.

### Controls

- UB-C09: the redress profile must exist and be current before an RE deal reaches `PILOT` (UP1).
- UB-C10: no Udofin role can set `RE_FINAL_REPLY` or close an RE-owned complaint (permission test; CF para 12(3); OUT para 56).
- UB-C11: T4 panel never displays for `COOP_ROUTE`; co-operative route never displays for an RE loan.
- UB-C12: templates containing discouraging phrases fail the content linter.
- UB-C13: every forwarded complaint has an RE receipt acknowledgement or an open escalation.

### Acceptance tests

- An RE with assets of ₹80 crore, no deposits: the T4 panel shows the CEPC regional office, not the RBI Ombudsman.
- An HFC loan never shows the RB-IOS panel and shows the configured NHB route.
- A complaint received by the RE on 1 Aug 2026 with no reply: the RE's 30-day period ends on 31 Aug 2026; the external route opens on 1 Sep 2026 and closes on 29 Nov 2026 (90 days after the period ends) [VERIFY day-count convention against RB-IOS 2026 cl.10]; the countdown is correct across month boundaries.
- The same complaint with an RE rejection sent on 15 Sep 2026: the window closes on 14 Dec 2026 (90 days after the later date).
- A complaint received by the RE on 20 Jun 2026 with no reply, filed by the borrower after 1 Jul 2026: the window closes on 18 Oct 2026 under the 2026 Scheme; a borrower-declared filing dated 25 Jun 2026 is tagged `RBIOS_2021`.
- A partial rejection by an `io_applicable` RE without an IO status by day 20 triggers an internal escalation page.
- A credit-information complaint without bank or UPI details cannot be submitted.
- A subscription complaint never reaches any RE and shows the consumer route.
- An AI-drafted reply cannot be sent without a staff approval, and no AI action can close a case.

## UB4. Borrower complaint capabilities and help centre

### Purpose and scope

Specify what a borrower can do with a complaint, what the case pack contains, how help-centre content is modelled and approved, and how all of it works in the borrower's language and accessibility needs.

### Borrower capabilities

| # | Capability | Behaviour | Event or record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Raise a complaint | From any screen, the help centre, a document, a payment or a notice; category picker in plain words; in the borrower's language; free text plus structured fields; voice note with transcript [REC] | `GrievanceRaised` |
| 2 | Attach evidence | Through the system document or photo picker only (no storage permission; Part 4.5); up to 10 files, 10 MB each [REC]; virus-scanned; hash recorded | `grievance_attachment` |
| 3 | Acknowledgement and reference | Instant reference number and acknowledgement in app and by SMS or email on the registered contact | U15 |
| 4 | Track | Owner (Udofin or [RE name]), tier, live clock, next option and its opening date, full timeline | `grievance_event` |
| 5 | Reply and add information | Threaded messages; RE information requests appear as tasks with reminders | `GrievanceUpdated` |
| 6 | Escalate | One tap when a timer expires or after a rejection: inside Udofin (T1a), to the RE (if raised against Udofin and the borrower wants the RE's review), or to the external route panel (T4) with instructions and the pre-filled case pack | `GrievanceEscalated`; `OmbudsmanReferralRecorded` when the borrower declares a filing |
| 7 | Download case pack | PDF/A plus JSON: summary, timeline with timestamps and time zone, the original complaint, attachments list with hashes, all replies, the RE's final reply, clock calculations and the basis for the receipt date, lender details (name, registration, GRO, PNO), Udofin's LSP details, loan reference partly masked, the route and window; signed by Udofin; sized for CMS upload limits [VERIFY CMS file limits] | `case_pack` |
| 8 | Reopen | Within 30 days of closure [REC]; same case ID; reason required; sent to the RE as a fresh receipt | `GrievanceReopened` |
| 9 | Rate the resolution | 1–5 stars plus optional text after closure; never shown to the handling agent before closure; a low rating prompts the escalation options, never a retention offer | `GrievanceRated` |
| 10 | Withdraw | At any time with an optional reason; withdrawal never removes the record | `grievance_event` |
| 11 | Nominate a representative | A person authorised in writing, not an advocate unless the advocate is the aggrieved person (RB-IOS cl.10(1)(b); RBI FAQ); authorisation and consent captured; the representative gets read-only case access by OTP on their own mobile | `grievance_representative` |
| 12 | Request a callback and choose an accessible format | Callback within the borrower's chosen window and lawful calling hours (Part 7H RA5); large text, screen reader, audio read-out, regional language, assisted channel; PwD tag (RBC para 28) | `callback_request`; `accessibility_preference` |

### Borrower-visible timeline

Every case page shows a vertical timeline, newest first, with time in IST and the actor: received by Udofin; classified (category in plain words); sent to [RE name] (with forwarding time); acknowledged by [RE name] (receipt date and its basis); information requested (task with due date); reply sent; escalated (tier, reason, "automatic" or "by you"); Internal Ombudsman review; final reply (type); your response; external route open (window dates and countdown); filing declared; Ombudsman stage (as the RE reports); closed, reopened, rated or withdrawn. Internal notes, staff names beyond the role, and AI drafts never appear. The same timeline is the spine of the case pack.

### Help-centre content model

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `article_id`, `type` | FAQ, guided flow, rights explainer, RE-specific article, product explainer, regulatory notice (for example RB-IOS salient features) |
| `scope` | Global, RE-specific (tenant), product, channel, lender class (RE or society) |
| `locale` and translations | Source language plus approved translations; machine translation only as a draft for human review [REC] |
| `owner` and `approver` | Udofin content owner; RE approver for RE-specific content (RBC para 10); Udofin legal for rights and regulatory content |
| `sources` | Citations to the regulation or RE policy version the article relies on |
| `version`, `effective_from`, `review_due` | Review at least every 6 months and on any linked regulation or policy change [REC] |
| `reading_level` | Target plain language (approximately grade 6–8) [REC] |
| `complaint_cta` | Mandatory "Raise a complaint" action on every article |
| `ai_usable` | Only approved, published, in-date articles feed the AI assistant (U20) |

**Rules.**

- **Deflection must never block.** Deflection metrics are reported but never used as a target that discourages complaints; the complaint button is never hidden behind a minimum number of articles or chatbot turns.
- **Accuracy over speed.** An article tied to a changed regulation is withdrawn from AI use the day its `review_due` is triggered.
- **RE content separation:** an RE's articles appear only for that RE's borrowers.

### Multilingual and accessible

- English and Hindi at launch; regional languages following the KFS language set (UP2 section 4); RB-IOS salient features in English, Hindi and the regional language.
- The complaint form, case page, case pack summary and help articles are available in each supported language; the RE's replies are shown as sent, with a machine translation clearly labelled as such [REC].
- WCAG 2.2 AA on web and platform accessibility APIs on mobile; no CAPTCHA without an accessible alternative; assisted channel (U22) for borrowers who cannot use the app.

### MIS and feedback

- Complaint MIS by RE, category (including FS 21(10) grounds), channel, tier reached, TAT, reopen rate, rating distribution, external referrals declared; feeds UP3 pack P4 and the RE's FPC conduct review (RBC para 8).
- Root-cause tags reviewed monthly by Udofin product and compliance [REC].

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attachments per complaint | Platform | 10 files, 10 MB each | Commercial [REC] |
| Reopen window | Platform | 30 days after closure | Commercial [REC]; never shorter |
| Rating prompt | Platform | On closure, once | Ratings hidden from handlers until closure (fixed) |
| Help-article review cycle | Platform | 6 months and on linked change | Tighten only |
| Languages | Platform | English, Hindi, plus the KFS language set | RB-IOS salient features always in English, Hindi and the regional language |
| Push content | Platform | No case content | Security floor |
| Minimum articles or bot turns before "Raise a complaint" | Platform | 0 | Fixed (deflection never blocks) |

### Menu and screens

- **Help** tab (A, B): search, top articles for the borrower's lender and loan, **Raise a complaint** (always visible), **My complaints**, **Call me back**, "verify this agent".
- **Help › Raise a complaint** wizard: what is it about (plain-word categories) → which loan or lender (pre-filled from the screen it was opened on) → describe (text or voice note) → attach (system picker) → contact preference and language → review → submit; inline validation (for example bank or UPI details required for credit-information complaints).
- **Help › My complaints**: list with owner, tier chip and next-option date; case page with timeline, clocks, messages and tasks, **Reply**, **Escalate** (enabled when a timer or rejection allows; explain-why text when disabled), **Download case pack**, **Reopen**, **Rate**, **Withdraw**, **Add representative**; external route panel when open. Empty state: "No complaints. If something is wrong, tell us here."
- **Operations portal › Help centre** (C): article list by owner, state and review date; editor with sources and approver; RE-specific articles in **Lender portal › Help content** (D) for RE approval. Push carries no case content; deep links open the authenticated case page; portals show the same timeline with role-based redaction.

### Controls

- UB-C14: attachments only through the picker; no storage permission in the manifest (CI).
- UB-C15: the case pack generator never includes another borrower's data or the RE's internal notes.
- UB-C16: ratings are hidden from handling staff until closure.
- UB-C17: every help article has an owner, approver, source and review date before publication.

### Acceptance tests

- A borrower completes all 12 capabilities on Android, iOS and web with identical results.
- A reopened case keeps its ID, records a new RE receipt time and recomputes the external window.
- The case pack validates as PDF/A, contains the clock basis and hashes, and excludes RE internal notes.
- A Hindi-locale borrower sees the complaint form, case page and RB-IOS salient features in Hindi.
- A representative nominated by the borrower can view but cannot reply, withdraw or reopen.
- An article past its review date is excluded from AI answers.
- A one-star rating shows escalation options and no promotional content.

# PART 7D — FINANCIAL WELLNESS ADD-ONS (SEPARATE FROM LOANS)

**Purpose.** Offer consumers, whether or not they borrow through Udofin, three optional money tools: credit report and score tracking obtained as the consumer's own agent from a credit information company, an educational score simulator, and an expense tracker and budget planner fed only by data the consumer enters or uploads. Each tool sits outside every loan journey, in a separate data store under separate consent, and is never used for any credit decision or shared with any lender without fresh, explicit consent.

**Status and launch gate.** This Part is built behind the feature flag `addons.wellness` and stays **off in production** until FW4's legality gate is passed: an owner decision recorded in Appendix B, a written legal opinion on the CF para 10(4) and 14(1) questions below, and (for FW1) a signed CIC consumer-partner agreement. Charging for any tool needs a second, separate owner decision (FW4). The owner may decide that a separate group entity or brand runs these tools to keep the LSP clean; the design below works either way because the store, consents and billing are already separate.

**Extends, does not replace.** U25 (borrower dashboard): its "Personal expense tracking … [assess]" bullet is replaced by FW3. U6 (credit data) is unchanged and remains the only route for lender bureau pulls. Billing, plans and Razorpay are Part 7G (RV1–RV3); grievances are UB3 (consumer route).

**Applicability.** Individuals aged 18 or over (U3 age gate; DPDP s.9). Not offered to business entities, not configurable or visible by any RE, not part of any deal (UP2 section 12), not offered inside the assisted or field app.

**Codes used.** `CICRA` (Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005; CIC Regulations, 2006, regs 3 and 9; CIC Rules), CIR (for what lenders must do), CF paras 7(4), 10(4), 13(1), 14(1)–(4), AA para 8(12) and 28, `DPDP`, `CCPA-DP` (Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023, Annexure 1 list), `CCPA-MA` (Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements, 2022), `SEBI-IA` (SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 and the SEBI Board decision of 27 Jun 2024, PR 12/2024, on association with unregistered persons), RBC Second Amendment 2026 sales-practice paragraphs (NBFC version, effective 1 Jan 2027) applied by analogy [REC], Google Play India personal-loan and permissions policies. Labels: **[LAW]**, **[REG]**, **[INTERP]**, **[REC]**, **[MKT]**; unconfirmed items carry `[VERIFY: …]`. New controls are `FW-Cnn`.

**Data owned by Udofin, as Data Fiduciary in its own right.** The wellness account, wellness consents, credit reports and score history received as the consumer's agent, simulator scenarios the user saves, uploaded statements (until parsed), transactions, categories, budgets and alerts. Stored only in the separate `wellness` data store (FW4). **No RE-facing events exist for this data**; nothing in it is a loan record.

**Events.** None cross-product for wellness content. Subscription billing (if approved) runs in Udofin's own billing service on its own Razorpay account (Part 7G); its plan, entitlement, invoice and payment records are Udofin-internal and are not cross-product events. The Operations Hub receives only the monthly `UsageRecorded` with `meter_kind = REVENUE_AGGREGATE` per plan (subscriber count, gross, GST), with no subscriber key, borrower identity or wellness data (Integration Spec 6.27).

**Navigation.** "Money tools" is an area reached from **Account › Money tools** on channels A and B (and from a Home tile only for users who have opted in); it is never a tab inside the loan journey and never linked from Loans or Pay (navigation table in Part 7C). Submenus: **Credit health** (FW1), **Score simulator** (FW2), **Expenses and budgets** (FW3), **Privacy and data** (FW4).
