## FW1. Credit report and score tracking

### Legal route

| Question | Position | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Can Udofin pull bureau data in its own name? | No. Udofin is not a credit institution, cannot be a CIC member under CIR para 6, and is not a Specified User (that route serves credit institutions, with RBI's 2022 criteria) | [LAW] CICRA s.2(l); CIC Regulations reg 3 (as amended 2021); [REG] CIR paras 4(3), 6 |
| Lawful basis for a consumer product | The consumer obtains **their own** credit information; Udofin acts as the consumer's appointed agent under a CIC's direct-to-consumer partner programme, receiving the report solely to authenticate and display it to that consumer | [LAW] CIC Regulations reg 9 purpose "to know his own credit information" [VERIFY reg 9 text]; [MKT] TransUnion CIBIL DTC Consumer Connect partner model [VERIFY partner eligibility, audit and price terms for each CIC] |
| Can an RE's underwriting report feed this feature? | Never. RBI has told REs not to give unregulated entities access to credit information; an RE's CIR is for the RE's credit decision only | [REG] RBI instruction of 2019 [VERIFY circular reference]; CIR para 20 |
| Free annual report | Every individual may obtain one free full credit report, including the score, each calendar year from each CIC, electronically after authentication | [REG] RBI circular DBR.CID.BC.No.11/20.16.042/2016-17, 1 Sep 2016 |
| Limits on CIC partner channels | The RBI (Credit Information Companies) Directions, 2025 as amended by RBI/DOR/2025-26/119 (in force 1 Jul 2026) may restrict partner channels, refresh frequency or marketing use | [REG] CIC-AMD [VERIFY: read the consolidated text before contracting] |

### States

`credit_health_enrolment`: `NOT_ENROLLED → CONSENT_PENDING → IDENTITY_AUTHENTICATION (CIC's own knowledge-based questions or OTP) → ACTIVE → {EXPIRED | REVOKED} → PURGED`, with `AUTH_FAILED` (retry limits per the CIC) and `NO_HIT` (no credit file: plain explanation, free-report links, never "bad credit").

### Consent artefact (separate from every loan consent)

`wellness_consent` with: consent ID; the named CIC; purposes, each a separate choice: display to me, monitoring and alerts, educational analysis; **marketing use of my credit data** as a separate tick, default No and never pre-selected; refresh frequency and term (no longer than the CIC partner term, commonly up to 6 months [MKT]); retention (the shortest of the term, the purpose or withdrawal); withdrawal channel (one tap in settings); DPDP notice version (stand-alone, itemised: DPDP Rules r.3); language; timestamp, device and IP. Renewal requires a fresh consent and fresh CIC authentication.

### Capabilities

- **Pull:** on enrolment and at the refresh frequency the consent allows; each pull logs `cic_request_id`, CIC, purpose code, consent ID, cost and response hash; pulls above the plan's frequency are refused.
- **Display (per CIC, never combined):** the score with its date and range and the fixed line "Score provided by [CIC name]. Udofin does not calculate or change it"; accounts, enquiries and the DPD grid as the CIC returns them; the CIC's own factor descriptions. No "Udofin score", no average across CICs, no colour scale that implies approval.
- **Free-report links:** links to each of the four CICs' free annual report pages are always visible on every credit screen, including to paying users (FW-C03).
- **Disputes:** a deep link to the CIC's own dispute page and a plain explanation that the CIC and the lender have a combined 30 days, with ₹100 per day compensation after that (CIR para 35); for an error on an Udofin-sourced loan, a shortcut to a UB3 `credit_information` complaint routed to that RE. A dispute tracker records what the user filed and when (user-entered).
- **Alerts** (only with the monitoring purpose): new account, new enquiry, DPD change, score band change; push and SMS carry no figures or lender names, only "There is an update in your credit report".
- **Thin file and new to credit:** neutral education; never a suggestion to take a loan to "build credit".

### Storage and access

- Reports are stored only in `consumer_credit_vault` inside the wellness store (FW4): separate KMS key, field-level encryption for identifiers, raw CIC response encrypted at rest, India-only (CF para 14(4) by policy).
- Retention follows the consent and the CIC partner terms; a purge job deletes on expiry or withdrawal and writes a purge certificate.
- **No reader outside FW1 and FW2.** U6, U7, U8, U13, U16, U19 (except aggregate counts), U20, U21, Part 7A modules and every RE-facing API run under roles with no grant on the vault (FW4).
- No large-language-model processing of report content in v1.2 [REC]; explanations come from approved static content keyed to the CIC's factor codes.

### Billing hooks (only after FW4's charging gate)

Free tier: one refresh per quarter and the free-report links [REC]. Paid tier: monthly refresh, alerts, simulator, dispute tracker. Plans and payments are Part 7G; the CIC cost per pull is captured for unit economics.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refresh frequency | User (within plan and CIC terms) | Free: one per quarter; paid: monthly | Commercial within the CIC partner terms |
| Monitoring alerts | User | Off | Separate purpose; opt-in |
| Marketing use of credit data | User | No | Separate tick; never pre-selected |
| Alert content | Platform | "There is an update in your credit report" only | Fixed; no figures or lender names |
| Free-report links | Platform | Always shown | Fixed (FW-C03) |
| LLM processing of report content | Platform | Off | Fixed in v1.2 |
| Break-glass access to report content | Platform | Off; DPO approval per case | Logged and reported in the separation audit |

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Money tools › Credit health** (A, B): enrol wizard (FW4 opt-in) → choose CIC → CIC authentication → report; report screen per CIC (score card with date and range, accounts, enquiries, DPD grid, factor descriptions), free-report links, **Dispute with [CIC]** deep link, dispute tracker, alerts settings, **Stop tracking** (one tap). Empty state for `NO_HIT`: neutral education and free-report links. No loan call-to-action on any credit screen (FW-C05).
- **Operations portal › Money tools** (C): enrolment counts, pull failures, CIC cost; no report content.

### Controls

- FW-C01: the bureau adapter used by FW1 uses Udofin's consumer-partner credentials only and cannot be called with an RE's credentials; U6's adapter cannot be called from FW1 (separate service accounts; CI test).
- FW-C02: every pull has a live consent with the display purpose and a successful CIC authentication within the consent term.
- FW-C03: free-report links render on every credit screen for every plan.
- FW-C04: no screen, message or advertisement claims "credit repair", "guaranteed improvement" or a "Udofin score" (content linter; CCPA-MA).
- FW-C05: no loan offer, lender name or eligibility message appears on any FW1 or FW2 screen.

### Acceptance tests

- A pull attempted after consent withdrawal is refused and the report is purged within the retention rule.
- An RE credential cannot be loaded into the FW1 adapter configuration (validation error).
- The U7 routing service receives "permission denied" when querying `consumer_credit_vault` (CI test).
- The free-report links for all four CICs appear on the score screen for free and paid users.
- A `NO_HIT` user sees neutral education and no loan prompt.
- Alert payloads contain no score, amount or lender name.

## FW2. Score simulator (educational)

### Purpose and scope

Help users understand how common actions tend to affect credit scores, in direction and rough size, without predicting a score, guaranteeing an outcome or suggesting any lender's decision.

### Engine

- **Inputs:** the user's own FW1 report (if enrolled) or a hypothetical profile the user enters; what-if actions: pay down a card balance, reduce utilisation to a chosen percentage, avoid new enquiries for N months, keep old accounts open, miss a payment, settle instead of repaying in full, add a new loan.
- **Method:** a transparent, versioned factor table (payment history, utilisation, length of credit history, credit mix, recent enquiries, adverse statuses such as "settled") drawn from the CICs' own published consumer education material, with direction and band rules; or a licensed CIC simulator interface with the CIC's own disclaimers [VERIFY availability].
- **Output:** direction (likely to improve, likely to worsen, no material change expected) and a band (small, moderate, large), plus the factor that drives it and a time note (for example "late payments generally weigh less as they age"). **Never a numeric score, never a range of scores, never a probability of loan approval.**
- **Fixed label on every result:** "Illustrative estimate for education. Not a credit score. Actual scores are calculated only by credit information companies, using their own methods, and may move differently."
- **No AI generation** of results; the factor table is the only engine.

### Governance

- Factor-table versions approved by Udofin product and legal; reviewed every 6 months and when a CIC changes its published guidance [REC]; version shown on the result screen.
- Settled-account education states the CIR position plainly: a settlement is reported as "settled" (CIR para 12(4)), which generally weighs against the borrower.
- Saved scenarios are stored only if the user saves them; otherwise runs are ephemeral and logged without inputs.

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Money tools › Score simulator** (A, B), also reachable from Credit health: choose "my report" (if enrolled) or "a sample profile"; pick what-if actions as cards; result card (direction, band, driver, time note, locked label, factor-table version); **Save scenario** (only on request). Works for non-enrolled users. No link from the simulator to loan offers.
- Settings: none user-facing beyond saving scenarios; the factor table is a governed platform setting (version, approver, review date).

### Controls

- FW-C06: the result component cannot render a numeric score (unit and snapshot tests).
- FW-C07: the label text is a locked string; changes need legal approval.
- FW-C08: the simulator has no access to U6 bureau data, RE decisions or offers.

### Acceptance tests

- Every result shows direction, band, driver and the fixed label, and no number.
- "Miss a payment" never shows "no material change".
- A user with no FW1 report can run the simulator on a hypothetical profile.
- No result screen contains a lender name, an offer or the words "approved" or "eligible".
- Changing the factor table creates a new version shown on results; old saved scenarios keep their version.

## FW3. Expense tracker and budget planner

### Purpose and scope

Let users record and understand their own spending and set budgets, using only data they type, upload or choose to link from their own Udofin loan records, without device scraping, bank credentials or Account Aggregator access in Udofin's name, and without investment or credit advice.

### Data sources

| Source | Status | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Manual entry | Allowed | Amount, date, category, note, payment mode |
| Statement upload (PDF, CSV, XLS, XLSX) | Allowed | Chosen through the Android Storage Access Framework or photo picker and the iOS document picker, which need no storage permission (Part 4.5; CF para 13(1)); password for a protected PDF used in memory only, never stored or logged; parsed in India; raw file deleted after parsing (default immediately; the user may choose to keep it up to 30 days [REC]) |
| CSV import (Udofin template or bank export) | Allowed | Column mapping screen; preview before import |
| The user's own Udofin loan EMIs | Allowed behind a toggle | Read-only projection of EMI amount and due date from U25 into the wellness store; never the reverse direction [INTERP: showing the borrower their own loan data] |
| SMS inbox reading, notification listener, accessibility-service scraping | **Blocked** | CF para 13(1) "telephony functions"; Google Play permissions policy; Part 4.5 |
| Contacts, call logs, media library | **Blocked** | CF para 13(1) |
| Net-banking or card credentials, screen scraping, email-inbox scraping | **Blocked** | Security and DPDP minimisation [REC] |
| UPI app transaction history | **Blocked** | Udofin is not a TPAP [REC] |
| Account Aggregator with Udofin as FIU | **Blocked** | An FIU must be regulated by a financial-sector regulator (AA para 8(12)); data use only as the consent artefact allows (AA para 28) |
| Account Aggregator through an RE or a regulated partner FIU running its own personal-finance service, with Udofin as technology service provider | **Not in v1.2; gated** | Needs a regulated FIU partner, a consent artefact naming that FIU and purpose, and a legal opinion; RE lending data is never reused for it [VERIFY: ReBIT purpose codes and RBI's view] |

### Pipeline

`upload → malware scan → parse (bank template, then generic parser) → normalise (date, amount, debit or credit, narration) → categorise (rules, then model suggestion, always user-editable) → de-duplicate (hash of date, amount and normalised narration within the account) → budgets and alerts`. Parse failures show what failed and offer CSV mapping; nothing is silently dropped.

### Categories, budgets and alerts

- **Default categories:** income; housing and rent; utilities; groceries; transport and fuel; health; education; EMIs and loan repayments; insurance premiums; savings and investments (shown as transfers only); shopping; dining and entertainment; transfers between own accounts; cash withdrawals; fees and charges; other. Users may rename, merge, add, split transactions and create their own rules.
- **Budgets:** monthly envelopes per category; optional roll-over; simple savings targets (a goal amount and date, with no product suggestion).
- **Alerts:** at 80% and 100% of a budget [REC], large-transaction and recurring-charge detection; push carries no amounts unless the user turns that on.
- **Insights:** descriptive only: month-on-month changes, top categories, recurring payments found. Obligations-to-income is shown as "Your recorded EMIs are ₹X, which is Y% of the income you recorded. Lenders decide eligibility using their own assessment." **Never** "you can afford a loan of ₹X", never a loan, card or product suggestion, never a lender name.

### No investment, insurance or credit advice

- No recommendation of securities, mutual funds, insurance or any financial product, and no return or performance claims (SEBI-IA; SEBI PR 12/2024; IRDAI rules on solicitation through unregistered persons [VERIFY]).
- Educational articles are generic, labelled "general information, not advice", and approved through the UB4 content model.
- Spending data never triggers a loan offer, a marketing message for credit, or a nudge into a loan journey (FW4).

### Retention and export

- Transactions are kept until the user deletes them, or deleted 12 months after the last activity with a notice at least 30 days before [REC; DPDP s.8(7)].
- Export as CSV and JSON with a README and manifest (the UB1 package format, as a separate wellness package).
- One-tap "delete all money-tools data" (FW4).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep raw uploaded file | User | Delete immediately after parsing | User may choose up to 30 days [REC] |
| EMI projection from own Udofin loans | User | Off | Opt-in toggle; one direction only |
| Budget alert thresholds | User | 80% and 100% | User may change |
| Amounts in push notifications | User | Off | Opt-in |
| Inactivity deletion | Platform | 12 months after last activity, 30 days' notice | Floor [REC] |
| SMS reading, notification listener, accessibility scraping, AA as FIU | Platform | None exist | Hard block (CF para 13(1); AA para 8(12)) |

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Money tools › Expenses and budgets** (A, B): tabs **Transactions** (list with filters by month, category and account; bulk **Re-categorise**, **Split**, **Delete**), **Budgets** (envelopes with progress bars and roll-over), **Insights** (descriptive only), **Import** (statement upload through the system picker or the web file input → password prompt if needed → parse → preview → confirm; CSV column mapping). Parse errors name the failing rows and offer CSV mapping; nothing is silently dropped. No background processing on the device beyond the upload itself.
- **Operations portal** (C): parser success rates; failure samples only after the user consents to share a failed file for support [REC].

### Controls

- FW-C09: the CI manifest gate (Part 8A, REQ-CF-13(1)) rejects any SMS, notification-listener, accessibility-service or storage permission added for FW3.
- FW-C10: statement passwords never reach logs, crash reports or persistent storage (log-scrubbing test).
- FW-C11: raw uploaded files are deleted within the chosen period; a daily job verifies and reports exceptions.
- FW-C12: the insight generator's output passes a content linter that rejects product names, lender names, "afford a loan" phrasing and return claims.

### Acceptance tests

- A password-protected PDF statement parses correctly and the password appears nowhere in logs or the database.
- Uploading the same statement twice creates no duplicate transactions.
- The Android build contains no `READ_SMS`, `RECEIVE_SMS`, `BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE`, `BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE`, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` or `READ_MEDIA_*` permission.
- Turning off the EMI toggle removes the EMI projection from the wellness store within 24 hours.
- An 80% budget alert fires once per category per month.
- No insight or alert text contains a lender name, a loan offer or an investment suggestion (linter test over the template set).

## FW4. Separation, consent and data controls for add-ons

### Purpose and scope

Make the separation between the money tools and Udofin's LSP business structural, provable and permanent; set the legality gate for launching and for charging; and ban the sales-practice patterns that would turn a wellness tool into a lending funnel.

### Legality gate

| Gate | Needed for | Evidence (`addon_legality_decision`) |
|---|---|---|
| G1 Owner decision to offer the tools at all, and through which entity or brand | Any production use, free or paid | Owner decision record (Appendix B) with date and approver |
| G2 Legal opinion | Any production use | Written opinion covering: whether CF para 10(4) ("fees, charges … payable to LSP … are not charged to or collected from the borrowers separately by LSP") reaches a non-loan subscription sold by an LSP to borrowers and non-borrowers alike [INTERP: the paragraph addresses fees for lending services; RBI may read it widely]; whether wellness data is "data … within the scope of the NBFC-LSP agreement" under CF para 14(1); CIC partner terms; DPDP; consumer-protection and e-commerce rules [VERIFY applicability of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020]; insurance and investment solicitation limits |
| G3 CIC consumer-partner agreement | FW1 and FW2 on real reports | Signed agreement, partner audit obligations, refresh and storage terms |
| G4 Separate owner decision to charge | Any paid plan | Owner decision plus G2 opinion addendum on pricing; plans published through Part 7G with the RV1 legality gate |
| G5 Re-review | Every 12 months and on any change to CF, the RBC sales-practice paragraphs, CIC Directions or DPDP Rules | Updated record; the flag turns off automatically if the review lapses |

### Structural separation

- **Separate store:** the `wellness` database (or a separate schema in its own cluster) with its own KMS key, its own service accounts, its own backups and its own retention jobs; no foreign keys into loan tables, only the borrower account ID.
- **Separate consents and notices:** each tool has its own stand-alone DPDP notice and consent artefacts (DPDP s.5–6; Rules r.3), never bundled with platform, loan, bureau, AA or marketing consents; every choice defaults to No; withdrawal is one tap and as easy as giving consent (RBC Second Amendment sales-practice paragraphs on default-No consent and easy unsubscribing, applied by analogy [REC; VERIFY final NBFC paragraph numbers]).
- **Separate navigation:** "Money tools" is its own area; no money-tools card, banner or prompt appears inside any loan application, offer view, KFS, execution, disbursal, repayment, overdue, settlement or grievance screen.
- **Separate support and complaints:** UB3 subscription route (Udofin GRO → National Consumer Helpline → consumer commission); never routed to any RE.
- **Separate export and deletion:** UB1 wellness package; one-tap delete-all with purge within 30 days [REC] and a confirmation receipt.

### Opt-in and withdrawal workflow

`wellness_optin` per tool: `NOT_OFFERED → INTRO_SHOWN → NOTICE_SHOWN → CONSENTED → ACTIVE → {PAUSED | WITHDRAWN} → PURGED`, with `DECLINED` (no re-prompt for 90 days [REC]).

| Step | Screen and rule |
|---|---|
| Intro | Who runs the tool (Udofin or the separate entity chosen under G1), what it does and does not do, "this is not part of any loan and no lender will see it"; **Not now** and **Continue** with equal weight |
| Notice | Stand-alone DPDP notice for that tool (Rules r.3), itemised, in the chosen language, with the withdrawal route |
| Consent | One screen per tool; each purpose a separate switch, all off by default; marketing use a separate tick; consent is recorded only on an explicit **Agree** (no scroll-to-accept, no pre-ticks); a loan consent can never be reused or bundled |
| Activation | FW1 needs CIC authentication; FW3 needs a first entry or upload; FW2 needs nothing |
| Pause | Stops pulls, alerts and imports; data kept; resume is one tap |
| Withdrawal | One tap in **Account › Money tools › Privacy and data**; processing stops at once, purge per the retention rule (within 30 days for delete-all) and a receipt is sent; the loan account is untouched |
| Renewal | At term end a fresh consent and, for FW1, fresh CIC authentication; no silent extension |

### Usage bans (hard-coded, not configurable)

Wellness data is never:

1. an input to matching, ranking, pre-qualification, eligibility, pricing, underwriting or limit decisions (CF para 7(4) neutrality; CF para 8; Part 4.6);
2. sent to any RE or lender, or used in any RE-facing report, event, export pack (UP3) or dashboard, except on the user's fresh, explicit, item-level consent naming the RE, for a stated purpose, recorded as a separate artefact (CF para 13(4)) — and in v1.2 the only such flow is the user downloading their own report or statement and choosing to attach it to an application as a supporting document;
3. used for collections, recovery, contact policy, hardship assessment or risk signals to REs (Part 7A; U24 sends no wellness-derived signal);
4. used to target advertising or promotions for credit products; any non-credit promotion using wellness data needs a separate, specific marketing consent, default No [REC];
5. used to train models outside the wellness tools without separate consent [REC];
6. read by AI services other than the wellness tools' own approved components (U20 inventory entry required).

### Subscription rules (if G4 is passed)

- Open to borrowers and non-borrowers at the **same price**; never a condition of, discount on, or benefit tied to any loan; never mentioned in any KFS, offer or loan communication.
- Never funded from a loan, added to a loan amount, deducted from a disbursal or collected through a loan mandate or an RE's merchant account (CF para 10; RBC Second Amendment rule against loan-funding add-ons without explicit consent, applied as an absolute ban [REC]).
- Paid only to Udofin's own merchant account with a descriptor distinct from any RE (Part 7G RV3); e-mandate or UPI AutoPay renewals follow the RBI E-mandate Directions, 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396): pre-debit notice at least 24 hours before each debit, no additional factor of authentication up to ₹15,000 per debit, opt-out at any time, and no charge to the customer for the mandate.
- No RE earns, pays or sees anything about the subscription.
- GST invoice for every charge and credit note for every refund (UB1 lists them).

### Dark-pattern ban and UI audit

Every money-tools screen and every billing screen is audited before each release against the CCPA-DP specified patterns: false urgency, basket sneaking, confirm shaming, forced action, subscription trap, interface interference, bait and switch, drip pricing, disguised advertisement, nagging, trick question, SaaS billing and rogue malware [VERIFY: current Annexure 1 list]. Specific rules:

- price including GST shown before any commitment; no hidden renewals; no pre-ticked boxes;
- cancellation from Settings in at most two taps, with no retention offer blocking the confirm button;
- a free trial converts to paid only on an explicit confirmation at the end of the trial [REC]; renewal reminder at least 7 days before each annual renewal [REC];
- no countdown timers, scarcity claims or "most users choose" nudges;
- declining a tool never degrades the loan journey or the free tier;
- advertisements, if any (Part 7G RV4), are labelled and never placed in credit or loan flows (CF para 7(4)).

### Separation audit and evidence

- **Quarterly separation audit:** database access logs prove that no service outside the wellness tools read the wellness store; any finding is a severity-2 incident [REC].
- **Results** go to Udofin's compliance committee and into the UP1 due-diligence pack as a declaration that add-ons are separate and that no RE data feeds them.
- **Breach handling** for the wellness store follows DPDP Rules r.7 with Udofin as fiduciary (U24).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addons.wellness` | Platform (production) | Off | Cannot be enabled while G1 or G2 is missing or G5 has lapsed; FW1 and FW2 also need G3 (FW-C13) |
| Paid plans | Platform | Off | Need G4 and an ACTIVE S09 stream (RV1) |
| Each consent purpose | User | No | Regulatory floor (default No; DPDP; RBC Second Amendment applied by analogy) |
| Re-prompt after decline | Platform | 90 days | Commercial [REC]; never inside a loan screen |
| Delete-all purge | Platform | Within 30 days | Floor [REC] |
| Separation audit | Platform | Quarterly | Tighten only |
| RE access, sponsorship or configuration | Deal | None exists | Hard block (UP2 section 12) |

### Menu and screens

- **Account › Money tools** (A, B): landing with the three tools, each showing status (not started, active, paused) and **Start** or **Open**; the opt-in wizard above.
- **Account › Money tools › Privacy and data**: consents per tool with **Withdraw**, data held, **Export** (separate wellness package), **Delete all**, purge receipts. Billing pages are **Account › Plans and billing** (Part 7G RV2.3).
- **Operations portal › Money tools governance** (C; compliance and DPO): legality-gate status G1–G5 with evidence and review dates, separation-audit results, dark-pattern audit status per release, purge certificates; no content.

### Controls

- FW-C13: `addons.wellness` cannot be enabled in production while G1 or G2 is missing or G5 has lapsed; FW1 and FW2 on real reports also need G3 (otherwise they run only against a CIC sandbox); paid plans cannot be published while G4 is missing.
- FW-C14: database roles for U6, U7, U8, U13, U16, U19, U20, U21, U24 and every RE-facing API have no grant on the wellness store (CI test enumerates roles).
- FW-C15: the event catalogue contains no event with a wellness data class; schema registry rejects one.
- FW-C16: a release is blocked if the dark-pattern UI audit has open critical findings.
- FW-C17: a money-tools component placed in a loan-journey UI slot fails the build (slot allow-list).

### Acceptance tests

- With G2 missing, enabling `addons.wellness` in production fails and logs the reason.
- Enumerating database grants shows no non-wellness role with access to the wellness store.
- A synthetic attempt by the routing service to read wellness data is denied and raises a severity-2 alert.
- A subscriber and a non-subscriber with identical loan requests receive identical offer sets and order.
- Cancelling a subscription takes at most two taps from Settings and sends a confirmation; no further charge occurs.
- No loan screen (application, offer, KFS, repayment, overdue) renders any money-tools element.
- Delete-all removes credit reports, transactions, budgets and scenarios within 30 days and issues a receipt; the loan export and loan records are unaffected.
- A subscription payment can never be routed to an RE merchant account or a loan mandate (configuration-validator test).
- Opting into the expense tracker creates no FW1 consent; withdrawing the FW1 consent stops pulls immediately and leaves FW3 data untouched; the consent screen has every switch off on first render.
- No event or `UsageRecorded` statement sent to the Operations Hub contains a subscriber key or wellness data (schema test).

# PART 7E — MEMBER AND GROUP LENDING: CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES AND MICROFINANCE

**Purpose.** This Part specifies the borrower-side and assisted-channel journeys for two lending models that do not fit the individual, app-first journey of Parts 3 and 6: (1) **credit co-operative societies** lending to their own members, where the society is a non-RE lender onboarded under the non-RE lender track (Part 7B UP4); and (2) **microfinance group lending** (joint liability groups and self-help groups) by partner REs. Udofin supplies the member and group experience, the assisted and offline-capable field tooling, and evidence. The lender decides membership, share linkage, sureties, group recognition, credit, pricing and collections posting, and keeps the ledger. The lender-side counterparts are Finbyx Part 7G (IP2 credit co-operative societies; IP4 microfinance JLG and SHG lifecycle); where the lender is on another system, the same contract applies through the connector framework (Part 5.3).

**Applicability.**

| Lender type | MG1 | MG2 | MG3 | MG4 | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Credit co-operative society, State Act (non-RE) | Yes | Only if its by-laws permit group lending [VERIFY per Act] | Only as an SHG-linkage lender where its by-laws permit | Yes | Part 7B UP4 contract; SCS rule pack |
| Multi-State credit co-operative society (MSCS Act 2002, non-RE) | Yes | As above | As above | Yes | Part 7B UP4 contract; MSCS rule pack |
| NBFC-MFI | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | CF Ch V; RBC Section H; MFI; SRO code |
| NBFC (BL, ML, UL) lending microfinance loans | No | Yes, within the 25% cap (MFI para 49) | Yes | Yes | CF Ch V; RBC Section H |
| Bank or SFB (SHG-Bank Linkage, JLG) | No | Yes [VERIFY: bank CF and RBC equivalents before onboarding] | Yes | Yes | Bank Directions not in docs/regulations/rbi/ (Part 4.1) |
| UCB, StCB, DCCB | No (they are banks, not societies; onboard as REs under Part 7B UP1) | [VERIFY: co-operative bank microfinance rules] | [VERIFY] | Yes | Part 4.1 |

**Codes used.** RBI: CF, RBC, MFI, CIR, KYC, OUT, TDCR. Non-RBI (codes as Finbyx Part 8A.37): `MSCS` (Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act 2002 and Rules 2023), `SCS` (State co-operative societies Acts and rules, one rule pack per State), `CICRA`, `DPDP`, `TRAI`. Self-regulatory: `MFIN` (MFIN Guardrails 2.0, Directive 14 of 25 Nov 2024; still current per CARE Ratings, Aug 2026). New requirement IDs follow the existing pattern, for example `REQ-MSCS-67`, `REQ-SCS-MH-144-5A`, `REQ-MFIN-GR2-1`.

**Data owned.** Udofin is the system of record for: membership-application and group-journey state in its channels; consent artefacts (borrower, surety, group member); assisted-session evidence; meeting attendance and training-attendance captures made in Udofin channels; collection receipts as issued through Udofin tooling (evidence copy); low-literacy consent evidence; and its own grievance tickets. The lender (society or RE) is the system of record for: the member register and class, admission decisions, share ledger, surety acceptance, group and centre recognition, household-income assessment and the 50% decision, credit decision, loan card, loan ledger, collection posting and the cash-in-transit ledger. Udofin holds labelled projections of the lender's data only within the agreement's minimal data set (CF para 14(1)).

**Non-negotiables for this Part (fail closed).**

1. **Udofin never takes, lists, markets, quotes rates for or displays the opening of deposits** for any lender, member class or product. There is no deposit journey in Udofin in any version (`REQ-MSCS-67`; `REQ-SCS-MH-144-5A`; BUDS Act First Schedule items 4(i) and 8; RBI press release 2021-22/1230, 22 Nov 2021).
2. **Udofin never holds cash or funds.** Repayments, share money and any member payment go to the lender's own bank account (CF para 10(1)–(4); mirrored by contract for societies, Part 7B UP4).
3. **No borrower-paid Udofin fee** on any member or group loan (CF para 10(4); mirrored by contract for societies).
4. **Joint liability is voluntary peer support only.** Udofin never debits, nets, cross-posts or demands one member's money for another member's dues.
5. **No co-lending, split routing or loan sale between a society or co-operative bank and an NBFC** (TDCR paras 12(4) proviso and 97). Parallel independent loans with aggregated affordability are not co-lending and are shown as separate loans.
6. **Regulated decisions are the lender's** (OUT para 15; KYC para 13): admission, share linkage, surety acceptance, group recognition, GRT outcome, sanction, pricing, collection posting.

## MG1. Co-operative society member journeys

### MG1.1 What binds Udofin

| Rule | Source | Effect on Udofin |
|---|---|---|
| A credit co-operative society is not an RBI RE; RBI digital-lending Directions do not bind it; Udofin applies RE-equivalent conduct by contract | [INTERP] RBI press release 22 Nov 2021; TDCR para 97 | UP4 deal clauses; enforced in MG1 journeys |
| No "bank", "banker" or "banking" in a society's name (from 29 Sep 2020) | [LAW] BR Act s.7 read with s.56 | Onboarding blocked in UP4; no "bank" label anywhere |
| MSCS deposits only from voting members; deposits from non-voting, nominal or associate members are unlicensed banking and not DICGC-covered; Maharashtra societies take no deposits from non-members | [LAW] MSCS s.67; MH MCS Act s.144-5A [VERIFY: Ch XI-1A text]; [REG] RBI press release 22 Nov 2021 | No deposit feature at all (non-negotiable 1) |
| No loan on the security of the member's own shares or of a non-member | [LAW] MSCS s.66(1) | Shares never described as security; non-member sureties shown as refused |
| Admission decided within 4 months and communicated within 15 days, else deemed refused; nominal and associate members have no vote and borrow only as by-laws allow | [LAW] MSCS ss.25(4), 26; MH MCS Act ss.2(19), 24(2) | Admission timer; class flags drive the journey (MG1.3) |
| Member disputes go to statutory forums (MSCS arbitrator appointed by the Central Registrar; Maharashtra Co-operative Court); Co-operative Ombudsman for MSCS members | [LAW] MSCS ss.84, 85A [VERIFY: text]; MH MCS Act s.91(3) | Equator gate and grievance tiers (MG1.9) |
| Coercive-action provisions apply to societies operating in Tamil Nadu; money-lending Acts exclude society loans in Maharashtra and Karnataka | [LAW] TN Act 40 of 2025 ss.2, 20; MH Money-Lending Act 2014 s.2(13)(e); KA Act 15 of 2025 s.1(3) [VERIFY: other States; KA platform-registration limb for Udofin] | State overlays (MG1.8) |

### MG1.2 Entry, lender card and the separate member space

- **Separate space, not the RE offer view.** A society's products appear only in a "Your co-operative society" space for its verified members, never inside the CF para 7 multi-lender offer view: the society is a different regime and member-only, and mixing it in would imply RBI regulation [REC; legal opinion in the regulatory register].
- **Lender card** (fixed component; legal-review configuration; cannot be themed away): society name; Act and State; Registrar; registration number; area of operation; audit class and year where the pack publishes one; and the fixed lines "This society is a co-operative society. It is not regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. Udofin is a technology platform used by the society and is not a lender."
- **Never** show RBI logos, CIMS references, "RBI-registered", "bank" or "banking" for a society.
- **Entry routes:** society deep link or QR; the society's branch in assisted mode (MG4); search inside Udofin, shown only to declared residents of the area of operation, unranked [REC].

### MG1.3 Membership verification and admission

**Verification against the register (before any loan journey opens).**

1. Borrower selects the society and gives a consent artefact naming the society and the purpose "membership verification".
2. Udofin calls `GET /v1/societies/{id}/members/{ref}` (Integration Spec 6.24; served by Finbyx IP2 or the society's certified system, or answered by society staff in the lender-portal verification queue) with the membership number plus a matching factor (mobile on record or date of birth) and the `consentref`. Udofin never bulk-downloads the register.
3. Response: `member_status` (ACTIVE, DEFAULTER, RESIGNED, EXPELLED, DECEASED; HTTP 404 is shown as "not found"), `member_class` (ORDINARY_VOTING, NOMINAL, ASSOCIATE, NON_VOTING_SHAREHOLDER, INSTITUTIONAL), `can_borrow`, `can_stand_surety` and KYC status. Udofin stores the response hash, reference and time only.
4. Only `ACTIVE` members with `can_borrow = true` reach the loan journey; a `DEFAULTER` sees "Please contact your society" with the society's contact and grievance block.

**Admission journey (non-members).**

- States: `INTEREST → APPLICATION_DRAFT → SUBMITTED_TO_SOCIETY → UNDER_SCRUTINY → {ADMITTED, REJECTED, DEEMED_REFUSED} → SHARE_MONEY_PENDING → MEMBER_ACTIVE`. Submission is `POST /v1/societies/{id}/membership-applications` with an Idempotency-Key (acknowledgement within 5 minutes; Integration Spec 6.24); a resubmission with the same key returns the original application; an unacknowledged submission retries with back-off for 24 hours, then shows "the society has not confirmed receipt" with the society's contact, and the statutory timer runs from the society's acknowledgement.
- Capture only what the society's admission form requires (U2): identity and address through Aadhaar offline XML or DigiLocker (never the full number; societies are not notified under PML Act s.11A [VERIFY]), residence in the area of operation, occupation, nominee, the Maharashtra Rule 45 one-credit-society declaration where that pack applies, and the by-law acknowledgement. The society's board or delegated officer decides; Udofin shows status only.
- **Timer:** MSCS 4 months to decide plus 15 days to communicate (`REQ-MSCS-25-4`); State timers from the SCS pack. At expiry Udofin shows "deemed refused under [section]" with the grievance route and flags the society.
- **Admission fee and share money** go only to the society's own account (merchant account or VPA; validator as Part 4.3); "payment initiated" until `ShareCapitalPosted`; the receipt is the society's. `MemberAdmitted` opens the member card and, if the class can borrow, the loan space.

### MG1.4 Share-capital linkage and sureties (society decisions)

- **Share linkage.** The society's system computes any top-up required by its by-laws (for example `ceil(loan × link% ÷ face value) − shares held`, Finbyx IP2) and returns it with the eligibility response. Udofin displays the figure, the by-law reference and two options the society permits: pay the top-up to the society's account before disbursal, or have it deducted from the disbursal **only** where the society allows it and the deduction is shown in the society's loan fact sheet and accepted by the member [REC]. Udofin never finances share purchase (CRCS model bye-laws cl.58(b)) and never describes shares as security (MSCS s.66(1)).
- **Sureties.** The member nominates sureties by membership number. Each surety receives an invitation on **their own** device (SMS on the society's DLT header with a one-time link) and gives a separate consent artefact: the loan, amount, tenor, the surety's liability as stated in the society's surety bond, and the right to decline. The society validates each surety (active, non-defaulter, within its per-surety limit) and accepts or rejects; Udofin shows the outcome only. A surety's acceptance evidence (OTP, timestamp, document hash of the bond as shown) is passed to the society.
- **Director and relative borrowers.** Where the society flags the borrower as a director or relative, the journey shows that the loan needs the society's recusal and disclosure process (MSCS s.39(3); CRCS model bye-laws cl.44) and waits for the society's decision.

### MG1.5 Member loan journey

1. Product choice from the society's published member products (U2 product-offer versions from the society; the configuration validator rejects deposit products, products named "bank", borrower-paid Udofin fees and any payment beneficiary other than the society or the member).
2. Data capture as the product template requires; household composition and income for every collateral-free loan, so the society can apply the CF para 51 test and the 50% cap as policy [REC; CF does not bind societies].
3. Eligibility response from the society (including share-linkage and surety requirements).
4. **Loan fact sheet** issued by the society (RE-equivalent of the KFS by contract): amount, tenor, rate type, all charges, APR computed the RBC Annex I way, repayment schedule, share-linkage and surety requirements, recovery forum, grievance route and the lender card lines. Udofin's independent APR check (U8) applies. Acknowledgement and acceptance recorded as for a KFS.
5. Execution: agreement with eSign where the society accepts electronic execution; a physical-execution hand-off where the State Act or the society requires wet signatures or a charge on land (for example MH MCS Act s.48) [VERIFY per State].
6. **Cooling-off** of at least one day adopted by contract (mirrors CF para 11) [REC].
7. Disbursal from the society's account to the member's own bank account only; status from the society's event.
8. Servicing in U12 and U25 from the society's events; the society's statements and certificates appear in My documents (Part 7C UB1).

### MG1.6 What Udofin never offers for a society

- No deposit opening, top-up, renewal, rate card, interest calculator, maturity reminder, "invest with your society" message or referral reward for deposits.
- No display of deposit balances, including deposits held as security; a loan against a deposit shows only the society's security reference in its loan fact sheet [REC].
- No marketing of membership to non-residents of the area of operation; no agent incentives for admissions.
- Templates containing deposit vocabulary ("FD", "RD", "deposit", "interest on savings") are rejected by the template linter for society tenants.

### MG1.7 Repayments, consent and data

- Repayments only to the society's account: eNACH or UPI AutoPay in the society's favour on its sponsor bank, UPI intent or QR on the society's merchant account, or a salary-deduction mandate where the society is a salary-earners' society and the employer pays the society directly [VERIFY: MH MCS Act s.49]. No Udofin collection account, no netting, no pass-through.
- Cash at the society's branch or by the society's staff is the society's process; Udofin records receipts only through MG4 tooling.
- Consent artefacts per purpose: membership verification, admission, KYC, bureau (only if the society is a CIC member; otherwise declarations, [VERIFY: CICRA status of credit societies]), loan application, surety, contact, Equator conciliation. Vernacular DPDP notices; withdrawal as easy as consent.
- The society's contact for data-principal requests is shown; Udofin forwards loan-data requests to the society (`DataPrincipalRequest`).

### MG1.8 State-law conduct (rule packs)

- **Rule pack key:** (Act, State, effective date). Packs ship for MSCS and Maharashtra; Rajasthan and Karnataka (KCS Act 1959 and Souharda Act 1997) next; other States as stubs completed at onboarding with counsel's review (Finbyx IP2 owns the full lender-side pack; Udofin consumes the conduct and disclosure fields).
- **Fields Udofin uses:** member classes and rights; admission timer; deposit-solicitation ban (always true); disclosure strings; contact windows; coercion overlay; dispute forum; recovery route label; grievance tiers; language requirements.
- **Contact windows** (enforced by `canContact`, Part 7A UR4): 09:00–18:00 for collateral-free loans to households with income up to ₹3,00,000; 08:00–19:00 for other loans; the borrower's preference narrows the window [REC; mirrors RBC paras 91(2) and 100 by contract, the same windows as Finbyx IP2.12]; from 1 Jan 2027 the contract adopts the RBC Third Amendment rule pack (pack B, Part 7A.0.4) and the society may only tighten it.
- **Coercion overlays:** Tamil Nadu Act 40 of 2025 s.20 for societies operating in Tamil Nadu (no following, frequenting home or work, seizing documents or belongings, or undue influence through agencies); every field event carries the checklist (MG4). Karnataka Act 15 of 2025 exempts KCS and Souharda societies; whether it binds an MSCS operating in Karnataka is open [VERIFY].
- **Never in any society communication:** threats of police action, public naming, contact with family or employer, statements that the society is a bank or RBI-regulated.

### MG1.9 Disputes, grievances and Equator

- **Grievance tiers for society members** (displayed in UB3, Part 7C): Udofin nodal grievance officer for platform matters → the society's grievance officer → the society's board → Registrar (State RCS or Central Registrar for MSCS) or the Co-operative Ombudsman for MSCS members (MSCS s.85A) → consumer commission or statutory forum. The RBI Ombudsman route is **not** shown for a society, because the society is outside RB-IOS 2026; showing it would mislead.
- **Equator gate.** Private arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 is **blocked** for disputes that the society's Act sends to a statutory forum (MSCS s.84; MH MCS Act s.91). Udofin shows Equator **conciliation only**, only where (a) the society refers the case, (b) the member gives written post-dispute consent, and (c) the society's rule pack records counsel's confirmation that conciliation is not barred by the State Act. Any settlement is filed before the statutory forum where the pack requires it. The borrower is told that Equator and Udofin are both Infrabyx group products (Integration Specification Part 8.6).
- **Recovery certificates and awards** (MH MCS Act s.101 certificate; Co-operative Court awards; MSCS arbitral awards) are the society's instruments. Udofin shows them only under the society's visibility policy (Part 7A UR3) and never issues or relays a demand in its own name.

### MG1.10 Events and APIs

- **Consumed:** `MemberAdmitted`, `ShareCapitalPosted` (society system → Udofin), `ProductCatalogPublished`, `LoanDisbursed`, `PaymentReceived`, `GrievanceUpdated`.
- **Produced:** `ConsentRecorded`, `ApplicationSubmitted` (with `lender_type = NON_RE_SOCIETY`; Integration Spec 6.24), `GrievanceRaised`.
- **APIs (synchronous; Integration Spec 6.24):** `GET /v1/societies/{id}/members/{ref}` (membership verification before any loan screen; p95 ≤ 800 ms) and `POST /v1/societies/{id}/membership-applications` (KYC evidence references without the Aadhaar number, area-of-operation proof, nominee, declared other-society borrowings, `consentref`), both served by the society's system of record. Status changes after admission reach Udofin only through the verification API, which Udofin calls again before each new loan application.

### Settings and options (MG1)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rule pack | Society | MSCS or the State pack | Per (Act, State, effective date) |
| Admission timer | Pack | MSCS 4 months + 15 days | Statutory; per State pack |
| Share top-up mode | Product | Pay before disbursal | Deduction from disbursal only where the society allows and the member accepts |
| Surety invitation expiry | Society | 7 days [REC] | Commercial |
| Contact windows | Product | MG1.8 windows | Tighten only |
| Deposit features, "bank" vocabulary | Tenant class | None exist | Hard block |
| Channels | Society | Web/PWA and assisted | Fixed until app-store policy is confirmed |

### Menu and screens (MG1)

- **Loans › Your society** (B, and assisted on E): society picker (deep link, QR or area search) → **Verify membership** → member card (class, status, share holding as the society reports) → products → application → loan fact sheet → execution; for non-members **Apply for membership** wizard (consent → KYC by offline XML or DigiLocker → area proof → nominee → declarations → submit) with a status page and deemed-refusal countdown; **Sureties** screen with invitation status per surety.
- **Lender portal › Partners › Members** (D, society staff): see UP4.

### Acceptance tests

- A non-member, a `NOMINAL` member whose class cannot borrow and a `DEFAULTER` cannot reach any loan screen; each sees the correct message and the society's contact.
- The membership timer for an MSCS society shows "deemed refused" 4 months and 15 days after submission without a society decision and raises a compliance flag.
- Share money and a repayment can only be initiated to the society's own account; configuring a Udofin or third-party beneficiary fails validation.
- No screen, template, push or SMS for a society tenant contains deposit vocabulary; the template linter rejects "FD", "RD" and "deposit" for society tenants; there is no deposit API route.
- A society product never appears in the RE multi-lender offer view; the lender card text cannot be removed by theming.
- A surety's consent can only be given on the surety's own device; an agent session cannot submit it.
- The RBI Ombudsman route is never shown on a society grievance; the Co-operative Ombudsman appears only for MSCS members.
- An Equator arbitration request on a society dispute is refused; conciliation is offered only when all three conditions in MG1.9 are recorded.
- A co-lending or split-loan route between a society and an NBFC cannot be configured; a parallel NBFC loan to the same member is shown as a separate loan with its own KFS.
- Contact attempts at 08:59 and 18:01 on a collateral-free low-income member loan are denied; a Tamil Nadu field visit without the s.20 checklist cannot be saved.

## MG2. Microfinance JLG journeys

### MG2.1 Division of work

The RE decides area selection, group approval, household-income assessment, the 50% test, guardrails, GRT outcome, sanction, pricing and posting (CF paras 52–58; OUT para 15). The RE's own staff conduct CGT (free of charge, RBC para 88) and GRT (by an officer independent of the CGT trainer); Udofin staff never conduct GRT, because its outcome is part of the credit process [REC]. Udofin supplies scheduling, capture, evidence, per-member KFS and loan-card delivery, digital repayment instructions on the RE's accounts, the contact-policy engine, the recovery-grievance channel (RBC para 92) and "verify this agent". The RE pulls the CIR under its own CIC membership (CIR para 6); Udofin never pulls.

### MG2.2 Group formation

- **Group record** (projection of the RE's group): group ID, RE, centre, village or ward, members, leader and deputy, formation date, status.
- **Group states:** `FORMING → MEMBERS_CAPTURED → CGT_SCHEDULED → CGT_COMPLETED → GRT_SCHEDULED → {GRT_PASSED, GRT_FAILED} → RECOGNISED → ACTIVE → {DORMANT, DISSOLVED}`. `RECOGNISED` happens only on the RE's `GroupFormed` event.
- **Composition checks** (warnings to the RE, configured from the RE's policy): group size within the RE's range (commonly 4–10; 5 typical) [VERIFY: NABARD and RE norms]; one member per household (address and household-roster match); declared close-relative links; members within the RE's area. Udofin never blocks a group the RE approves; it records that the warning was shown and who overrode it.
- **Per-member capture:** identity through Aadhaar offline XML or DigiLocker (masked; never stored in full); Voter ID with e-validation through the RE's provider, where "no hit" is shown to the RE as a guardrail failure (`REQ-MFIN-GR2-7`); PAN where held; nominee; bank account with penny-drop name match; household roster (spouse and unmarried children under CF para 51).
- **Consent per member,** on the member's own device by OTP, or by the low-literacy route in MG4.4. A group leader cannot consent for a member.

### MG2.3 Household income and the 50% test (capture for the RE's assessment)

- **Questionnaire** follows CF para 52(1): household profile; income by earning member and source over at least one year, with a double-counting prompt (para 52(1)(ii)(c)); regular and irregular expenses (para 52(1)(iii)). Fields configured per RE in U2 (Part 8A.1 `REQ-CF-52`).
- **Thresholds shown to the RE:** annual household income ≤ ₹3,00,000 (CF para 51); above it the application is routed to the RE's non-microfinance product, not rejected by Udofin.
- **Indicative obligation ratio** = (sum of monthly repayment obligations of all household loans from the RE's bureau result and declarations, including bullet loans converted under the RE's method and loans with missing EMI tradelines, plus the proposed EMI) ÷ monthly household income, excluding expected income from the financed activity (CF paras 55–56 and Explanation). Shown against 50% or the RE's lower Board cap. Udofin labels it "indicative; [RE name] decides". Above the cap, Udofin shows the RE's message and, where existing loans exceed the cap, "existing loans continue; no new loan until within the limit" (CF para 57).
- **Divergence capture** when the assessed income differs from income previously reported to CICs: reason text from the member (CF para 54), passed to the RE.

### MG2.4 MFIN Guardrails 2.0 surfaced

The RE applies the guardrails from its own bureau pull (CIR not older than 15 days). Udofin surfaces each result on the member's application in the RE's portal and the field app, never as Udofin's decision:

| Guardrail | Display rule | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| Number of microfinance lenders ≤ 3, counting this RE (from 1 Apr 2025) | Count and lender names as permitted by the RE | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-1` |
| Total unsecured indebtedness ≤ ₹2,00,000 including the proposed loan, excluding secured retail (from 1 Jan 2025) | Amount and headroom | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-2` |
| No new loan if any loan with more than ₹3,000 outstanding is more than 60 days past due | Flag with tradeline reference | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-3` |
| Processing fee ≤ 1.5% plus GST; only the fee and credit-life premium deducted at disbursal | KFS charge check; any other deduction blocks display | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-4` |
| Third-party products only with consent and at least one month after disbursal | XP4 blocks any cross-sell journey for 30 days after `LoanDisbursed` on a microfinance loan | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-5`; RBC para 80 |
| CIR validity 15 days | Stale CIR blocks the sanction screen | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-6` |
| Voter ID e-validation; reject "no hit" | Guardrail flag | `REQ-MFIN-GR2-7` |

Where the RE is not an MFIN member, it applies the guardrails it adopts by policy; Udofin shows only the ones the RE configures [REC: recommend adoption].

### MG2.5 CGT and GRT scheduling

- **Scheduler** in the field app and the RE portal: sessions per group, trainer (RE staff), date, time, place (a public or community place agreed with members), language, planned duration (CGT commonly 3–5 days [VERIFY: RE norm]).
- **Attendance** per member per session: present, absent, reason; geo-time stamp from the **staff** device; photo of the session venue only, never of members' homes or of members without consent.
- **Content checklist** from the RE (loan terms, rights, no prepayment charge, grievance route, recovery-grievance mechanism, the meaning of voluntary peer support, data rights). Training is free (RBC para 88); a fee field does not exist.
- **GRT checklist** (RE officer): knowledge check, house-visit confirmation, coercion screen ("has anyone asked you for money or documents to join?"), household-data confirmation. Outcome PASS or FAIL with reasons is the RE's; Udofin records it.
- **Gate:** sanction screens stay locked until the RE marks GRT passed.

### MG2.6 Sanction, KFS and loan card per member

- **One KFS per member** (each member is a separate borrower): RE-issued, unique proposal number, validity, APR sheet and schedule in the member's language (RBC para 29(1)–(3)). Group-level summaries are never a substitute.
- **Loan card** (RBC paras 78–79; Part 8A.5 `REQ-RBC-78`) in the member's language, plus MFIN grievance details where the RE is an MFIN member; rendered in U25 from the RE's data and updated on each `PaymentReceived`; printable for the RE.
- **No prepayment charge**; delay charge only on the overdue amount (RBC para 81) — U8 blocks a microfinance KFS that shows otherwise.
- **Repayment periodicity** chosen by the member from the RE's options (weekly, fortnightly, monthly; CF para 59).
- **Rate display:** the RE's minimum, maximum and average microfinance rates (RBC para 82) on the product page; rate changes shown as prospective only (para 83).
- **Cooling-off** of at least one day for loans sourced through the DLA (CF para 11).
- **Non-credit products** (for example credit-life cover) only with full, separate consent and with fees on the loan card (RBC para 80); never pre-ticked; never a condition of sanction (XP2, XP4).

### MG2.7 Centre meetings

- **Centre** (2–6 groups commonly [MKT]) with a fixed day, time and place agreed with the members: this is the **designated place** for collection (RBC para 90). Changes need the members' agreement, recorded in the meeting minutes.
- **Meeting record:** date, start and end time, attendance per member, collections per member (MG4), loan-card entries, issues raised, next meeting. `CentreMeetingHeld` is produced on close.
- **Home or work visit** for collection is allowed by the contact-policy engine only after two or more successive non-appearances at the designated place (RBC para 90), counted from meeting records.
- **Voluntary peer support only.**
  - The app never shows one member's dues as another member's liability.
  - There is no "group dues" payment button. A member may pay another member's instalment only through a separate, explicit, revocable consent artefact naming the beneficiary member, the amount and the occasion, captured on the paying member's own device; each such payment is receipted to the paying member.
  - No public defaulter lists, no naming in meetings, no shaming messages (RBC para 91(4)); the leader's view shows own-group members' status as paid or not yet paid, with amounts masked unless the member consents.

### MG2.8 Contact rules, language and accessibility

- **Call and contact window:** 09:00–18:00 (RBC para 91(2)) for every microfinance-flagged loan until 31 Dec 2026; from 1 Jan 2027 the RBC Third Amendment rule pack (RBI/2026-27/230; pack B, Part 7A.0.4) governs the window and visit rules (paras 100Y(4), (5) and (7)) [VERIFY: official text]. `canContact` selects the pack by the timestamp of each attempt; an RE may configure a narrower window (Finbyx IP4.8 keeps 09:00–18:00 by default), never a wider one. No persistent calling; the RE's Board frequency cap applies.
- **Vernacular:** every member-facing screen, message and document in the member's chosen language; English and Hindi at launch plus the RE's regional languages; KFS and loan card in the member's language (RBC paras 29(1), 79).
- **Low-literacy UX:** icon-led navigation, numerals with spoken values, read-aloud (TTS) for KFS summary, loan card and receipts, voice prompts, no free-text where a choice works, large touch targets, colour never the only signal (WCAG 2.2 AA equivalent; Part 10.3).
- **Assisted mode** per MG4.

### MG2.9 Repayment, closure, death and repeat cycles

- **Digital first:** per-member dynamic UPI QR or intent on the RE's merchant account, reference = loan ID plus instalment number; eNACH or UPI AutoPay per member. No group account, no leader-collected pooled UPI.
- **Utilisation check** at 30–45 days [MKT] scheduled from the RE's rule; evidence captured on the staff device.
- **Closure:** final-discharge acknowledgement on the loan card (RBC para 78(4)); NOC in My documents.
- **Death of a member:** on the RE's notification, all reminders and demands stop at once; co-members are never asked to pay; insurance-claim assistance for any credit-life cover (XP2); excess collected after death refunded to the nominee by the RE (MFIN Directive 6) [VERIFY: PMJJBY and PMSBY terms where relevant].
- **Repeat cycle:** a fresh household-income assessment and bureau pull by the RE; no auto-renewal.
- **State overlays:** Karnataka Act 15 of 2025 (non-exempt lenders only) and Tamil Nadu Act 40 of 2025 s.20 checklists on every field event (Part 7A.0.4).

### MG2.10 Events

- **Consumed:** `GroupFormed`, `GroupCollectionPosted`, `LoanDisbursed`, `PaymentReceived`, `ProductCatalogPublished`.
- **Produced:** `CentreMeetingHeld` (only when the meeting is closed in Udofin tooling), `ApplicationSubmitted` (one per member, `productfamily = MFI`), `ConsentRecorded`.
- Producer rule (Integration Spec 6.24; Finbyx IP4.4): the RE's system of record (Finbyx or another certified LMS) produces `GroupFormed` and `GroupCollectionPosted`; `CentreMeetingHeld` comes from whichever system closes the meeting, and a meeting is never closed in both: a close attempt in Udofin for a meeting the RE's field app has closed is rejected with the closing system's reference, and Udofin then consumes the RE's `CentreMeetingHeld`.

### Settings and options (MG2)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household-income ceiling | Platform | ₹3,00,000 a year | Regulatory (CF para 51) |
| Obligation cap shown | RE | 50% | Regulatory ceiling (CF para 55); RE may only lower |
| MFIN guardrail display | RE | On for MFIN members | SRO code; others show what they adopt |
| Group size warning range | RE | 4–10 | RE policy; warning only |
| CGT duration | RE | RE norm | RE policy |
| Repayment periodicity offered | RE product | Weekly, fortnightly, monthly | Member chooses (CF para 59) |
| Contact window (microfinance) | RE product | 09:00–18:00 until 31 Dec 2026; RBC Third Amendment pack from 1 Jan 2027 | Regulatory; tighten only |
| Cross-sell embargo after disbursal | Platform | 30 days | SRO floor (MFIN; RBC para 80) |
| Collection mode at meetings | RE product | Per-member UPI QR | Cash only with the RE's legal opinion recorded (MG4.1) |

### Menu and screens (MG2)

- **Field app › Today** (E): centres due today with state chips (scheduled, in progress, closed, sync pending), offline badge and last-sync time; **Start meeting**.
- **Field app › Groups**: group pipeline (`FORMING` to `ACTIVE`), member roster with household and guardrail status, **Add member** (assisted wizard, MG4.2), **Schedule CGT** and **Schedule GRT** (RE trainer and RE officer pickers; the GRT picker excludes the CGT trainer).
- **Field app › Today › Meeting**: attendance grid, collection sheet with per-member QR, receipts, issues, **Close meeting** (disabled with an explain-why message while any receipt is unsynced or a conflict is open).
- **Loans › Group loan** (A, B, member's own device): my KFS, loan card, schedule, my payments, **Pay my instalment** (per-member QR or intent), "pay for another member" only through the separate consent flow, grievance and "verify this agent".
- **Lender portal › Microfinance** (D): applications per member with indicative ratio and guardrail results, GRT outcomes (RE officers only), meeting records, exceptions (unsynced receipts, suspense, conflicts).

### Acceptance tests

- A member whose household income exceeds ₹3,00,000 is routed to the RE's non-microfinance product and never shown a microfinance KFS.
- The indicative ratio includes a converted bullet loan and a tradeline without an EMI; it excludes expected income from the financed activity; the screen states that the RE decides.
- A member with a loan of ₹3,500 at 61 DPD shows the guardrail flag; a CIR older than 15 days locks the sanction screen.
- Sanction screens stay locked until the RE records GRT passed; a Udofin staff role cannot record a GRT outcome.
- Each member receives an individual KFS and loan card in the chosen language; a microfinance KFS showing a prepayment charge is blocked.
- There is no group-dues button; a payment by one member for another requires the payer's own consent and is receipted to the payer.
- A home-visit attempt after one non-appearance is denied; after two successive non-appearances it is permitted within 09:00–18:00 (attempts dated in 2026); an attempt dated 4 Jan 2027 is evaluated against pack B.
- A cross-sell journey cannot start within 30 days of disbursal of a microfinance loan.
- On a death notification, scheduled reminders for that loan are cancelled within one minute and no co-member receives any message about it.
- Read-aloud plays the KFS summary in the member's language; every screen passes the accessibility suite.

## MG3. SHG journeys

### MG3.1 Scope and boundaries

- **Who borrows.** In SHG-Bank Linkage and SHG lending by NBFC-MFIs, the SHG borrows as a group from the lender, and members then borrow from the SHG under the SHG's own rules ("internal lending"). The lender's loan is to the SHG (with member attribution for CIC reporting); **internal lending is the SHG's own activity**, not a loan by Udofin or by the RE.
- **Udofin provides:** SHG onboarding and grading data capture for the lender's assessment; bank-linkage application and status; member-level data collection for CIC reporting by the lender; the lender's loan servicing view; and an SHG book-keeping view as a service to the SHG.
- **Udofin never:** lends, sets or recommends internal-lending rates, holds SHG funds, collects savings, reports internal loans to CICs, or presents internal loans as RE loans.

### MG3.2 SHG profile and office bearers

- **Profile:** SHG name, formation date, promoting institution (DAY-NRLM, NGO, bank) [VERIFY: DAY-NRLM norms], village, federation links (village organisation, cluster-level federation) where applicable, SHG savings bank account (bank, IFSC, masked number; penny-drop name match to the SHG name), meeting frequency, members (commonly 10–20 [VERIFY: DAY-NRLM norms]), office bearers (president, secretary, treasurer) and the SHG resolution authorising them.
- **Roles in Udofin:** office bearers act for the SHG on group matters only under a resolution uploaded as a document; each member keeps individual control of her own consents and data. Book entries need maker-checker between two office bearers [REC].

### MG3.3 Grading data and bank linkage

- **Grading data capture** for the lender's assessment, using the lender's grading tool (commonly the Panchasutra parameters: regular meetings, regular savings, regular internal lending, timely repayment, up-to-date books [VERIFY: current DAY-NRLM grading format]): meeting regularity and attendance from the book-keeping view, savings regularity, internal-loan repayment rates, books' currency, age of the group. Computed indicators are labelled "from SHG records; [lender] grades".
- **Linkage application:** SHG resolution to borrow, loan purpose, micro-credit plan where the lender requires one, the corpus figure from the books, member-level non-credit information for all members (CIR para 13(3)(ii)), and member Tables 1 or 2 (CIR Annex III) depending on whether the amount attributed to a member exceeds ₹30,000 (CIR para 13(2)).
- **Credit information:** member-level credit data is reported by the lender only for SHGs that take loans above ₹1,00,000 (CIR para 13(3)(ii)); Udofin collects per the lender's configuration and passes it to the lender; the lender reports in UCRF (MFI) Form 3. Udofin does not report.
- **Household data:** where the lender applies the CF para 51 test or MFIN guardrails to SHG members, the MG2.3 questionnaire runs per member with her own consent.
- **States (linkage):** `PROFILE_DRAFT → DOCUMENTS_COMPLETE → GRADING_DATA_SUBMITTED → LENDER_ASSESSMENT → {SANCTIONED, DECLINED} → DISBURSED_TO_SHG_ACCOUNT → ACTIVE → CLOSED`.
- **Disbursal** only to the SHG's own savings bank account; **repayment** only from the SHG account to the lender's account (UPI, NEFT, mandate on the SHG account). Udofin shows instructions and status.

### MG3.4 Book-keeping view (the SHG's own books)

- **Registers:** meeting minutes and attendance; member savings ledger; internal loan register (borrower member, amount, rate as resolved by the SHG, schedule, repayments); SHG cash book and bank book; linkage loan ledger (projection of the lender's data, read-only); federation dues.
- **Rules:** entries are the SHG's records, entered by office bearers with maker-checker; corrections are reversal entries, never edits; every member can see her own savings and internal-loan entries; the group's summary is visible to all members of that SHG only.
- **Internal-lending calculator** computes schedules from the rate and terms the SHG enters, with the label "SHG's own decision; not advice". No default rate is suggested.
- **Exports:** monthly statement PDF and CSV for the SHG and its promoting institution, with the SHG's consent.
- **Data role:** the SHG book-keeping service is Udofin's own service to the SHG, so Udofin acts as Data Fiduciary for it [VERIFY: DPDP role where the SHG is unincorporated], with its own notice and consent per member; book data is never shared with any lender except as the SHG resolves for a specific linkage application.

### MG3.5 Conduct and contact

- Same contact window, language, low-literacy and assisted-mode rules as MG2.8.
- SHG meetings are the SHG's own; RE staff attend only by invitation for linkage-loan matters.
- No pressure on members to save or borrow internally; no messages from Udofin about internal-loan arrears to anyone except the SHG's office bearers and the member concerned.

### Acceptance tests

- An internal loan never appears as an RE loan, never generates a CIC record and never triggers RE reminders.
- A linkage disbursal or repayment instruction to any account other than the SHG's own account and the lender's account fails validation.
- Member Tables 1 or 2 are selected correctly at ₹30,000 and ₹30,001 attributed amounts; member-level credit data collection is required only when the SHG loan exceeds ₹1,00,000.
- A book entry by one office bearer stays pending until a second office bearer approves it; a correction creates a reversal and a new entry.
- The internal-lending calculator has no default rate and shows the "not advice" label.
- A member sees her own savings and internal-loan entries but not another member's details beyond the group summary.

### Settings and options (MG3)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Book-entry maker-checker | SHG | Two office bearers | Fixed [REC] |
| Internal-lending default rate | Platform | None | Fixed (no rate is ever suggested) |
| Statement exports to the promoting institution | SHG | Off | SHG resolution and member consent |
| Member-level credit data collection | Lender | Only for SHG loans above ₹1,00,000 | Regulatory (CIR para 13(3)(ii)) |
| Office-bearer authority | SHG | From the uploaded resolution | Expires with the resolution's validity |

### Menu and screens (MG3)

- **Loans › My SHG** (A, B; office bearers also on E in assisted mode): SHG profile, office bearers and resolution, **Books** (meetings, savings ledger, internal loans, cash book, bank book, linkage loan view), approval queue for the second office bearer, **Apply for bank linkage** wizard (resolution → purpose → plan → corpus from books → member data with each member's consent → submit), linkage status, monthly statement export.
- Each member's view: her own savings, internal loans and the group summary only.
