## RV2. Billing, plan and settings pages

### RV2.1 Naming

- "Plan" is used for Udofin's commercial plans. "Membership" in Udofin means only membership of a co-operative society (Part 7E); a consumer plan is never called a membership [REC], so a borrower cannot confuse a paid Udofin plan with society membership or with a loan benefit.

### RV2.2 RE and non-RE lender users (lender portal: `Billing and plan`)

| Page | Content | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Plan and deal summary | Current deal version (Part 7B UP2): streams, pricing models, rates, minimums, effective dates; attached modules and seats; DLG arrangement summary | RE finance and admin roles |
| Plan explainer | For each stream: what Udofin does, what the RE pays, how it is measured, what changes when switching models; the fixed statement "Fees are paid by [RE] to Udofin and are never charged to borrowers (RBI Credit Facilities Directions, para 10(4)). Fees never affect how offers are matched or ranked." | All RE users with billing view |
| Usage | Meters by month with drill-down to source events (masked IDs); export CSV and XLSX | RE finance |
| Invoices and credit notes | From OH8 (`InvoiceIssued`): PDF, e-invoice IRN and QR where applicable, GSTIN details, TDS deducted fields; dispute button opening an OH support ticket | RE finance |
| Payment methods | eNACH or bank-transfer virtual account (via OH); card or UPI for small one-time items | RE finance with maker-checker |
| Change requests | Plan, module or seat change; downgrade or termination notice; maker-checker inside the RE and approval in Udofin | RE admin |
| Billing settings | Billing contacts, GSTIN, PAN, place of supply, PO numbers, TDS certificate upload (Form 131) [VERIFY: ITA25 form number] | RE finance |

- **Non-payment never cuts an RE off from its data:** during dunning, read access and exports stay available to the RE (OUT paras 34(ii), 87) and borrower-facing servicing for existing loans continues; only new sourcing can be paused, with notice under the agreement [REC]. Continued non-payment ends only in a termination notice that starts the Part 7B UP5 exit (OH `SubscriptionCancelled` carries exit path UP5); there is never a hard cancel.

### RV2.3 Consumers (app and web: `Account › Plans and billing`)

Exists only when S09 is `ACTIVE`.

- **Plans page:** Free plan first, with what it includes (for example one credit-report refresh a quarter and the CIC free annual report link; Part 7D FW1); paid plan(s) with price including GST, billing period, renewal date, what is added; a comparison table with identical styling for every plan; no pre-selection.
- **Fixed statements** on every plan screen and in the plan's terms: "Plans are optional tools. Buying or not buying a plan has no effect on any loan application, offer, approval, price or service. Lenders do not see whether you have a plan." and "Udofin is paid by lenders for loan services; you never pay Udofin for anything to do with a loan."
- **Purchase:** explicit, separate consent to the plan terms (default No); total price shown before payment; no drip pricing; mandate details (amount cap, frequency, validity) shown before authorisation.
- **Free trials** do not auto-convert to paid; at trial end the user is asked to choose [REC; avoids the subscription-trap pattern].
- **Manage:** cancel in one tap from the same page (no retention maze; one optional "tell us why" question that can be skipped); downgrade at term end; refund request; invoices and credit notes; change payment method; pause [REC].
- **Settings** (`Account › Settings`): language; notification and marketing preferences (U16); privacy dashboard (U4); devices; plan-related data export (Part 7C UB1).
- **Entry points:** `Account › Plans and billing` and the `Account › Money tools` pages only (never a bottom tab; on web, the left navigation under Account); never from loan screens, offers, KFS, payment, overdue or grievance screens.

### RV2.4 Where B2C billing runs

- B2C plans are billed by Udofin's own billing service on Udofin's Razorpay account (RV3). Their plan, entitlement, invoice and payment events are Udofin-internal. OH8 remains the catalogue owner and receives B2C revenue only as a monthly `UsageRecorded` with `meter_kind = REVENUE_AGGREGATE` per plan (subscriber count, gross, GST; no subscriber key), so no borrower identity or wellness data enters the Operations Hub (Integration Spec 6.27).
- B2B (RE) invoicing runs in OH8; Udofin's lender portal displays OH's invoices through the Integration Specification billing APIs.

### RV2.5 Plan changes and proration

| Step | RE plan or deal change (B2B) | Consumer plan change (B2C, only while S09 is `ACTIVE`) |
|---|---|---|
| Request | RE admin (maker) in `Billing and plan › Change requests`, or Udofin partnerships; idempotency key per request | Consumer in `Account › Plans and billing › Change plan` |
| Preview | Proration preview from OH8: credit for the unused current period, charge for the new plan from the effective date, GST, next invoice date | Upgrade: (new price − current price) × remaining days ÷ days in period, in paise, rounded half up, plus GST, shown as one total before confirmation; downgrade: effective at period end, no charge |
| Approve or consent | RE checker, then Udofin approver (maker-checker on both sides); a new deal version (UP2) | Explicit consent to the new plan terms (default No) |
| Mandate | RE payment method unchanged unless the RE edits it | If the new price exceeds the mandate cap (RV3.3), a fresh mandate is authorised first; the old mandate is cancelled only after the new one is active |
| Effective | On OH8's signed `EntitlementChanged`; default effective date is the first day of the next billing period, mid-period only if the RE asks | Upgrade immediately after the prorated charge is captured; downgrade at period end |
| Failure | OH8 rejection or signature failure: request returns to `REQUESTED` with the reason; entitlements unchanged | Mandate authorisation or prorated charge fails: the consumer stays on the current plan, no partial change, retry offered; a credit note issues for any captured amount later reversed |

**States:** `REQUESTED → PRICED → APPROVED` (B2B) or `CONSENTED` (B2C) `→ MANDATE_UPDATED` (where needed) `→ EFFECTIVE`, with `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN` and `FAILED`; a priced preview expires at its `valid_until` (Integration Spec 6.27: default 7 days for RE quotes priced by OH8; 24 hours for borrower plans priced by Udofin's own billing) and must then be recomputed.

### Settings and options (RV2)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed statements on billing and plan screens | Platform | RV2.2 and RV2.3 texts | Floor; a theme cannot hide or restyle them |
| Billing contacts, GSTIN, PAN, place of supply, PO numbers | RE | From onboarding | RE choice with maker-checker |
| Invoice delivery | RE | Lender portal and email to billing contacts | RE choice |
| Plan-change effective date | RE | Next billing period | RE may request mid-period |
| Consumer trial end | Platform | Ask the consumer; never auto-convert | Floor |
| Consumer renewal reminders | Consumer | 7 days and 1 day before renewal | Consumer may add channels, not switch off the pre-debit notice |
| Pause plan | Consumer | Up to 2 months a year [REC] | Commercial choice |

### Menu and screens

| Channel and path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| Lender portal (D): `Billing and plan › Plan and deal` | Current deal version, streams, rates, modules and seats; plan explainer with the fixed statement | RE finance and admin; all RE users with billing view |
| D: `Billing and plan › Usage` | Meters by month, drill-down with masked IDs, CSV and XLSX export | RE finance |
| D: `Billing and plan › Invoices` | OH8 invoices and credit notes (PDF, IRN and QR), TDS fields, "dispute this invoice" opening an OH support ticket; filters by period and status | RE finance |
| D: `Billing and plan › Payment methods` and `› Change requests` | eNACH or virtual account set-up (via OH), change wizard with proration preview, approval queue, request history | RE finance and admin (maker-checker) |
| D: `Billing and plan › Settings` | Billing contacts, GSTIN, PAN, place of supply, PO numbers, TDS certificate upload | RE finance |
| Borrower app and web (A, B): `Account › Plans and billing` | Plans comparison (Free first), current plan, change plan with preview, cancel in one tap, invoices and credit notes, payment method, refund request; absent while S09 is inactive | Consumer |
| Operations portal (C): `Finance › Billing operations` | Consumer subscriptions (masked), RE change requests awaiting Udofin approval, dunning status per RE (read access never affected) | Finance operations |

Empty and error states: a failed payment shows what happened, that the plan has not changed and what to do next; an RE in dunning sees a banner with the outstanding invoice and the statement that data access and borrower servicing continue.

### Acceptance tests

- The borrower plan pages and checkout are unreachable while S09 is inactive.
- Every plan screen shows both fixed statements; a theme cannot hide them.
- Cancellation takes no more taps than purchase; the cancel flow has at most one skippable question.
- A trial ends without a charge unless the user actively chooses a paid plan.
- An RE in dunning can still view and export all its data and its borrowers can still service existing loans.
- No plan or billing entry point renders on any loan, offer, KFS, payment, overdue or grievance screen (route scan).
- An upgrade on day 10 of a 30-day ₹300 plan to a ₹600 plan previews and charges ₹200.00 plus GST once (replay of the request charges nothing more); a failed mandate authorisation leaves the old plan and mandate in force.
- An RE plan change takes effect only on a verified `EntitlementChanged`; RE non-payment produces a termination notice and a UP5 exit, never a hard cancel.

## RV3. Payments via Razorpay

### RV3.1 Separation of money

- **Two configurations, never mixed:** (a) Udofin's own Razorpay merchant account for Udofin revenue (S09 subscriptions; any small B2B one-time items not invoiced through OH); (b) each RE's merchant account for loan repayments, set up and owned by the RE (Part 4.3; U11). The configuration validator tags every gateway credential with `purpose` (`UDOFIN_REVENUE` or `RE_LOAN:[re_id]`) and rejects any flow that uses the wrong purpose.
- **Never:** Razorpay Route, split settlements, Smart Collect or any pooled or nodal mechanism for loan money (CF para 10(2)–(3)). Society share money and repayments use the society's own gateway account (Part 7E).

### RV3.2 Checkout and card-data scope

- **Hosted or redirect checkout** (Razorpay Standard Checkout in redirect mode, or Payment Links) so that card entry happens on Razorpay's page; Udofin never sees, stores or logs a card number (RBI card-on-file tokenisation circular, 7 Sep 2021: only issuers and networks store card data) (`PCI`: target SAQ A for Udofin's own billing).
- **Client-side script control** on any page that launches checkout: strict CSP with nonces, script inventory, Subresource Integrity where possible; meets the SAQ A eligibility criterion that the page "is not susceptible to attacks from scripts" (PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ A, revised Jan 2025) [VERIFY: current SAQ A wording].
- **Razorpay's assurance:** obtain and file Razorpay's PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance and its PA authorisation status annually (PA Directions 2025); Razorpay's certification is not Udofin's (RA4).

### RV3.3 Subscriptions and mandates

- **Razorpay Subscriptions** for S09 plans: plan objects mirrored from the catalogue; subscription with an authorisation transaction; recurring charges by UPI AutoPay, card e-mandate or eNACH (eNACH under NPCI rules).
- **E-mandate rules** (EMD): mandate validity stated (para 4(b)); pre-debit notice at least 24 hours before each debit with merchant, amount, date and time, reference and reason (paras 6(a)–(b)), sent by the issuer; Udofin also sends a courtesy notice 48 hours before [REC]; opt-out at any time with additional factor of authentication (para 6(c)), and Udofin's one-tap cancel also cancels the mandate through the API; no additional factor for debits up to ₹15,000 (para 8(a)); **no charge to the customer** for the mandate (para 10(a)).
- **Amount caps:** the mandate's maximum equals the plan price including GST, so a price increase needs a fresh mandate and consent [REC].

### RV3.4 Webhooks and reconciliation

- **Verification:** `X-Razorpay-Signature` is the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the webhook secret; verify before parsing; reject on mismatch.
- **Idempotency and ordering:** de-duplicate on the `x-razorpay-event-id` header; events can arrive out of order, so apply them as upserts against a status precedence (for example captured beats authorised; refunded beats captured); never treat a client-side success as final.
- **Secret rotation:** dual-secret window so retries signed with the old secret still validate during rotation.
- **Events handled** (names per Razorpay documentation at build time [VERIFY]): payment authorised, captured, failed; subscription authenticated, activated, charged, pending, halted, cancelled, completed; refund created, processed, failed; invoice paid; settlement processed.
- **Daily reconciliation:** Razorpay settlement report ↔ Udofin billing ledger ↔ U17 journals; breaks queue in the operations portal; settlement to Udofin's bank account only.

### RV3.5 Refunds and dunning

- **Refunds:** full or partial, to the original source; reasons (cancellation within the refund window, duplicate, service failure, mis-selling review under Part 7F XP4.4, goodwill); maker-checker above a threshold; a GST credit note for each refund of an invoiced amount (CGST Act s.34).
- **Refund window:** pro-rata refund on cancellation of an annual plan; full refund within 7 days of first purchase [REC].
- **B2C dunning:** retry at D+1 and D+3; on final failure the user moves to the Free plan at period end. An unpaid consumer subscription is **never** treated as a debt: no collection calls, no CIC reporting, no effect on loans, no legal notices.
- **B2B dunning** runs in OH8 with the RV2.2 data-access protection.

### RV3.6 GST invoices

- **B2C invoice** for every charge: Udofin's legal name, GSTIN and address; invoice number in a financial-year series of at most 16 characters (CGST Rules r.46) [VERIFY]; date; customer name; place of supply (customer's State); SAC [VERIFY]; taxable value; CGST and SGST or IGST at 18% [VERIFY rate]; total.
- **B2B** (where a consumer supplies a GSTIN, or a one-time RE item billed by Udofin): buyer GSTIN validated by checksum; e-invoice with IRN and QR where Udofin's aggregate turnover exceeds the e-invoicing threshold (₹5 crore) [VERIFY].
- Invoices and credit notes appear in the user's Plans and billing page and in My documents; U17 books them.

### RV3.7 Events

- **Produced by Udofin to OH8 (billing domain, `in.infrabyx.billing.*`):** `UsageRecorded` only: `meter_kind = USAGE` for RE meters (RV1.2) and `meter_kind = REVENUE_AGGREGATE` for B2C plan revenue (RV2.4).
- **Consumed from OH8 (RE commercial relationship):** `PlanChanged`, `EntitlementChanged` (signed; verified against the pinned Hub key), `InvoiceIssued` (RE invoices), `SubscriptionPaymentReceived` and `SubscriptionPaymentFailed` (RE fee payments), `SubscriptionCancelled` (exit path UP5 for an RE).
- **Udofin-internal (not cross-product subjects):** B2C plan changes, entitlements, invoices, credit notes, payments, refunds and cancellations. Internal handlers key on the full internal event type; the loan-repayment `PaymentReceived` (payments domain) is never reused for billing.
- Billing events carry `productfamily = na` and never contain loan references.

### Settings and options (RV3)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway credentials and purpose tags | Platform | `UDOFIN_REVENUE` for Udofin billing; `RE_LOAN:[re_id]` per RE | Floor; a purpose can never be changed on an existing credential |
| Webhook secret rotation | Platform | Every 90 days with a dual-secret window [REC] | Floor |
| B2C retry schedule | Platform | D+1 and D+3, then Free plan at period end | Commercial choice; never collection activity |
| Courtesy notice before each debit | Platform | 48 hours (in addition to the issuer's 24-hour notice) | Udofin default [REC] |
| Refund window and maker-checker threshold | Platform | Full refund within 7 days of first purchase; checker above ₹5,000 [REC] | Commercial choice |
| Invoice series and SAC | Platform | One series per financial year | Regulatory floor (CGST r.46) [VERIFY] |

### Menu and screens (operations portal, channel C)

| Path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `Finance › Billing operations › Payments` | Payments by status with precedence history; no card data anywhere | Finance operations |
| `… › Refunds` | Refund requests with reason, maker-checker above the threshold, credit-note link | Finance (maker), Finance lead (checker) |
| `… › Reconciliation` | Daily run (Razorpay settlement ↔ billing ledger ↔ U17), breaks queue with ageing, resolve with note | Finance operations |
| `… › Webhooks` | Received events, signature result, duplicates suppressed, out-of-order applications, replay of a stored event (idempotent) | Engineering on-call (read), Finance (read) |

### Acceptance tests

- A loan repayment cannot be initiated through a credential tagged `UDOFIN_REVENUE`; a subscription charge cannot use an RE credential.
- No card number appears in any Udofin request log, database, crash report or analytics event (automated PAN-pattern scan in CI and on log samples).
- A webhook with a tampered body is rejected; the same event delivered twice is applied once; an out-of-order "captured" after "refunded" does not revert the refund.
- Cancelling a plan in the app cancels the mandate at Razorpay within one minute and no further debit occurs.
- A failed consumer renewal never creates a collection case, CIC record or loan flag.
- Every charge produces a GST invoice and every refund of an invoiced amount produces a credit note; the daily reconciliation has zero unexplained breaks.

## RV4. Advertising and sponsored content rules

### RV4.1 Where ads may and may not appear

| Surface | Ads allowed? | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-lender offer view, product chooser for loans, eligibility and offer pages | **Never**; no sponsored ranking, badges or paid prominence | CF para 7(4) |
| Application, KYC, consent, KFS, eSign, eStamp, mandate, payment, disbursal status | **Never** | CF para 7(4); Part 10.7 (no marketing in these steps) |
| Loan dashboard, loan mirror, statements, documents, overdue and settlement centre, recovery, notices, grievance and help-centre complaint screens | **Never** | RBC conduct; Part 7A; [REC] |
| Credit-report and score pages (Part 7D FW1–FW2) | **Never** (an ad there is targeting by credit data) | CF para 13; DPDP; [REC] |
| Home feed outside any journey, financial-education articles, public website content pages | Yes, labelled, within RV4.2–RV4.5 | ASCI; CCPA |
| Expense tracker and budget pages (FW3) | Only contextual ads unrelated to the user's entries, or none [REC: none at launch] | DPDP; [REC] |
| Push, SMS, WhatsApp, email | Only with promotional consent, from 140-series or registered headers, within hours (RA5) | TCCCPR; RBC Second Amendment para 101L (draft) |

### RV4.2 Labelling and disclosure

- Every ad and sponsored item carries an "Ad" or "Sponsored" label in the user's language, at the top-left of the unit, in body text size or larger, with a visual treatment distinct from Udofin content; disguised ads are banned (CCPA 2023 "disguised advertisement").
- Sponsored articles name the sponsor at the top; financial-education content is never sponsored by a lender or product provider [REC].
- An ad never uses Udofin's or an RE's KFS styling, offer-card styling or the words "pre-approved", "approved" or "guaranteed" unless the advertiser is an RE and the claim is the RE's documented, current pre-approval for that user [REC: default ban].

### RV4.3 Targeting and data

- **Default:** contextual targeting (page topic, language, State) and declared interests the user chooses in settings; no personal data reaches advertisers; advertisers receive only aggregated reports with minimum cohort sizes [REC: at least 100].
- **Never used for targeting without explicit, separate, revocable consent** (default No; DPDP s.6): loan applications, offers, loan status, DPD, credit reports and scores, expense-tracker data, KYC data, income, household data, precise location, device identifiers, contacts. Even with consent, credit-report and expense data are used only inside Udofin's ad server and never shared with an advertiser.
- **No third-party ad SDKs or trackers** that receive personal data in the app or the authenticated web (Part 10.6 privacy row); first-party ad serving only; no Advertising ID unless approved and consented (Part 4.5).
- **Children:** no ads directed at children and no tracking or behavioural monitoring of children (DPDP s.9(3)); Udofin accounts are 18+ (U3); public website ad units avoid content directed at children.

### RV4.4 Advertiser and creative rules

- **Advertiser verification:** legal entity, GSTIN, sector licence where relevant (RBI CoR or bank licence and presence on RBI's DLA list for any lender; IRDAI registration for insurance; SEBI or AMFI registration for investments); unregulated lenders and lending apps are refused.
- **Prohibited categories:** unregulated lending, credit repair or debt-settlement claims, digital gold, crypto-assets, real-money gaming and betting, unregistered investment advice or return claims (SEBI, 27 Jun 2024), "guaranteed approval" or "no credit check" loans, alcohol and tobacco, deposits of credit co-operative societies (Part 7E), payday-loan promotion in store apps (Part 6.2).
- **Creative review:** ASCI Code (truthful, substantiated, no misleading financial claims; disclaimers legible), CCPA Misleading Advertisements Guidelines 2022, sector codes (IRDAI advertisement rules for insurance, SEBI and AMFI codes for mutual funds [VERIFY current texts]); RE lender ads also need the RE compliance team's approval and carry the RE's name and "loans subject to [RE name]'s credit assessment".
- **Workflow:** `SUBMITTED → POLICY_CHECK → COMPLIANCE_REVIEW → {APPROVED, REJECTED} → SCHEDULED → LIVE → {PAUSED, TAKEN_DOWN, ENDED}`; every state change logged; creatives versioned and hashed.
- **"Report this ad"** on every unit; reports reviewed within 2 business days; ASCI complaints tracked to closure.

### RV4.5 Neutrality monitoring

- Lender ads never change matching, ranking or the order of unmatched lenders; U19's offer-neutrality checks (share of borrowers choosing each rank, by RE) are compared before and after any lender campaign, and a significant shift triggers a review [REC].
- Ad revenue is a separate S10 line; ad sales staff have no access to borrower-level data.
- Frequency caps per user per day; no interstitials; no ads during the first session after registration [REC].

### Settings and options (RV4)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Advertising (S10) | Platform | Off (`DRAFT`) until the owner's advertising-policy decision (Appendix B item 29) | Owner decision |
| Surface matrix | Platform | RV4.1 | Floor; "Never" surfaces cannot be enabled |
| Minimum reporting cohort | Platform | 100 | May only be raised |
| Frequency cap | Platform | 3 ad impressions per user per day; none in the first session [REC] | Commercial choice within the floor |
| Prohibited categories | Platform | RV4.4 list | Floor; may only be extended |
| Declared interests and targeting consent | Consumer | None; all consents off | Consumer choice (`Account › Settings › Ads and interests`) |

### Menu and screens

| Channel and path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| Operations portal (C): `Marketing › Advertising › Advertisers` | Verification wizard (entity, GSTIN, sector licence, DLA-list check), status, re-verification dates | Ad operations (maker), Compliance (checker) |
| C: `… › Creatives` | Review queue by state, policy check result, compliance decision with reasons, version and hash history | Compliance |
| C: `… › Campaigns` | Placements limited to permitted surfaces, schedule, targeting (contextual or declared only), pause and take-down | Ad operations |

### Acceptance tests

- A route scan finds no ad unit on any surface marked "Never" in RV4.1.
- Every ad unit renders the "Ad" or "Sponsored" label in the active language; a creative without it cannot be scheduled.
- An ad request from the credit-report page, any loan screen or a user under the consent-off default never includes financial, credit, expense or KYC attributes.
- The app bundle and authenticated web contain no third-party ad or tracking SDK (dependency scan).
- An advertiser without an RBI CoR or DLA listing cannot run a lending ad; a prohibited category is rejected at policy check.
- A lender campaign changes no field in `offer` ordering inputs; the neutrality report for the campaign period is generated automatically.
- With S10 off, no ad unit, advertiser screen action or ad request exists in production.

# PART 7H — RISK FUNCTION, SUPERVISORY ACCESS, DATA PORTABILITY AND ENGINEERING OPERATIONS

**Purpose.** Each partner RE stays fully responsible for what Udofin does (CF para 6(7)) and must be able to show RBI that its LSP is controlled, auditable, portable and secure. This Part gives Udofin (1) a proportionate **LSP risk management function** with a register, KRIs, DLG cap monitoring and a quarterly pack to each RE, feeding LawDocsComply; (2) **read-only, time-bound, scoped and logged access** for each RE's auditors and RBI supervisors under that RE's contract; (3) **self-explanatory export archives and RE-controlled storage** per deal, with borrower data kept in India; (4) the **engineering-operations and certification-readiness** programme shared with Finbyx, with Udofin's mobile-specific controls; and (5) **provider-neutral voice, AI contact-centre and Jio adapters** that respect TRAI number series, calling hours, AI disclosure and recording rules.

**Applicability.** Udofin as LSP to every RE (all NBFC layers, HFCs, NBFC-MFIs, banks where onboarded) and as technology provider to non-RE lenders (Part 7B UP4). RE-specific obligations scale with the RE's layer and asset size (CYB chapter, OUT Chapter IV materiality); Udofin builds once for the highest common requirement and switches per RE.

**Codes used.** RBI: CF, OUT, CYB, FRM, RBC (including the Third Amendment pack B from 1 Jan 2027, Part 7A.0.4), DPS, ORM guidance note (DOR.ORG.REC.301/14.10.001/2025-26; guidance, not a Direction). `FREE-AI` (RBI FREE-AI framework report, 13 Aug 2025; guidance). Non-RBI (Part 8A.17 codes, shared with Finbyx Part 8A.37): `DPDP`, `TRAI` (TCCCPR 2018 as amended 12 Feb 2025; TRAI Direction of 19 Nov 2025 on 1600-series numbers; TRAI clarification of 10 Jul 2026), `CERTIN` (CERT-In Directions of 28 Apr 2022 under IT Act s.70B(6)), `CA13`, `ISO`, `SOC2`, `PCI`.

**Data owned.** Udofin owns its risk register, RCSA results, loss events, KRI values, DLG cap snapshots, quarterly packs, external-access grants and logs, export jobs and manifests, storage-target registrations, backup and restore evidence, release and change evidence, VAPT records, control evidence, communication-routing decisions, call recordings and AI transcripts made in its channels. REs own their prudential metrics, their risk appetite and their supervisory relationship; LawDocsComply holds the GRC records (register, RCSA campaigns, issues, attestations) for each tenant that uses it.

## RA1. LSP risk management function and LawDocsComply feed

### RA1.1 Basis and operating model

- **No RBI risk-function mandate binds Udofin directly**; the obligations reach it through each RE: due diligence and periodic review of the LSP (CF para 6(2)–(4); OUT paras 30, 38), the provider's operational resilience at least equivalent to the RE's (ORM para 73), incident reporting to the RE (OUT para 61), and fraud accountability (FRM para 31). Udofin therefore runs a proportionate, Board-approved risk function [REC].
- **Roles:** Head of Risk and Compliance (second line; reports to Udofin's Board risk or audit committee; no sales targets; not the DLG commercial owner); product and operations owners (first line); internal audit (third line; may be outsourced to an independent firm).
- **Cadence:** RCSA semi-annually; KRI monitoring daily to monthly by KRI; quarterly pack to each RE and to Udofin's Board; annual policy review.
- **Must not:** compute or display any RE's prudential ratios (CRAR, NPA, ALM) as Udofin's metrics; make or influence credit decisions; accept DLG in any form other than cash with the RE, an FD with a scheduled commercial bank liened to the RE, or a bank guarantee in the RE's favour (CF para 23).

### RA1.2 Risk register (15 risks)

| ID | Risk | Main controls (module) | Primary sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | Mis-selling, dark patterns and loss of offer neutrality | Ranking engine blind to fees and DLG; UI audits; neutrality reports (U7, U8, U19; Part 7F XP4) | CF para 7; CCPA 2023; RBC Second Amendment |
| R02 | Disclosure error: KFS, APR, charges or loan card shown wrongly | Independent APR check; KFS rendering tests; charge guard (U8, U12) | RBC paras 29, 78; CF para 7(3) |
| R03 | Data over-collection, consent misuse or purpose creep | Permission manifest CI gate; consent engine; data map; separate vaults for add-ons and insurance (U4; Part 7D FW4) | CF paras 13–15; DPDP |
| R04 | Data breach or cyber incident | Security controls (Part 10.6); SIEM; incident runbook (U24) | OUT paras 25, 61; CYB; CERT-In 2022 |
| R05 | Data localisation breach (storage or processing outside India) | Region checks on every vendor and storage target (RA3); vendor attestations | CF para 14(4); OUT para 74(vi) |
| R06 | Fund-flow breach: any money touching Udofin, wrong beneficiary or pooled flow | Configuration validator; credential purpose tags (Part 7G RV3); daily reconciliation (U11) | CF para 10 |
| R07 | Identity and application fraud: synthetic identity, mule accounts, device farms, agent fraud | Device integrity, velocity and document-tamper signals; agent controls (U24; Part 7E MG4) | FRM; KYC |
| R08 | Recovery and field conduct breach, including microfinance and State coercion overlays | `canContact`; agent gates; field checklists (Part 7A UR4; Part 7E) | RBC paras 90–100, 100A–100AB; TN Act 40 of 2025; KA Act 15 of 2025 |
| R09 | Grievance handling failure: missed routing, timers or escalation information | Grievance chain v2 with timers (Part 7C UB3) | CF para 12; RB-IOS 2026 |
| R10 | DLG cap breach or DLG loss beyond appetite | DLG cap monitor (RA1.4); arrangement validator (U14) | CF paras 19–29 |
| R11 | RE concentration and partner exit (revenue or operational dependence on few REs) | Deal portfolio monitoring; exit runbooks (Part 7B UP5) | OUT paras 84–89 (RE exit planning) |
| R12 | Vendor and sub-processor failure (KYC, eSign, messaging, cloud, voice, AI) | Sub-processor register with RE consent; fallbacks; vendor reviews | OUT paras 34(iv), 74(xi), 82 |
| R13 | Platform outage beyond impact tolerance for an RE's critical operation | SLOs; DR; impact-tolerance metrics per RE critical operation | ORM paras 31–33; CYB paras 129–138 |
| R14 | Regulatory, licence and platform-policy non-compliance (DLA register, CIMS data, app-store policies, TRAI DLT, IRDAI and other product licences) | Regulatory register; licence gate (Part 7F XP1); store-declaration gate (RA4) | CF para 18; TCCCPR; IRDAI; Play and App Store policies |
| R15 | AI and model risk: wrong answers, bias, undisclosed automation, unapproved messages | Governed AI layer; prompt and output logs; human handover (U20; RA5) | `FREE-AI` (guidance); DPDP |

Each register entry holds: owner, inherent likelihood and impact (5 × 5), controls with test references, residual rating, appetite statement, KRIs, loss-event categories, RE impact flag (which REs are affected), and links to issues in LawDocsComply.

### RA1.3 KRIs

| KRI | Formula | Frequency | Amber / red [REC] | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Complaints per 10,000 loans sourced | complaints received ÷ loans sourced × 10,000, by RE and product | Monthly | 15 / 30 | R01, R09 |
| Complaints resolved or forwarded within TAT | on-time ÷ total | Weekly | below 98% / below 95% | R09 |
| Consent-withdrawal SLA | withdrawals actioned within 24 h ÷ total | Daily | below 99% / below 97% | R03 |
| KFS acknowledged before execution | executions with acknowledgement ÷ executions | Daily | below 100% / any miss is red | R02 |
| APR-check failures | mismatches blocked ÷ offers | Daily | above 0.5% / above 2% | R02 |
| Security incidents and RE notification time | incidents; median and maximum minutes to RE notice | Per event | any notice over 90 min / any over 120 min | R04 |
| Non-India processing detections | count | Daily | any is red | R05 |
| Reconciliation breaks touching beneficiary or settlement accounts | count unexplained after 1 business day | Daily | 1 / 3 | R06 |
| Fraud per 1,000 applications | confirmed fraud ÷ applications × 1,000 | Monthly | RE-specific | R07 |
| Contact-policy denials and violations | violations (attempts outside policy that were not denied) | Daily | any violation is red | R08 |
| DLG utilisation per set and aggregate | cover ÷ amount disbursed per set; aggregate cover ÷ Udofin net worth | Daily | 4.5% / 5.0% per set; aggregate per Board appetite | R10 |
| Revenue share of largest RE | top RE revenue ÷ total | Quarterly | 40% / 60% | R11 |
| Critical vendor availability | uptime per vendor | Daily | below SLA / two breaches in a month | R12 |
| Journey availability against impact tolerance | minutes of outage per critical operation | Real time | 50% of tolerance / tolerance breached | R13 |
| Licence and declaration currency | items expiring within 30 days; store or DLA mismatches | Daily | any due within 30 days / any expired | R14 |
| AI escalations and incorrect-answer rate | human handovers; QA-sampled wrong answers ÷ sampled | Weekly | 2% / 5% wrong answers | R15 |

Thresholds are set by Udofin's Board and may be tightened per RE in the deal (Part 7B UP2). A red value raises `KriBreached`.

### RA1.4 DLG 5% cap monitoring

- **Per DLG set, daily, on every `LoanDisbursed` and on every cover change:** `cover_ratio = DLG cover provided ÷ total amount disbursed out of the set` must stay ≤ 5% (CF para 24(1)). The set is fixed once sanctioned (para 24(2)); the denominator is cumulative disbursal, so repayments, maturities and write-offs never reduce it; `available_cover = min(contracted cover, 5% × disbursed) − invoked`, and invoked cover is never reinstated, even through recoveries (paras 24(3) Illustration, 25(4)). For implicit arrangements, performance risk borne ≤ 5% of the portfolio.
- **Pre-entry check:** a new or renewed arrangement is blocked unless the form is permitted (CF para 23), the statutory auditor's declaration is current (CF para 20(3)), loans covered by trust-fund credit-guarantee schemes are excluded (CF para 21(1)), and the term covers the longest loan tenor in the set (CF para 27(2)).
- **Invocation watch:** the RE invokes within 120 days overdue (CF para 27(1)); Udofin records each invocation against the set and never reinstates it (CF para 25(4)); recoveries shared only as the contract allows (para 25(3)).
- **Disclosure watch:** monthly website disclosure published within 7 working days of month-end (CF para 28); a missed deadline raises `KriBreached`.
- **Breach:** a cover deposit, top-up or amendment that would exceed 5% is refused before it is recorded; any computed ratio above 5% (for example after a data correction) raises `LimitBreached` (`limit_type = DLG_CAP`, `status = OPEN`) to the RE and LawDocsComply, blocks further cover in that set and opens an issue; the cure is an update with `status = CURED` and a higher `update_seq`; the RE decides remediation.

### RA1.5 Loss events, RCSA and impact tolerances

- **Loss and near-miss events** recorded with occurrence, discovery and accounting dates, gross and net impact, root cause, control failed, affected REs and borrowers (counts) (ORM para 42) → `LossEventRecorded`.
- **RCSA** semi-annual per process: inherent risk, control design and operating effectiveness, residual risk; results feed the register and LawDocsComply.
- **Impact tolerances:** for each RE critical operation that depends on Udofin (for example application intake, KFS delivery, repayment initiation), Udofin publishes maximum tolerable disruption, data-loss tolerance and service level (ORM para 33), with RTO and RPO (Part 10.5), tested in DR drills (RA4).

### RA1.6 Quarterly pack to each RE

- **Scope:** strictly that RE's data and Udofin-wide items that affect it; never another RE's name or figures.
- **Contents:** KRI table with trends; incidents and RE notification times; complaints statistics and TAT; conduct metrics (offer-neutrality, contact-policy, UI audits); DLG positions, invocations and disclosures; sub-processor changes; VAPT and audit findings status (summaries); BCP and DR test results; regulatory changes and Udofin's actions; open issues and remediation dates; attestation by Udofin's Head of Risk and Compliance.
- **Delivery:** within 15 days of quarter-end [REC] through the lender portal (PDF and XLSX) and as `RiskSnapshotPublished` to the RE's GRC tool or LawDocsComply tenant (U18); the same pack in aggregate to Udofin's Board.

### RA1.7 LawDocsComply feed

- **Events produced** (Integration Specification v1.1 risk domain): `KriBreached`, `LossEventRecorded`, `LimitBreached` (DLG cap), `RiskSnapshotPublished`; existing `RiskSignalRaised` continues for fraud signals to REs.
- **Recipients:** Udofin's own LawDocsComply tenant (compliance mode), and each RE's GRC target under the compliance-mode switch (Part 2) for RE-scoped events only.
- **Content rules:** aggregates and HMAC pseudonyms keyed in the receiving tenant's KMS only; no borrower PII; each event carries `as_of`, metric version, citation and hash-chain fields per the specification.
- **Inbound:** KRI definitions, thresholds and RCSA campaigns from LawDocsComply through the generic GRC contract (`KRI` resource; U18).

### Settings and options (RA1)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| KRI thresholds | Platform (Udofin Board), per deal | RA1.3 amber and red values | Board-approved; a deal may only tighten (Part 7B UP2) |
| KRI source | Platform | Udofin library; LawDocsComply definitions where the RE's GRC supplies them | Versioned; the stricter threshold wins |
| RCSA cycle | Platform | Semi-annual per process | Floor |
| Quarterly pack due date and recipients | RE | 15 days after quarter-end; RE CCO and CRO | RE may add recipients and ask for an earlier date |
| Risk-feed destination | RE | Compliance-mode switch (Part 2) | RE choice; RE-scoped events only |
| DLG headroom alert | Per DLG set | Amber 4.5%, red 5.0% | Red is the regulatory cap |

| C: `Risk › KRIs` | KRI dashboard by RE and risk with RAG and trend; breach queue with acknowledgement and action; threshold history | Risk team |

### Acceptance tests

- Every R01–R15 entry has an owner, at least one control with a test and at least one KRI.
- A KFS execution without acknowledgement turns the KRI red and raises `KriBreached` within 5 minutes.
- A cover deposit or top-up that would take a DLG set above 5% of its total amount disbursed is refused; a ratio above 5% after a data correction raises `LimitBreached` (`DLG_CAP`, OPEN), blocks further cover and opens an issue, and its cure is sent as CURED with a higher `update_seq`; repayments never increase headroom and invoked cover is never reinstated; a non-permitted DLG form cannot be saved.
- A quarterly pack for RE A contains no data about RE B (automated content check).
- No risk event payload contains a name, phone number, PAN, account number or Aadhaar reference (schema test).
- The risk dashboard has no CRAR, NPA or ALM metric labelled as Udofin's.

## RA2. RE auditor and supervisor read-only access

### RA2.1 Legal basis

- **Contract, not statute.** RBI's inspection powers over NBFCs (RBI Act s.45N) and their group companies (s.45NAA) do not reach a non-group LSP; RBI's and the RE's access to Udofin rests on the LSP agreement: RE access to books, records, data, logs and alerts (OUT paras 34(ii), 74(ii)); RE audit rights (34(vii)); RBI access to the RE's records held by Udofin (34(viii)); RBI's right to inspect Udofin and its sub-contractors (34(ix), 74(xii)); unrestricted and effective access to data and premises for the RE, its auditors, RBI and competent authorities (para 81); pooled audits (para 77).
- **CYB paras 46 and 57** require the RE to give RBI supervisors read-only access to its MIS and auditors audit-mode access; where Udofin hosts RE MIS or records, Udofin supports both. Both paragraphs sit in Chapter IV (BL NBFCs with assets ≥ ₹500 crore) and Chapter V has no equivalent text; build for every RE as a supervisory expectation [REC; Integration Spec 4.7; Finbyx Part 7D AU7].
- **Non-RE lenders:** society auditors and Registrar inspections reach Udofin only through the society's contract (Part 7B UP4) [VERIFY per State Act].
- **Group company caveat:** if an RE ever becomes a group company of Udofin, record whether s.45NAA applies [VERIFY].

### RA2.2 Grantees and scope

- **Grantee types** (Udofin subset of the Integration Spec 4.7 code table): `RE_INTERNAL_AUDITOR`, `RE_CONCURRENT_AUDITOR`, `RE_IS_AUDITOR`, `RE_STATUTORY_AUDITOR`, `POOLED_AUDIT_FIRM`, `RBI_SUPERVISOR`, `RBI_INSPECTION_TEAM`, `NHB` (HFC REs), `COOP_AUDITOR`, `REGISTRAR_INSPECTOR`; basis codes, `pii_level`, `export_level` and `query_level` use the same code tables.
- **Scope object:** one RE only (never multi-RE, except a pooled audit where each RE approves its own slice); periods; datasets from a fixed catalogue (applications and journey logs; consents; offer-display and ranking logs; KFS view and acceptance events; documents; DLA register and CIMS extracts; grievance register and escalations; communications and contact attempts; agent activity, recordings and cash receipts; DLG records; incidents; sub-processors; BCP and DR evidence; configuration and rule versions; AI logs; access logs); PII level (`MASKED` default; `UNMASK_ON_REQUEST`; `FULL` only with RE approval); export allowed (none, capped, full); duration.

### RA2.3 Workflow

Lifecycle (Integration Spec 4.7): `REQUESTED → BASIS_RECORDED → SCOPE_DEFINED → RE_APPROVED → PROVIDER_APPROVED → PROVISIONED → ACTIVE ⇄ EXTENDED → EXPIRED or REVOKED → ARCHIVED`. A grant may also arrive already RE-approved from the RE's register (Finbyx AU7 or the RE's GRC) through `POST /v1/external-access/grants`; Udofin then starts at `PROVIDER_APPROVED`.

| State | Entry and owner | Exit, timer and allowed actions | Failure or rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REQUESTED` | RE user in the lender portal (engagement letter, RBI letter or DAKSH reference attached), or RBI directly to Udofin under the contract right | Basis recorded within 1 business day; for a direct RBI request Udofin verifies authority (letter on RBI letterhead, officer identity, confirmation through RBI's official channel) and notifies the RE within 1 hour unless legally barred (counsel's reference recorded) [VERIFY: counsel's opinion] | Unverifiable authority: closed without provisioning (reason `UNVERIFIED_AUTHORITY`) and `ARCHIVED`; the RE is told and RBI is asked to confirm through its official channel |
| `BASIS_RECORDED` | Udofin compliance records the basis code and engagement or inspection ID | Scope next | Missing document: back to `REQUESTED` |
| `SCOPE_DEFINED` | RE (or RBI's stated scope) fills the RA2.2 scope object | RE approval next; scope diff shown against any earlier grant | A multi-RE scope is refused (pooled audits get one slice per RE) |
| `RE_APPROVED` | RE CCO or nominee (maker) and CISO or MD and CEO delegate (checker); CFO as maker for statutory auditors | Provider approval within 1 business day | For an RBI request the RE cannot narrow scope; its approval records awareness |
| `PROVIDER_APPROVED` | Udofin compliance confirms provisioning against scope; it cannot refuse a valid request | Provisioning within 1 business day [REC] | A scope Udofin cannot technically serve is returned with the gap named, never silently reduced |
| `PROVISIONED` → `ACTIVE` | Named users only; e-mail domain check (`rbi.org.in`; the audit firm's domain); MFA; optional IP allowlist; `ExternalAccessGranted` | Default duration 30 days; first login moves to `ACTIVE`; expiry warnings at 7 days and 1 day to the RE and grantee | Unused for 14 days: reminder to the RE; no auto-extension |
| `EXTENDED` (⇄ `ACTIVE`) | Extension request with reason; same RE maker-checker and provider approval | New `valid_to` never later than 90 days from the original `valid_from` (hard maximum per grant); beyond that a fresh grant with fresh approvals | Refused extension: grant expires on its date |
| `EXPIRED` or `REVOKED` | End time reached, or revocation by the RE, Udofin compliance (security incident) or the grantee | Sessions end within 60 seconds; `ExternalAccessRevoked` | — |
| `ARCHIVED` | After expiry or revocation | Grant, scope, logs and exports kept for the inspection cycle plus 8 years [REC] | Legal hold extends retention |

### RA2.4 Controls

- Read-only replica or point-in-time snapshot; SELECT-only grants and `read:*` API scopes; no write path, no shared accounts, no break-glass reuse.
- Row-level security by RE and scope; field masking of PAN, Aadhaar references, account and phone numbers; unmasking per record with a typed reason, logged and visible to the RE.
- Every query, view and download logged (who, what, rows and fields counts, time); daily activity report to the RE's CCO and Udofin compliance; `ExternalAccessUsed` per session (counts only).
- Exports watermarked with grantee and time, hashed, size-capped; bulk PII export only if the scope allows it and the RE approved it.
- Session timeout 15 minutes idle; confidentiality banner on each login; DPDP: disclosure to RBI under a legal duty (DPDP s.7) does not lift security safeguards or purpose limits [VERIFY: s.7 clause]; exports are not reused for any other purpose.
- **Premises and sub-processors:** on-site inspection logistics (rooms, systems walkthrough, document production) and sub-processor access coordinated under OUT paras 74(xii) and 81; sub-processor contracts carry the same right.

### RA2.5 Relationship with other modules

- RA2 is the live workspace; RE audit and inspection **export packs** are Part 7B UP3; U18 keeps the regulatory register and evidence; Finbyx Part 7D AU7 is the RE-side equivalent where the RE runs Finbyx.
- **Events:** `ExternalAccessGranted`, `ExternalAccessUsed` (daily aggregate per grant and per session, by 09:00 IST next day), `ExternalAccessRevoked` to the RE (lender portal and GRC target) and to LawDocsComply; the Operations Hub receives counts only.

### Settings and options (RA2)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grant duration | RE, per grant | 30 days | Hard maximum 90 days per grant including extensions |
| PII level and export level | RE, per grant | `MASKED`; export `NONE` | `FULL` needs a second RE approval |
| Session idle timeout | Platform | 15 minutes | May only be shortened |
| IP allowlist | RE, per grant | Off | RE choice |
| Daily activity report recipients | RE | RE CCO and Udofin compliance | RE may add the CISO and internal audit |
| Direct-RBI-request notice | Platform | RE notified within 1 hour | Floor; "notice barred" only with counsel's reference |

### Menu and screens

| Channel and path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| Lender portal (D): `Audit access › Requests` | New request wizard (grantee type, basis and document, scope from the dataset catalogue, PII and export levels, duration); approval queue for maker and checker; scope diff | RE CCO (maker), CISO or MD delegate (checker) |
| D: `Audit access › Active grants` | Grants with countdown, users, last activity; extend (within the 90-day cap) or revoke | RE CCO |
| D: `Audit access › Activity` | Daily reports, unmask log with reasons, exports with hashes; filters by grant, user and date; CSV export | RE CCO, CISO |
| Auditor and supervisor workspace (G): `Datasets`, `Query`, `Exports`, `Help` | Scope banner and countdown on every screen; dataset browser limited to scope; read-only query builder; per-record unmask with typed reason; watermarked export within the cap; no write action exists | Grantees |
| Operations portal (C): `Compliance › External access` | Provisioning queue, direct RBI requests with the 1-hour RE-notice timer, on-site inspection log | Udofin compliance |

### Acceptance tests

- A grant cannot be provisioned without a recorded basis, RE approval and an expiry; it expires automatically at the end time; an extension that would end more than 90 days after `valid_from` is refused.
- A grantee cannot read another RE's data, write any record or call any non-`read` API (penetration test cases).
- Masked fields stay masked unless a per-record unmask with reason is logged; the RE sees each unmask in its daily report.
- An export carries the watermark and hash and is refused above the cap.
- A direct RBI request creates an RE notification within 1 hour unless the "notice barred" flag is set with counsel's reference.
- Revocation ends active sessions within 60 seconds and emits `ExternalAccessRevoked`.

## RA3. Data export, archives and RE-controlled storage

### RA3.1 Data classes and who may export them

| Class | Holder role | Exportable to | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| RE-scoped LSP data (applications, consents, KFS events, documents, grievances, communications, agent activity, DLG) | Udofin as the RE's LSP and processor | The RE only | OUT paras 34(xii), 42, 87, 97(xvi); CF para 14(1) |
| Non-RE lender data (Part 7E member and group lending for societies) | Udofin as processor | The society only | Part 7B UP4 DPA |
| Borrower self-service data | Borrower | The borrower (Part 7C UB1) | DPDP s.11 |
| Wellness add-on data (Part 7D) and insurance data (Part 7F) | Udofin as fiduciary in its own right | The consumer only | Never in any RE archive |
| Udofin's own business records (books, contracts, HR) | Udofin | Udofin's auditors and authorities | Companies Act s.128; Accounts Rules r.3(5) daily India backup of electronic books [VERIFY] |

### RA3.2 Archive standard

Udofin implements the Infrabyx archive standard (Integration Spec 12.1, folder profile `udofin_re_v1`; the same standard as Finbyx Part 7J DP1) without changing its structure:

- **Root:** `[RE legal name] - Udofin Archive - [scope] - as of [YYYY-MM-DD]/`; Windows-safe names, full path ≤ 240 characters, no personal data in any folder or file name.
- **`00 Start Here/`:** `README.pdf`, `README.docx` and `README.txt` (English; Hindi optional); `export-manifest.csv`, `manifest.json` and `manifest.json.jws` (detached JWS with the RE tenant's export-signing key, fingerprint printed in the README); `data-dictionary.xlsx` and `.csv`; `relationships.csv` and `relationship-map.pdf`; `code-tables/`; `schemas/` (JSON Schema 2020-12); `verify/` (open-source verifier and instructions).
- **Datasets:** `[dataset].csv` (RFC 4180, UTF-8 with BOM, ISO 8601 dates with time zone, amounts as fixed two-decimal strings with a currency column, code plus label columns), `[dataset].xlsx` (with a "Read me" sheet, typed cells, leading zeros kept) and `[dataset].schema.json`; optional `[dataset].jsonl`.
- **Documents and reports:** originals byte-for-byte with their hashes and signature evidence; narrative renditions as PDF/A-2b plus DOCX; audit trail as `audit-events.jsonl` per month plus an XLSX digest, verifiable offline with daily anchors.
- **Control totals** (applications, consents, KFS events, documents and bytes, grievances, audit-event count and last anchor) are reconciled to the live system at the snapshot instant before signing; any difference fails the job.

**Udofin RE-archive folders:**

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| 00 Start Here | README (PDF, DOCX, TXT), manifests, data dictionary, relationships, code tables, schemas, verifier |
| 01 Deal and configuration | Deal versions (Part 7B UP2), product-offer versions, journey and rule versions, matching-mechanism versions, templates |
| 02 DLA register and CIMS | DLA register lines and change history; CIMS extracts; certification evidence |
| 03 Applications and journeys | Applications, state transitions, eligibility requests and responses, offer sets, unmatched lenders |
| 04 Consents and privacy | Consent artefacts and events; data-principal requests forwarded |
| 05 KYC evidence | Evidence references and hashes (masked; no full Aadhaar) |
| 06 Offers, KFS and acceptance | Offers as displayed with rank and metric; KFS documents; view and acceptance events; cooling-off |
| 07 Documents | Executed documents and eSign and eStamp evidence |
| 08 Payments evidence | Payment instructions, mandate references, reconciliation files (no money held) |
| 09 Loan mirror | Projections with as-at sequence |
| 10 Grievances | Tickets, routing, timers, escalations, case packs |
| 11 Communications | Templates used, messages sent, contact attempts, routing decisions |
| 12 Collections and recovery (restricted) | Allocations, agent records, recordings index, cash receipts |
| 13 DLG | Arrangements, sets, cover snapshots, invocations, disclosures |
| 14 Member and group lending | Groups, meetings, attendance, receipts (Part 7E) |
| 15 Security and incidents | Incidents affecting the RE, notification times |
| 16 Access logs | RA2 grants and logs; Udofin staff access to the RE's data |
| 17 Audit trail | Hash-chained audit events for the RE's scope |

Folder 12 (collections and recovery) is a separate AES-256 encrypted ZIP with its own manifest, included only for a requester holding `export.restricted.recovery` for that RE and approved by a second RE approver and the RE's DPO; the password is generated per archive and delivered out of band to the named recipient. Aadhaar numbers and card data are never exported.

### RA3.3 Export jobs

- **Types:** full, by period, by dataset, scheduled incremental (daily, weekly or monthly), and exit (Part 7B UP5).
- **States:** `REQUESTED → APPROVED (RE admin; a full or exit export needs a second RE approver and a Udofin operations checker) → SNAPSHOT (point in time) → RENDER → PACKAGE → SIGN → DELIVER → CONFIRMED`; download links expire after 7 days; `ExportRequested` and `ExportCompleted`.
- **Quality:** CI renders every generated XLSX, DOCX and PDF/A output in headless LibreOffice and validates PDF/A with veraPDF; a rendering failure blocks the release; control totals reconcile at the snapshot (RA3.2).
- **Failures:** a job that fails at RENDER, PACKAGE or SIGN is retried from the same snapshot (identical hashes); a DELIVER failure retries with back-off for 24 hours, then alerts the RE and Udofin operations; a target whose residency re-check fails blocks delivery; the RE can cancel a job before SIGN.

### RA3.4 RE-controlled storage per deal

- **Configured in the deal** (Part 7B UP2) as a `storage_target` with type, region, credentials reference, encryption mode, schedule and retention responsibility (RACI).

| Target | Mechanism | Region rule for borrower data |
|---|---|---|
| AWS S3 (RE account) | Cross-account IAM role with `ExternalId`; bucket policy limited to the Udofin role; optional S3 Object Lock | ap-south-1 or ap-south-2 only |
| Azure Blob (RE subscription) | Entra workload identity federation or a user-delegation SAS valid ≤ 7 days; optional immutability policy | Central India, South India or West India only |
| Google Cloud Storage (RE project) | Workload identity federation; optional bucket lock | asia-south1 or asia-south2 only |
| Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive (RE tenant) | Microsoft Graph with `Sites.Selected` for the granted site only | Only if the RE's tenant data location for that workload is India, attested by the RE's IT head and re-attested annually [VERIFY: Graph property; RE confirms Microsoft 365 data residency] |
| RE data centre | SFTP (ed25519 keys, pinned host key) to an India-hosted endpoint, or an outbound-only mTLS pull agent installed by the RE | India only, by signed RE attestation |
| Google Drive | Shared drive only, minimal scope | **Non-regulated data only** (no personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR data): never borrower data, because Google Workspace offers no India data region |

- **Region validation** at registration, weekly and before every full or exit export (`StorageTarget.verifyResidency()`, Integration Spec 12.2): a non-India or unverifiable region blocks the target (CF para 14(4); OUT para 74(vi)); a canary write and read-back follow; `StorageTargetConnected` on success.
- **Health:** daily health check and canary; credential-expiry warning 30 days ahead; one missed backup raises a P2 alert, two consecutive misses a P1 alert and an RE notice.
- **Encryption:** archives encrypted at rest under the RE's per-tenant KMS key; optional encryption to the RE's public key so that only the RE can open them; BYOK where the RE requires (Part 10.6).
- **No arbitrary disk attachment** and no promise of recovery after the RE purges its own store.

### RA3.5 Backups to RE storage and restore testing

- **Optional per deal:** daily encrypted incremental archive to the RE's target plus a weekly full archive; `BackupCompleted` with manifest hash.
- **Restore test** at least quarterly: the RE (or Udofin on the RE's instruction in a sandbox) restores the latest archive with the verifier, reconciles record counts and checksums, and signs off; `RestoreTested`. Udofin's own platform backups and restore tests remain as Part 10.5.
- **Exit:** during transition Udofin does not erase, purge or alter the RE's data unless RBI or the RE instructs (OUT para 87); purge after the RE's sign-off with a purge certificate and independent assurance (OUT para 97(xvi)); run by Part 7B UP5.

### Settings and options (RA3)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduled incremental export | RE deal | Off; when on, monthly | RE choice (daily, weekly or monthly) |
| Backups to RE storage | RE deal | Off; when on, daily incremental and weekly full | RE choice |
| Restore test | RE deal | Quarterly | Floor once backups are on |
| Download-link validity | Platform | 7 days | May only be shortened |
| Archive language | RE | English README; Hindi optional | RE choice |
| Key mode | RE | Platform-managed per-tenant KMS key; BYOK or encryption to the RE's public key on request | RE choice; HYOK only with the RE's written risk acceptance |
| Write-once on target | RE, per target | Off | RE choice where the provider supports a lock |

### Menu and screens (lender portal, channel D)

| Path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `Exports › New export` | Wizard: type (full, period, dataset, incremental), datasets, period, restricted folder request, target or download; second-approver step for full and exit exports | RE admin (maker), second RE approver |
| `Exports › Jobs` | Job list by state with progress, control-total check, manifest hash, download (link countdown), retry or cancel before SIGN; filters by type, state and date | RE admin |
| `Exports › Storage targets` | Register a target (wizard with residency check and canary), health status, re-attestation dates, disable | RE IT admin (maker), RE CISO (checker) |
| `Exports › Backups and restore tests` | Backup runs, restore-test records and sign-off, failed-test issues | RE IT admin |
| Operations portal (C): `Portability › Jobs` | Cross-RE job health (counts and states only), Udofin operations checker for full and exit exports | Udofin operations |

Empty state: "No storage target is registered. Archives can be downloaded from Jobs, or register an India-region target."

### Acceptance tests

- A Google Drive target cannot be selected for any borrower data class, and an S3, Azure or GCS target in a non-India region cannot be registered for an RE.
- An RE archive never contains wellness, credit-report or insurance data, or another RE's data (content scan).
- A full export without a second RE approver stays in `REQUESTED`; links expire after 7 days.
- The verifier validates the signed manifest and detects a single altered byte.
- Generated XLSX, DOCX and PDF/A files open in headless LibreOffice in CI.
- A quarterly restore test produces matching record counts and checksums; a failed test raises an issue.

## RA4. Engineering operations and certification readiness

### RA4.1 Same programme as Finbyx

Udofin runs the **same engineering-operations programme as Finbyx Part 7L (EO1–EO5)**, with the evidence collected in the Operations Hub engineering-operations console and control library (OH13, OH14): GitHub rulesets and branch protection, CODEOWNERS for sensitive paths, signed commits, required checks, production environments with reviewers, change and patch management with the platform SLAs of Finbyx EO1.6 for product code and infrastructure (from triage: critical, KEV-listed or actively exploited 72 hours; high 7 days; medium 30 days; low 90 days; a stricter RE contract value wins; CYB paras 125–126), SBOM and supply-chain controls, VA every 6 months and PT every 12 months (CYB paras 121–126), backup and restore evidence, CYB para 105 escrow and para 106 certificates for REs that require them (Part 10.8 items 10–11), and the common control framework. This section adds only what is specific to Udofin as a mobile, borrower-facing DLA. Releases emit `ReleasePublished`; approved changes emit `ChangeApproved`; collected evidence emits `ControlEvidenceCollected`.

### RA4.2 App-store release controls

- **Build provenance:** production builds only from protected tags in CI (Part 10.3); EAS production profile; build number, commit, SBOM and permission manifest stored in the release record.
- **Store-declaration gate:** every release compares the merged Android manifest, iOS Info.plist and privacy manifest, the Google Play Data safety form, the Financial features declaration (including the India personal-loan declaration), Apple's privacy labels and the App Store review notes with the approved versions; any difference blocks submission until Compliance approves and the declarations are updated.
- **Partner-list check:** the Play listing's partner-RE list and the in-app partner list match the DLA register; adding an RE to the listing is blocked until that RE confirms its CIMS DLA entry (Appendix B item 1).
- **Staged rollout:** Play staged percentages (for example 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) and App Store phased release, with automatic halt when crash-free sessions fall below 99.5%, ANR exceeds Play's bad-behaviour threshold, or a P1 incident opens.
- **OTA policy enforcement:** an OTA update that changes permissions, data collection, consent or disclosure screens, payment flows, product availability or a security control is rejected by the release pipeline (Part 10.3).
- **Account security:** organisation accounts; hardware-key MFA for every Play Console and App Store Connect user; least-privilege roles; two-person rule for release to production and for signing-key operations; quarterly access review.
- **Policy watch:** Google Play Financial Services and Personal Loans policy, Apple App Review Guidelines 3.2.2, target-API-level deadlines and SDK policy changes tracked in the regulatory register with owners and dates (R14).
- **Release evidence pack:** change ticket, test results, VAPT status, declaration diff, rollout log, rollback plan; filed to OH13.

### RA4.3 Mobile app VAPT and MASVS

- **Standard:** OWASP MASVS v2.1.0 controls tested with the OWASP MASTG under the MAS-L2 and MAS-R testing profiles (MASVS v2 itself has no levels; Part 10.1), with MASWE weakness IDs, mapped to the Part 10.6 control table.
- **Scope:** Android and iOS borrower apps, the field app (channel E), and their APIs; web and PWA to OWASP ASVS L2.
- **Techniques:** static analysis of source and binaries; dynamic testing with runtime instrumentation; network interception against pinning; storage and keychain review; deep-link and WebView abuse; permission and FLAG_SECURE checks; root, jailbreak, hooking, emulator and repackaging resistance; third-party SDK inventory and data-flow review.
- **Frequency:** before each major release, after any change to authentication, payment, consent or KYC flows, and at least annually; plus the CYB cadence for internet-facing systems; retest after remediation.
- **Testers:** independent and appropriately trained (CYB para 122); CERT-In-empanelled by Udofin policy.
- **Findings:** tracked to closure under the EO1.6 platform SLAs above, whoever raised them (including an RE-commissioned VAPT); retest by the tester; exceptions only with a CISO risk acceptance expiring within 90 days; summaries and remediation status shared with REs (Part 10.8 item 10).

### RA4.4 Certification readiness

- **Targets** [REC]: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (with Amendment 1:2024) for the Udofin platform; SOC 2 Type 1, then Type 2 over at least 6 months; ISO/IEC 27701:2025 (stand-alone privacy management system) after 27001; ISO 22301 later; ISO/IEC 42001 only if AI becomes material; PCI DSS SAQ A for Udofin's own billing (Part 7G RV3).
- **Udofin-specific controls** added to the common control library: CF paras 13–16 (permissions, consent, minimal data, localisation); DLA register currency (CF para 18); offer neutrality (CF para 7); fund-flow guards (CF para 10); DLT template and number-series routing (RA5); app-store declaration gate (RA4.2); MASVS testing (RA4.3).
- **Claims rule:** no certification, report or "compliant" claim in any store listing, website, sales or RE document until the certificate or report is issued; "aligned to" or "in progress" only; a copy linter checks marketing and listing text for certification claims.

### Settings and options (RA4)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patch SLAs and exception expiry | Platform (all group repositories, through OH13) | EO1.6: 72 hours, 7, 30 and 90 days; exceptions ≤ 90 days | Floor; an RE contract may only shorten |
| Staged-rollout steps and halt criteria | Platform | 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%; halt below 99.5% crash-free, on Play's ANR threshold or a P1 | Floor; steps may be slower |
| OTA allow-list | Platform | JavaScript and asset fixes only | Floor |
| Store-declaration approvers | Platform | Compliance and the CISO | Floor (two-person rule) |
| VAPT cadence | Platform | VA every 6 months, PT every 12 months, MAS-L2 and MAS-R before each major release and yearly | Floor |
| RE evidence recipients | RE | RE CISO and CCO | RE may add recipients; full reports under NDA |

### Menu and screens (operations portal, channel C; lender portal, channel D)

| Path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `Engineering › Releases` | Release records (build, commit, SBOM, permission-manifest hash), gate results with the failing gate named, evidence pack, rollout log, halt and rollback | Release manager, CISO |
| `Engineering › Store declarations` | Approved versions and diffs (manifest, Info.plist, privacy manifest, Data safety, Financial features, privacy labels), approve with two people; partner-list check against the DLA register | Compliance, CISO |
| `Engineering › Vulnerabilities and VAPT` | Findings by severity with SLA clocks, exceptions with expiry, MASVS and VAPT reports, retests | Security engineering, CISO |
| `Engineering › Certification` | Readiness by scheme (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27701, PCI DSS SAQ A), control evidence status, claims-linter results; issued certificates only in the register | CISO, Compliance |
| Lender portal (D): `Settings › Security and trust` | Release notes with regulatory impact, VAPT and MASVS summaries, SBOM, sub-processor list, CYB para 106 certificate and escrow status where required, issued certificates only | RE CISO, CCO |

### Acceptance tests

- A release whose permission manifest or Data safety answers differ from the approved versions cannot be submitted.
- Adding an RE to the store listing without its CIMS confirmation fails the release pipeline.
- A staged rollout halts automatically when crash-free sessions drop below 99.5% in a test simulation.
- An OTA bundle that adds a permission-dependent module is rejected.
- The latest MAS-L2 and MAS-R assessment is less than 12 months old and has no open critical or high finding past its EO1.6 SLA before a major release; a critical finding open beyond 72 hours without a risk acceptance blocks release.
- The copy linter fails a build whose store listing or website says "ISO 27001 certified" or "SOC 2 compliant" without an issued certificate record.
